Contributes: the file every other part reads

A canvas is a markdown file. Prose stays prose. A brick is a fence or a comment wrap. Every markdown reader shows the file. Git shows a useful diff. The ast module reads the dataflow between code bricks off the code itself. Nobody draws an edge.

The whole format. KINDS is the vocabulary. A word outside it does not parse. The parser is a line scan. A canvas fence inside a longer markdown fence is an example of a brick, not a brick. order reads the dependency graph off the code. On a cycle the visit stops and document order stands, and a plan with a loop in it still opens. save writes through a temporary file in the same folder. A torn write cannot reach the document.

prop x and prop y are the only trace the canvas leaves in the file. A document nobody has laid out is still complete. arrange places an unopened one.

One function for every change, whether a person or the helper asked for it. replace, kind, remove and replace_selection now retire the names their brick defined. A renamed or deleted definition cannot stay readable downstream.

A canvas executed its Python in the web process. One while True: hung every request Leela served. One os._exit() ended Leela. The code runs in a kunda kernel now. It runs only after somebody says it may.

A question names its own scope, pins and budget. resolve returns the exact bricks and the reason each one is there. The budget sheds the least useful brick first, never a pin or the goal.

Dataflow is the half that does not care where code runs. Nothing in it reaches into a namespace dict. Runtime is this process's, for the spike and the tests. KernelRuntime is a kernel. It holds the timeout itself. Kunda's execute(timeout=) does not return on a busy loop. So it waits, interrupts, waits again, shuts the kernel down and starts another.

One process-global store served every workspace. store_for scopes it to the open roots. It keys on the resolved path. Two spellings of one file cannot fork a namespace. allow sets Open.trusted. A save carries rev, and the store refuses a stale write.

Contributes: all of the review step

A bundle claims a region, names a goal and owns a list of files. coverage compares the claim with the diff. A diff tool holds one of those two sets. It can produce neither list.

coverage is the comparison. matched is a claim the diff confirms. unmet is a claim with nothing behind it. unclaimed is a file that moved with no claim on it. review is the literate diff, and it built this page. For each file it emits the hunks, then every brick citing that path. A file id is its basename, or its whole path when two files share one basename. place_diff is the other half. It fills a slot with one brick a file.

The renderer folds anything longer than a phone screen. It writes no script. The fold is <details>, and the page works with JavaScript off. A diff body scrolls sideways inside its own box. A long line never widens the page. Past DIFF_CAP lines a hunk ends in a count. One committed HTML page had otherwise taken this review to three megabytes.

canvas_path is the one gate. Every source and destination passes it, including save's to and page's out. With a folder open, fs._check decides. With none, which is the spike and the tests, the canvas folder decides. _runs_code is the trust line. It gates what evaluates, not what edits. You can still write in an untrusted document.

Both frames are sandbox=allow-scripts. Nothing grants allow-same-origin. A component gets an opaque origin. It cannot read this page's DOM, cookies or routes. A message speaks for the brick whose frame sent it, never for the id it claims. Blur records and one chain writes. Clicking Save cannot race the blur it causes. Untouched prose never returns from the DOM.

cvEsc escaped &<> only. A quote in a URL or a link label closed the attribute and opened one of the author's choosing. It escapes quotes too now. cvUrl passes http, https, mailto, a relative path, an anchor and a raster data URL. A javascript: scheme and a data SVG do not pass.

OWN_BUNDLE names the blocks that serve their own page. The build writes and commits each one, like the IDE's three. The order comes from that block's own ui.FILES, written down once.

Attached

Every changed file is claimed and every task is done.

Does this change do what the goal says, and what would you push back on?

A component comes from an installed library

Give Leela one document that holds a goal, its plan, its research, its code and its questions, and one page that shows all five to a reviewer on a phone.
measure
tools you open to review one branch
baseline
4: tracker, notebook, diff, deck
target
1 page
by
2026-10-31

Contributes: the palette, with no second process

The palette used to be an HTTP call to a second server. It is an entry-point group now. A library answers four questions. Its manifest, one brick, that brick's wiring, and its own routes.

Change

needs reads the imports out of the wiring text. A component cannot claim a dependency its code does not import. It cannot hide one it does import. LIB comes from __name__. Renaming the package renames every src it serves. That is why these eight files extracted with no code change.

A library is any module with manifest() and find(name). There is no base class and nothing to register. Leela reads manifest in process. The palette needs no second server.

Contributes: one spelling per name

test_seams.py guarded eleven libraries. It did not guard kunda or pullup, the two Leela composes most. Eight reaches into their private names went uncounted. This is the widest change in the branch. It reaches blocks with nothing to do with a canvas.

  • [x]Reduce each seam to what Leela adds, and guard kunda and pullup like the rest.me

Change

The code built a Drive and then told it which interpreter to use. Pullup had already resolved commands against Leela's own. A Drive now takes the interpreter it will run under. A changed interpreter builds a new Drive instead of mutating the live one.

Two private kunda imports were unused, and the branch drops them. The six load-bearing ones sit in ALLOWED in the seams test. Each one names the library that would have to open it.

It re-exported almost the whole of kunda's support half. core/envs.py went straight to kunda for three of the same names. clean_env had two spellings, depending on which module you read. The module keeps LEELA_PY, the one name Leela renames. Fifteen call sites in ten modules now import from kunda directly.

Nine lines of pure pass-through, deleted. Its two callers import from pullup.wfbuild.

Contributes: a suite that finishes

The kernel killed pytest -m slow a third of the way in. It reported nothing. Not the tests it could never run, and not the ones above them that pass in seconds. Two suites resolved a real local model, because the machine happened to hold its bundle in the cache.

  • [x]Make `pytest -m slow` finish, and fix what running it found.me

Change

The fix reads ident first. A worker with no ident never started, and _reap leaves it alone. A worker that started and then stopped has finished. Only then does the turn retire.

tests/blocks/test_agent_threads.py +26 -0
@@ -230,6 +230,32 @@ def test_a_second_turn_is_rejected_while_the_first_is_pending_registration(): assert not worker.is_alive() and result['accepted']['run'] == 'run-1' +def _pending_entry(worker):+ "The record `start` publishes, with `worker` as the thread that has yet to speak."+ return {'id': 'x', 'event': threading.Event(), 'gate': threading.Event(),+ 'accepted': False, 'run': '', 'error': None, 'at': time.time(), 'worker': worker}+++def test_a_pending_turn_is_not_reaped_before_its_worker_starts():+ """`start` publishes the pending turn and only then starts the worker. A request arriving in+ that window read the unstarted thread as a finished one, reaped the turn and was accepted,+ which is the second live turn `_pending` exists to refuse. `Thread.is_alive` is False both+ before `start` and after the run, so `ident` is what tells the two apart.+ """+ ws = _Workspace(); runner = TurnRunner(ws)+ runner._pending['x'] = _pending_entry(threading.Thread(target=lambda: None))+ assert runner._reap(ws.ai) == [], 'an unstarted worker is not a finished one'+ assert 'x' in runner._pending, 'and the turn it is setting up still holds the thread'+++def test_a_pending_turn_whose_worker_finished_is_reaped():+ "The other half: once the worker has run and gone, nothing is running and the turn clears."+ ws = _Workspace(); runner = TurnRunner(ws)+ worker = threading.Thread(target=lambda: None); worker.start(); worker.join()+ runner._pending['x'] = _pending_entry(worker)+ assert runner._reap(ws.ai) == ['x'] and not runner._pending++ class _Latched(_AI): "An assistant that registers its run before the engine reports it, as Ramabana's `stream` does." registered = False

TurnRunner._reap read Thread.is_alive alone. That is False before a thread starts, and False after it ends. start publishes the pending turn and only then starts its worker. So a request arriving in that window reaped a live turn and won acceptance. Two tests hold each half.

The test called read_only(tools) bare and expected it to drop the delegate tools. Shalya moved that to a block= the caller passes. Both places in Leela pass NO_SUB. The test was red while the behaviour was right. It now tests what delegate hands a sub-agent. It lives here, not in a suite that needs a local model.

The gate asked whether the cache held the model bundle. It never asked whether the machine could hold it. One engine climbs from 123MB to 12.2GB. A run that reached 13.4GB died with 3.1GB nominally free. The number is 16000, and the comment says where it came from.

Five monkeypatches aimed at Leela's re-exports, not at the name the library reads. kunda.pool imports Kernel under its own roof. _class_for reads it there. So the pool ignored the fakes. One test failed. One hung on a real kernel that never signalled. A sixth fake was missing the touch the pool calls before start. The file went from hanging to 17 passing in 11 seconds.

The harness built engines through Routing. No engine sat at 290MB. The first took it to 871MB and the second to 3.1GB. Each streaming test then added two to three gigabytes. The Python heap stayed flat, which puts the growth inside the engines and outside Python. A browser test drives the painting and the panels. It needs no model. Every workspace gets the scripted backend. 80 tests, 4m29s, 967MB peak. One test also read a notebook out of an untracked folder. A real kernel had written that folder into the checkout. Three more tests counted the buttons in a bar. The bar now holds a fourth.

12.9 to 2.9. Three patterns carried most of the weight. A sentence that states a thing and then restates its opposite. A closing line that reverses the one before it. A passive clause that drops the doer. ste.md bans all three by name.

@@ -0,0 +1,200 @@+# Dynamic documents++A goal like "increase procurement productivity by 10%" is neither a coding task nor a writing task. Reaching it takes five steps. Frame the measure. Collect what the team already knows. Pull an extract apart until the numbers say something. Prototype the one rule that might work. Write the recommendation. Today those five steps live in five tools. The notebook holds the extract. The deck holds the recommendation. The research sits in tabs, and the plan sits in a tracker. Only a person carries context between them.++Leela already holds four of the five. It has the kernel, the files, the vault, the agent and the notebook. It lacks a document that follows the work rather than a script.++Two branches have gone at that. `claude/dynamic-document-canvas-ohgfud` built the file and the runtime, wired into Leela as a block. `leela/blocks/canvas` builds the context engine on that file. This document is the design both halves answer to.++## What a flat list cannot be++Every notebook is one flat list. Its prompt cells read from the top of the document down to the cell being asked, which `Notebook.context` does in `leela/blocks/nb/nb.py`. The list works because it is the order the work happened in. Every cell above yours is work you did before, and the model should probably know it.++That rule dies the moment the document holds more than one line of work. Framing the goal, reading the audit, cleaning the extract and drafting the recommendation are four strands, not four consecutive steps. Ask the recommendation prompt to read everything above it and it reads three failed attempts at a groupby. Ask it to read nothing and you are pasting again.++The audit is the case that makes it concrete. It belongs in the context of the synthesis question near the top, and in the context of the risk question near the bottom, and in nothing between them. Position cannot express that. Nothing about where a brick sits says which questions it answers.++## The file++`*.canvas.md`. Prose is prose. A brick markdown cannot show is a fence, `` ```canvas code id=c1 ``. A brick whose body is markdown a plain renderer should still show is a comment wrap, `<!--canvas goal id=goal-->`. Headings are the document's regions. Frontmatter carries the title.++This is the canvas branch's format. A plan, a design doc and a set of research clippings are prose, and nobody reads or reviews prose held in JSON. Markdown gives three things. `git diff` shows the argument changing rather than a re-serialised tree. The document opens in any reader. The design doc and the code that tests it stay in one file.++Reading it works line by line rather than by one regex over the file. A canvas fence inside a longer markdown fence is an example of a brick and not a brick. A document about canvases therefore parses as a document. This rule matters, because a `source` brick holding a clipped page is where quoted markup arrives.++## What AFFiNE contributes++AFFiNE's [BlockSuite](https://blocksuite.io) puts one block tree behind two views. A document is a list of blocks, each with a flavour named `namespace:name`. Page mode reads the tree top to bottom. Edgeless mode reads the same blocks off a surface that gives them coordinates, frames that group them, and connectors that join them. Neither view owns the document.++Two of those ideas belong here, and the code replaces the third.++The named kind belongs. A notebook cell has three types, because a notebook holds three kinds of thing. A document that holds a goal, a task, a clipping and a chart needs a name for each. A `goal` brick carries `measure`, `baseline`, `target` and `by`, which holds a measure better than a markdown cell and a convention.++The two views belong. The list is the right way to read finished work, and the only way to review it. Eight files moved, and the only edit added a `Registry` to `bricks.py`.+<!--/canvas-->++The palette this branch resolves, in process:++```canvas code id=c-palette+from leela.blocks.canvas.bricks import libraries, palette+p = palette(libraries())+[(b['src'], b['needs']) for b in p['bricks']]+```++# The editor++<!--canvas bundle id=u-ed title="The editor the merge brought in"+ goal=g+ contributes="the run step and every insert menu"+ covers="The editor,What running it found,t8,t13"+ paths=leela/blocks/canvas/app.py,leela/blocks/canvas/ui.py,tests/test_web_slow.py,leela/blocks/canvas/live.py,leela/blocks/canvas/helper.py,leela/blocks/canvas/store.py,leela/blocks/canvas/*.js,leela/blocks/canvas/canvas.css,leela/blocks/canvas/*.canvas.md,leela/blocks/canvas/triage.diff,examples/canvas/*,docs/screenshots/*,media/canvas/*+ refs=doc:docs/canvas.md-->+The canvas branch built the editor: a gutter, a block menu, a slash menu, a component palette, an+inline helper and a live kernel. Both branches read the same file format, and the merge therefore kept one+`doc.py` and one palette.+<!--/canvas-->++Four ways to add a brick, and all four write the same markdown. The gutter handle opens the block+menu, and a slash on an empty line opens the filter. The palette lists what an installed library+ships, and a pasted URL or file becomes a `source` or a `pdf`. `docs/screenshots/canvas-blockmenu.png`,+`canvas-slash.png` and `canvas-palette.png` show the first three.++<!--canvas bundle id=u-wire title="Wiring the block into Leela"+ goal=g+ contributes="the block loads with the IDE, and its routes are checked"+ covers="The wiring,t10"+ paths=leela/blocks/__init__.py,leela/blocks/canvas/__init__.py,leela/skills/*,tools/build_ide_js.py,tests/routes.txt,tests/test_canvas.py,tests/test_canvas_doc.py,pyproject.toml,extensions/bricks/pyproject.toml,.gitignore+ refs=file:leela/blocks/__init__.py-->+A block declares the context it reads in `CAPS`, and `blocks.NAMES` lists the folder. The IDE+build names every `.js` file. `tests/routes.txt` is the record of what the block serves,+so a new route cannot appear unrecorded.+<!--/canvas-->++# The wiring++`CAPS` must name exactly what the routes read off `ctx`. The canvas block reads two things: the+file system, and the model.++```canvas snippet id=s-caps path=leela/blocks/canvas/app.py lines=24-24+`CAPS` is a promise about `ctx`, and Leela checks it. A route that reads a capability the block did+not declare fails at load, not at the request that reads it.+```++# What running it found++Two faults survived every reading of the merged block. Running it end to end found both.++<!--canvas note id=n-stale-->+The editor lost typing in a code brick. An insert anywhere in the document runs `cvSync`, which keeps the+element and hands it a new brick object. The textarea then wrote to an object the document no+longer held, and the next flush read the older body. `cvEdit` writes through to `cvBrick(id)`, and+`cvKeepEdits` carries an edited body across the sync. The browser test in `tests/test_web_slow.py`+returns the empty body on the code before the fix.+<!--/canvas-->++<!--canvas note id=n-basket-->+The context basket has a route and no panel. `/canvas/context` returns the exact bricks one question+will send, each with the rule that chose it, and 51 tests cover the model. The merged editor has no+control that opens it. Neither branch built one, because the canvas branch built the editor and+this side built the basket. `t14` above records the gap.+<!--/canvas-->++<!--canvas task id=t13 status=done owner=me-->+Fix the stale-object write and add the browser test that reproduces it.+<!--/canvas-->++<!--canvas task id=t14 status=todo owner=me-->+Give the basket a panel: a control on an `ask` brick that shows what the question will send.+<!--/canvas-->++# The prose++<!--canvas bundle id=u-prose title="Every page scored, and the English fixed"+ goal=g2+ contributes="the English a reviewer actually reads"+ covers="The prose,t15,t16"+ paths=README.md,docs/*.md,examples/canvas/*.canvas.md,extensions/bricks/README.md,media/*.md,leela/blocks/canvas/procurement.canvas.md,leela/blocks/canvas/explain.md,leela/blocks/canvas/*.py,extensions/bricks/leela_bricks/*.py,leela/blocks/agent/threads.py,tests/blocks/test_agent_threads.py,tests/test_core.py,tests/test_packaging.py,tests/test_projects.py,tests/test_runtime.py,tests/test_agent.py+ refs=pkg:slopometer,pkg:fastaistyle,doc:leela/blocks/canvas/ste.md-->+`slopometer` scores a page against the reference-prose rules, and `chkstyle` scores Python against+fastai's. Both ran over every file this branch adds. `ste.md` already held the rules, and nobody had+checked a hand-written page against them.+<!--/canvas-->++`explain.md` hands `ste.md` to the model that drafts a snippet. A drafted sentence therefore met+the rules, and a hand-written one did not. Three patterns carried most of the weight. A sentence states a+thing and then restates its opposite. A closing line reverses the sentence before it. A passive+clause drops the doer. `ste.md` bans all three by name.++<!--canvas data id=n-slop-->+worst_page_before = 26.8+worst_page_after = 7.5174 more lines, not shown

The same document read as a canvas: the goals, the plan, the basket, the change and the diff. The worst page on the branch fell from 26.8 to 2.5 and four pages now score zero.

Taking it to {worst[0]+10:.0f}% would be worth about ${(won*(worst[0]+10)/worst[0]-won)*deal/1000:.0f}k a year, against a customer acquisition cost of ${cac:,} and {payback} months of gross margin to pay it back."+```++```canvas brick id=sf6 src=leela_bricks:viz.series+bind labels = names+bind series = [{'name': 'conversion %', 'values': rates}]+prop height = 240+```++<!--canvas note id=sf7-->+The chart above binds to `rates`. Why is payback measured against gross margin rather than revenue+<!--/canvas-->

examples/canvas/pricing-a-run.canvas.md +69 -0
@@ -0,0 +1,69 @@+---+title: Pricing a run+mode: make+---++# Pricing a run++An agent run costs four numbers and one multiplication. Every argument about the cost is an+argument about one of the four. Put the four in a cell, and the argument becomes editable.++```canvas code id=p1+in_tokens = 18_000+out_tokens = 2_400+runs_a_day = 400+prices = {'Opus 5': (15, 75), 'Sonnet 5': (3, 15), 'Haiku 4.5': (0.8, 4)}+```++```canvas code id=p2+def cost(model):+ i, o = prices[model]+ return in_tokens/1e6*i + out_tokens/1e6*o++rows = [{'label': m, 'per_request': round(cost(m), 5), 'monthly': round(cost(m)*runs_a_day*30, 2)}+ for m in prices]+rows+```++```canvas brick id=p3 src=leela_bricks:thrifty.costs emit_row=picked+bind rows = rows+prop height = 220+```++```canvas code id=p4+picked = rows[-1]+```++```canvas data id=p5+bind text = f"**{picked['label']}** at this shape of request is ${picked['per_request']} a call and ${picked['monthly']:,.0f} a month at {runs_a_day} runs a day. The cheapest option is {(min(rows, key=lambda r: r['monthly'])['monthly']/picked['monthly']*100):.0f}% of that."+```++Click a row. `picked` changes, and the sentence below binds to `picked`, which changes it too.++## The knob that actually matters++```canvas sim id=p6+prop height = 120+const draw = () => {+ root.innerHTML = `<div class="row"><label style="width:140px">runs a day</label>+ <input type=range min=50 max=5000 step=50 id=r><b id=v></b></div>`;+ const r = root.querySelector('#r');+ r.value = props.runs_a_day ?? 400;+ const show = () => root.querySelector('#v').textContent = r.value;+ r.oninput = show; r.onchange = () => { show(); emit('runs_a_day', +r.value); }; show();+};+```++```canvas brick id=p7 src=leela_bricks:viz.series+bind labels = [r['label'] for r in rows]+bind series = [{'name': 'monthly $', 'values': [r['monthly'] for r in rows]}]+prop height = 240+```++Every model here prices an output token at four to five times an input token. A+barrier half again as thick therefore leaks much less than half as much.++```canvas ask id=q6+explain tunnelling+```++```canvas video id=q7 src=Ltni6c1lC4c+Sixty Symbols explains quantum tunnelling aloud.+```++<!--canvas quiz id=q8-->+1. Why does doubling the barrier width cost more than doubling its height+2. What is the packet doing inside the barrier, if it is not oscillating+3. int(op.get(&#x27;nth&#x27;) or 0))</span><span class="dl a">+ if at is None: return {&#x27;ok&#x27;: False, &#x27;error&#x27;: &#x27;that selection is no longer in this brick&#x27;}</span><span class="dl a">+ i, n = at</span><span class="dl a">+ b.body = b.body[:i] + now + b.body[i + n:]</span><span class="dl a">+ gone = runtime.retire(b) if runtime is not None else []</span><span class="dl brick&#x27;}</span><span class="dl a">+ r = runtime.run(b)</span><span class="dl a">+ settle = runtime.react(canvas.bricks, r[&#x27;defs&#x27;], skip=[b.id])</span><span class="dl a">+ return The gap is almost</span><span class="dl a">+entirely low-value tail spend that never needed a buyer.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas source id=s-audit title=&quot;Internal audit, Q3 FY25&quot; path=drive/audit-q3.pdf--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+34% of purchase orders raised in Q3 were under EUR 2,000. Use only the three sources here.</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas reply of=q-synth--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+Tail spend is the only pool big enough. 34% of POs are under EUR 2,000 and carry a three-person</span><span class="dl a">+approval chain that the audit found nobody ever rejects. Auto-approving that band would take</span><span class="dl a">+roughly a third of PO volume off the buyers without touching the categories where negotiation</span><span class="dl a">+earns money. On the interview evidence that is about 12% of buyer time, which clears the target.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Baseline the tail</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas code id=c-load</span><span class="dl a">+pos = read_extract(&#x27;drive/po-q3.parquet&#x27;)</span><span class="dl a">+preferred = frozenset(contracted_suppliers())</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas code id=c-band</span><span class="dl a">+#|export</span><span class="dl a">+def bands(pos, cut=2000):</span><span class="dl a">+ &quot;Split a PO extract into the tail below `cut` and the rest.&quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ tail = pos[pos.value_eur &lt; cut]</span><span class="dl a">+ return tail, pos.drop(tail.index)</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas code id=c-share</span><span class="dl a">+tail, rest = bands(pos)</span><span class="dl a">+share = len(tail) / len(pos)</span><span class="dl a">+chain = tail.approvers.median()</span><span class="dl a">+share, chain</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas code id=c-cycle</span><span class="dl a">+cycle = tail.assign(days=(tail.approved_at - tail.raised_at).dt.days).groupby(&#x27;region&#x27;).days.mean()</span><span class="dl a">+cycle</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas data id=d-say</span><span class="dl a">+bind text = f&quot;The tail is **{share:.0%}** of all POs, sits behind **{chain:.0f}** approvers, and takes **{cycle.mean():.1f} days** to clear.&quot;</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The sentence above binds to the numbers rather than quoting them. Rebuild the cycle time from the timestamps and leave it as `cycle`.</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Prototype the triage rule</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas bundle id=triage title=&quot;Auto-approve the contracted tail&quot; goal=goal contributes=&quot;most of the 10 points; the cap is the rest&quot; paths=tests/test_triage.py refs=file:procure/core.py,pkg:pandas,doc:drive/audit-q3.pdf--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+Adds `triage`, the rule that lets an indirect PO under EUR 2,000 from a contracted supplier skip</span><span class="dl a">+the approval chain. Backtested against the Q3 extract. Check it against the audit.</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas reply of=q-risk--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+79% of the tail clears the rule, which is 27% of all POs. One page, no hedging.</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas reply of=q-rec--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+Auto-approve indirect POs under EUR 2,000 from contracted suppliers, capped per supplier per</span><span class="dl a">+month. One markdown file where prose is prose and everything else is a</span><span class="dl a">+brick, and where each brick recomputes when what it reads moves. The document is the program and</span><span class="dl a">+the note about the program at once.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## The file</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`*.canvas.md`. Optional YAML frontmatter carries `title` and `mode`. Prose between bricks is a</span><span class="dl a">+`text` brick and needs no markup of its own.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A brick that is opaque to markdown is a fence:</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+ ```canvas &lt;kind&gt; id=&lt;id&gt; key=value ...</span><span class="dl a">+ &lt;body&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+ ```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A brick whose body is markdown a plain renderer should still show is a comment wrap:</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+ &lt;!--canvas &lt;kind&gt; id=&lt;id&gt;--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+ Ordinary **markdown**.</span><span class="dl a">+ &lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Fenced kinds: `code`, `ask`, `brick`, `sim`, `data`, `pdf`, `video`.</span><span class="dl a">+Wrapped kinds: `reply`, `note`, `quiz`.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A non-code brick body holds directives, one per line, and nothing else:</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+ bind &lt;port&gt; = &lt;expression&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+ prop &lt;key&gt; = &lt;value&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A code brick body is the code, kept exactly. They run in dependency order derived from the AST, not document</span><span class="dl a">+order, so a cell may be written above the cell it needs. A canvas stores no outputs: opening one</span><span class="dl a">+runs it.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`bind port = expression` evaluates the expression against that namespace and hands the result to</span><span class="dl a">+the brick. When a name the expression reads moves, the binding is resolved again. A binding that</span><span class="dl a">+raises reports on the brick rather than blanking it.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`data` is the brick that makes prose live: `bind text = f&quot;...&quot;` renders the result as markdown.</span><span class="dl a">+Prefer it over writing a number into prose. A number written by hand is wrong the moment anything</span><span class="dl a">+above it changes.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Emits: what a component hands back</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A component brick emits. `emit_&lt;port&gt;=&lt;name&gt;` in its attributes says which name in the namespace a</span><span class="dl a">+port writes to. Clicking a funnel bar, a rasi or an organelle sets that name and reruns everything</span><span class="dl a">+that reads it. A component is an input as much as an output.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Two components in one document must not write to the same name unless they are meant to.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Components, bricks and sketches</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`brick` embeds a component from a package: `src=lego.bricks:viz.series`. The package declares the</span><span class="dl a">+ports, what it emits, and the code that fills it. Take that code rather than writing your own:</span><span class="dl a">+`canvas_wire(name)` returns it, `canvas_insert` puts it in the document as an ordinary code brick,</span><span class="dl a">+and `canvas_bind` points the ports at what it defined. The wiring stays visible in the file.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`sim` is a component written in the document itself. Its body is JavaScript with `root`, `props`</span><span class="dl a">+and `emit` in scope, and nothing else. Promote one into a package without changing a line.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Your tools: the ports into the document</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+| tool | does |</span><span class="dl a">+|---|---|</span><span class="dl a">+| `canvas_read` | the document as it stands: every brick, its kind, its bindings, what it defines |</span><span class="dl a">+| `canvas_insert` | a new brick at a position. `after=&lt;id&gt;` or `at=&lt;index&gt;` |</span><span class="dl a">+| `canvas_replace` | rewrite one brick, by id |</span><span class="dl a">+| `canvas_remove` | take a brick out, by id |</span><span class="dl a">+| `canvas_bind` | point one port of one brick at an expression |</span><span class="dl a">+| `canvas_run` | run a code brick and let the dataflow settle |</span><span class="dl a">+| `canvas_answer` | prose written back into the document, attached to the question that asked for it |</span><span class="dl a">+| `canvas_values` | read names out of the live namespace |</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Every one goes through the same function the person&#x27;s own edits go through. There is no second</span><span class="dl a">+path into the document, and nothing else you can reach touches it.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## How to work</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Read before you write. `canvas_read` costs one call and tells you what ids exist, what each cell</span><span class="dl a">+defines and what every binding reads. Editing by guess breaks bindings that were fine.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Answer where the question was asked. `canvas_answer(of=&lt;ask id&gt;)` puts the reply under the ask and</span><span class="dl a">+replaces the previous one rather than stacking. Prose that belongs in the document goes in the</span><span class="dl a">+document, not only in the reply.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Change the smallest thing. A wrong number is usually one binding, not a rewritten section. Rewrite</span><span class="dl a">+a selection with `canvas_replace` only for the span you were given.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Insert code that runs. A code brick arrives to be run: it runs where it lands, and anything bound</span><span class="dl a">+to the names it defines resolves. Do not insert a cell that needs a second call to be useful.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Bind rather than paste. If a value already exists in the namespace, bind to it. Pasting the value</span><span class="dl a">+makes a document that was live into a document that was true once.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Name what you emit. When you add a component whose clicks should drive something, set</span><span class="dl a">+`emit_&lt;port&gt;` to a name the document already reads, or add the cell that reads it in the same turn.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Prefer a brick to a paragraph about a brick. A canvas is for showing the thing.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## The trail, and where a question came from</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A question carries where it was asked from: the brick, and the text that was selected in it. The</span><span class="dl a">+last dozen of those are the trail, and they arrive with the turn. Use them. &quot;Why is that one</span><span class="dl a">+cheaper&quot; resolves against the row that was clicked, and asking the person to repeat themselves</span><span class="dl a">+wastes the context you were given.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A selection is a span, not a topic. to be an HTTP call to a second server. It is an entry-point group now. A library+answers four questions. Its manifest, one brick, that brick's wiring, and its own routes.</p>+<h3>Change</h3>+<details><summary>docs/bricks.md +104 -0</summary><div class="in"><div class="diff"><div class="body"><span class="dl h">@@ -0,0 +1,104 @@</span><span class="dl a">+# Bricks</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A `brick` in a canvas document embeds a component from a library. `src=leela_bricks:viz.series` says which library and which component. This is where a component comes from, and what a library has to be.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Read this with [dynamic-documents.md](dynamic-documents.md), which is what a brick sits in.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Where a component comes from</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`leela/blocks/canvas/bricks.py` finds libraries three ways, in this order.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+An entry point under `leela.bricks`, which is how a pip-installed library publishes itself. `shalya` finds pyskills the same way, and the codebase therefore already uses this pattern.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A name in `KNOWN`, for a library that publishes no entry point. `lego.bricks` is the only one.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`LEELA_BRICK_HOST`, for a library nobody installed. It is empty by default. The earlier design defaulted it to `http://127.0.0.1:5001`, which is Leela&#x27;s own port. A fresh install therefore fetched its palette from Leela, got nothing, and reported nothing.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A library is any module with `manifest()` and `find(name)`. There is no base class and nothing to register. `leela_bricks` satisfies it.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## What Leela does with one</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`palette(libs)` merges every library&#x27;s manifest and stamps each row with the library it came from. `locate(src)` returns the library and the brick. `wire(src)` returns the snippet that fills the brick&#x27;s ports. `mount(app)` registers each library&#x27;s own routes on Leela&#x27;s app.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The library&#x27;s `serve.py` takes `(app, page=None)`, and it opens with &quot;Nothing here imports the application it is mounted in&quot;. Leela&#x27;s own process therefore serves the gallery, the component frame and the port data, on Leela&#x27;s own port. No second server runs, and `LEELA_BRICK_HOST` serves only a library nobody installed.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`split_src` keeps the library prefix. The earlier code did `src.split(&#x27;:&#x27;)[-1]` and threw it away, which makes two libraries that each have a `viz.series` resolve to whichever answered first. Only the named library now answers a prefixed `src`. A bare name searches every library and takes the first, which is why a document should write the prefix.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## What was measured</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Eight files went into an empty package with a two-line `__init__.py`, and nothing else changed. The package imports on `fastcore` and `fasthtml` alone. Leela&#x27;s resolver reads it as 10 bricks in 4 groups. `locate` finds ports and emits. `wire` returns the package&#x27;s own snippet and its remote fallback. `mount` registers all seven routes on a `FastHTML` app. `data.fill(&#x27;viz.series&#x27;)` runs the snippet and returns real values.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The extraction is a packaging change rather than a redesign, and the code already sits on the right side of the line.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Two facts decide where the line goes.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`lego/__init__.py` is `from .app import *` and `lego/bricks/__init__.py` is `from .app import connect`. Either one is enough to make `import lego.bricks` boot lego&#x27;s whole application. In this container it fails on `ujson`, one of lego&#x27;s thirteen dependencies. Nothing under `lego/bricks/` other than `app.py` imports `lego`.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Four of the ten bricks carry wiring that imports a domain package. `panchanga.day`, `panchanga.horas` and `panchanga.wheel` import `lego.muhurtha.panchanga`. `thrifty.costs` imports `lego.thrifty.data`. The other six, every `viz.*` and every `learn.*`, ship no wiring at all. They are display components that read whatever the document already computed.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## What to extract</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Take the contract and the six domain-free bricks. Leave the four domain bricks with the packages their wiring needs.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+| goes | is |</span><span class="dl a">+|---|---|</span><span class="dl a">+| `bricks.py` | `Port`, `Brick`, the registry, `manifest()`, `find()` |</span><span class="dl a">+| `cfg.py` | the seven route paths |</span><span class="dl a">+| `serve.py` | `connect(app, page=None)`, which imports nothing about the app |</span><span class="dl a">+| `data.py` | `fill()` runs a brick&#x27;s snippet here; `remote_wire()` is the call for a document that lacks the package |</span><span class="dl a">+| `ui.py`, `bricks.js`, `bricks.css`, `frame.js` | the gallery, the frame, and the drawing keyed by brick name |</span><span class="dl a">+| `viz.*`, `learn.*` | six bricks with no wiring and no domain dependency |</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+| stays | why |</span><span class="dl a">+|---|---|</span><span class="dl a">+| `app.py` | it is the upstream seam: `lego.core`, `RouteOverrides`, the upstream nav |</span><span class="dl a">+| `panchanga.*`, `thrifty.*` | their wiring imports `lego.muhurtha` and `lego.thrifty` |</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## The spec is now built</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`extensions/bricks` is the extracted package, `leela-bricks`. Eight files moved with no</span><span class="dl a">+edit. Only `bricks.py` changed, and it took all four changes below.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+ uv pip install -e extensions/bricks</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+That is the whole install, and the entry point does the rest. `libraries()` finds</span><span class="dl a">+`leela_bricks`, `palette()` reads ten components in four groups, and the notes list is empty.</span><span class="dl a">+`KNOWN` still names `lego.bricks` for a library that publishes no entry point, and an absent</span><span class="dl a">+library produces no note.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The four domain bricks came too, and their wiring still imports `lego.muhurtha` and `lego.thrifty`.</span><span class="dl a">+`needs` exists for that case, and the palette therefore names the package a component wants before the cell runs.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+| brick | needs |</span><span class="dl a">+|---|---|</span><span class="dl a">+| `panchanga.day`, `panchanga.horas`, `panchanga.wheel` | `lego.muhurtha.panchanga` |</span><span class="dl a">+| `thrifty.costs` | `lego.thrifty.data` |</span><span class="dl a">+| `viz.tiles`, `viz.series`, `viz.funnel` | nothing |</span><span class="dl a">+| `learn.cell`, `learn.wavepacket`, `learn.orbit` | nothing |</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Four changes the extracted package needs</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+**Own the `src` prefix.** `Brick.src` was `f&#x27;lego.bricks:{self.name}&#x27;`, hardcoded. After extraction that string names a package that no longer holds the brick. `LIB = __name__.rsplit(&#x27;.&#x27;, 1)[0]` derives it. Renaming the package therefore updates every `src` it serves.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+**Give each library its own registry.** `BRICKS` is a module-global dict and `brick()` mutates it. That works while one package registers everything. It breaks as soon as a second library keeps its own bricks. That library would call `brick()` into the extracted package&#x27;s global, and then every library&#x27;s `manifest()` would return every library&#x27;s bricks. The package exposes a `Registry` a library instantiates, with `manifest()` and `find()` reading its own. `manifest()` also returns `library`, which tells a caller which registry answered.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+**Publish the entry point.** `[project.entry-points.&quot;leela.bricks&quot;]` so Leela finds the library without `KNOWN`. `pip install` is the whole of procurement. `KNOWN` stays for a library that publishes none.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+**Say when a snippet needs a package.** A brick whose `wire` imports something should declare it. `data.fill` already catches the failure, and `remote_wire` is already the fallback. A document still discovers the missing package by running a cell and reading a traceback. The manifest row carries `needs`. A regex over the wiring&#x27;s own `import` lines produces it, minus the standard library. A component cannot claim a dependency its code does not import, and cannot hide one it does.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## What Leela ships</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Leela includes no components of its own. A `sim` is a component the document itself defines, in JavaScript, with `root`, `props` and `emit` in scope. A `sim` needs no package, and Leela therefore stays fully usable with no library installed. The canvas skill states that you can move a `sim` into a package without changing a line.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Leela ships the resolver and the contract. A chart is not IDE behaviour. A bundled component library would become a compatibility surface, held forever on Leela&#x27;s release clock rather than the library&#x27;s. The same reason keeps `kunda`, `kavacha` and `pullup` out of this repository.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## What the merge connected</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`leela/blocks/canvas/app.py` now holds both halves. The palette route is the resolver, and the two</span><span class="dl a">+routes that fetched from a host have gone. `/canvas/palette` reads `palette(libs)`, and</span><span class="dl a">+`/canvas/wire/{name}` reads the library. `_wire_from_host` keeps its name and reads the library</span><span class="dl a">+too, and it no longer drops the `src` prefix. Nothing in the block imports `urllib` any more.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`brick_host()` survives as the base for `remote_wire`. `remote_wire` is the snippet a document</span><span class="dl a">+runs when it holds the component but not the package that fills it. HTTP is the right answer in</span><span class="dl a">+that one case, and in no other.</span></div></div></div></details><figure><div class="diff"><div class="hd"><span class="p">extensions/bricks/.gitignore</span><span class="chip add">+1</span><span class="chip rm">-0</span></div><div class="body"><span class="dl h">@@ -0,0 +1 @@</span><span class="dl a">+__pycache__/</span></div></div></figure><details><summary>extensions/bricks/README.md +57 -0</summary><div class="in"><div class="diff"><div class="body"><span class="dl h">@@ -0,0 +1,57 @@</span><span class="dl a">+# leela-bricks</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Components a canvas document can embed. Ten of them, in four groups.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A canvas document embeds one with a `brick` brick:</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```markdown</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas brick id=b1 src=leela_bricks:viz.series emit_point=point</span><span class="dl a">+bind labels = list(cycle.index)</span><span class="dl a">+bind series = [{&#x27;name&#x27;: &#x27;days to clear&#x27;, &#x27;values&#x27;: list(cycle.values)}]</span><span class="dl a">+prop height = 240</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Install</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```sh</span><span class="dl a">+pip install -e extensions/bricks</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Leela finds it through the `leela.bricks` entry point. Leela needs no other configuration, and</span><span class="dl a">+`LEELA_BRICK_HOST` serves only a library nobody installed. See</span><span class="dl a">+[docs/bricks.md](../../docs/bricks.md).</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## What a brick declares</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`Registry.brick(name, title, group, ports, emits, wire, height, doc)`. `ports` name what the component draws</span><span class="dl a">+from. `emits` name what a click writes back into the document&#x27;s namespace. `wire` is the code</span><span class="dl a">+that fills the ports.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`wire` gives `needs`, and nobody declares it. `needs` is the top-level packages the snippet</span><span class="dl a">+imports, minus the standard library. Six of the ten need nothing. The four under `panchanga` and</span><span class="dl a">+`thrifty` each import a domain package, and a document without that package reads its ports over</span><span class="dl a">+`data.remote_wire` instead.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`src` is `LIB:name`, and `LIB` is this package&#x27;s own module name. Another pid, an interrupted loop with the namespace</span><span class="dl a">+intact, and recovery after `os._exit`.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas task id=t6 status=done owner=me--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+Make `pytest -m slow` finish, and fix what running it found.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+# The prose</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas bundle id=u-prose title=&quot;Every page scored, and the English fixed&quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ goal=g</span><span class="dl a">+ contributes=&quot;the English a reviewer reads&quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ covers=&quot;t7&quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ paths=README.md,docs/*.md,examples/canvas/*,docs/screenshots/*,media/*,.gitignore</span><span class="dl a">+ refs=pkg:slopometer,pkg:fastaistyle,doc:leela/blocks/canvas/ste.md--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+`slopometer` scores a page against the reference-prose rules. `chkstyle` scores Python against</span><span class="dl a">+fastai&#x27;s. `ste.md` already held the rules. `explain.md` handed them to the model that drafts a</span><span class="dl a">+snippet. A drafted sentence met them. A hand-written one did not.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas note id=n-readme path=README.md--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+12.9 to 2.9. Three patterns carried most of the weight. A sentence that states a thing and then</span><span class="dl a">+restates its opposite. A closing line that reverses the one before it.
