The</span><span class="dl a">+worst page on the branch fell from 26.8 to 2.5 and four pages now score zero.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas task id=t7 status=done owner=me--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+Score every page with slopometer, and rewrite the prose that fails ASD-STE100.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+# The numbers</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas data id=n-tally--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+files = 137</span><span class="dl a">+insertions = 12508</span><span class="dl a">+deletions = 290</span><span class="dl a">+tests = 2045</span><span class="dl a">+slow_tests = 139</span><span class="dl a">+review_findings_closed = 17</span><span class="dl a">+worst_page_before = 26.8</span><span class="dl a">+worst_page_after = 2.5</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas ask id=q1 scope=doc budget=40000--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+Name the change here you would push back on, and say what you would want instead.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span></div></div></div></details><details><summary>docs/bricks.md +104 -0</summary><div class="in"><div class="diff"><div class="body"><span class="dl h">@@ -0,0 +1,104 @@</span><span class="dl a">+# Bricks</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A `brick` in a canvas document embeds a component from a library. `src=leela_bricks:viz.series` says which library and which component. This is where a component comes from, and what a library has to be.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Read this with [dynamic-documents.md](dynamic-documents.md), which is what a brick sits in.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Where a component comes from</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`leela/blocks/canvas/bricks.py` finds libraries three ways, in this order.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+An entry point under `leela.bricks`, which is how a pip-installed library publishes itself. `shalya` finds pyskills the same way, and the codebase therefore already uses this pattern.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A name in `KNOWN`, for a library that publishes no entry point. `lego.bricks` is the only one.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`LEELA_BRICK_HOST`, for a library nobody installed. It is empty by default. The earlier design defaulted it to `http://127.0.0.1:5001`, which is Leela&#x27;s own port. A fresh install therefore fetched its palette from Leela, got nothing, and reported nothing.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A library is any module with `manifest()` and `find(name)`. There is no base class and nothing to register. `leela_bricks` satisfies it.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## What Leela does with one</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`palette(libs)` merges every library&#x27;s manifest and stamps each row with the library it came from. `locate(src)` returns the library and the brick. `wire(src)` returns the snippet that fills the brick&#x27;s ports. `mount(app)` registers each library&#x27;s own routes on Leela&#x27;s app.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The library&#x27;s `serve.py` takes `(app, page=None)`, and it opens with &quot;Nothing here imports the application it is mounted in&quot;. Leela&#x27;s own process therefore serves the gallery, the component frame and the port data, on Leela&#x27;s own port. No second server runs, and `LEELA_BRICK_HOST` serves only a library nobody installed.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`split_src` keeps the library prefix. The earlier code did `src.split(&#x27;:&#x27;)[-1]` and threw it away, which makes two libraries that each have a `viz.series` resolve to whichever answered first. Only the named library now answers a prefixed `src`. A bare name searches every library and takes the first, which is why a document should write the prefix.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## What was measured</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Eight files went into an empty package with a two-line `__init__.py`, and nothing else changed. The package imports on `fastcore` and `fasthtml` alone. Leela&#x27;s resolver reads it as 10 bricks in 4 groups. `locate` finds ports and emits. `wire` returns the package&#x27;s own snippet and its remote fallback. `mount` registers all seven routes on a `FastHTML` app. `data.fill(&#x27;viz.series&#x27;)` runs the snippet and returns real values.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The extraction is a packaging change rather than a redesign, and the code already sits on the right side of the line.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Two facts decide where the line goes.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`lego/__init__.py` is `from .app import *` and `lego/bricks/__init__.py` is `from .app import connect`. Either one is enough to make `import lego.bricks` boot lego&#x27;s whole application. In this container it fails on `ujson`, one of lego&#x27;s thirteen dependencies. Nothing under `lego/bricks/` other than `app.py` imports `lego`.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Four of the ten bricks carry wiring that imports a domain package. `panchanga.day`, `panchanga.horas` and `panchanga.wheel` import `lego.muhurtha.panchanga`. `thrifty.costs` imports `lego.thrifty.data`. The other six, every `viz.*` and every `learn.*`, ship no wiring at all. They are display components that read whatever the document already computed.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## What to extract</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Take the contract and the six domain-free bricks. Leave the four domain bricks with the packages their wiring needs.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+| goes | is |</span><span class="dl a">+|---|---|</span><span class="dl a">+| `bricks.py` | `Port`, `Brick`, the registry, `manifest()`, `find()` |</span><span class="dl a">+| `cfg.py` | the seven route paths |</span><span class="dl a">+| `serve.py` | `connect(app, page=None)`, which imports nothing about the app |</span><span class="dl a">+| `data.py` | `fill()` runs a brick&#x27;s snippet here; `remote_wire()` is the call for a document that lacks the package |</span><span class="dl a">+| `ui.py`, `bricks.js`, `bricks.css`, `frame.js` | the gallery, the frame, and the drawing keyed by brick name |</span><span class="dl a">+| `viz.*`, `learn.*` | six bricks with no wiring and no domain dependency |</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+| stays | why |</span><span class="dl a">+|---|---|</span><span class="dl a">+| `app.py` | it is the upstream seam: `lego.core`, `RouteOverrides`, the upstream nav |</span><span class="dl a">+| `panchanga.*`, `thrifty.*` | their wiring imports `lego.muhurtha` and `lego.thrifty` |</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## The spec is now built</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`extensions/bricks` is the extracted package, `leela-bricks`. Eight files moved with no</span><span class="dl a">+edit. Only `bricks.py` changed, and it took all four changes below.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+ uv pip install -e extensions/bricks</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+That is the whole install, and the entry point does the rest. `libraries()` finds</span><span class="dl a">+`leela_bricks`, `palette()` reads ten components in four groups, and the notes list is empty.</span><span class="dl a">+`KNOWN` still names `lego.bricks` for a library that publishes no entry point, and an absent</span><span class="dl a">+library produces no note.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The four domain bricks came too, and their wiring still imports `lego.muhurtha` and `lego.thrifty`.</span><span class="dl a">+`needs` exists for that case, and the palette therefore names the package a component wants before the cell runs.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+| brick | needs |</span><span class="dl a">+|---|---|</span><span class="dl a">+| `panchanga.day`, `panchanga.horas`, `panchanga.wheel` | `lego.muhurtha.panchanga` |</span><span class="dl a">+| `thrifty.costs` | `lego.thrifty.data` |</span><span class="dl a">+| `viz.tiles`, `viz.series`, `viz.funnel` | nothing |</span><span class="dl a">+| `learn.cell`, `learn.wavepacket`, `learn.orbit` | nothing |</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Four changes the extracted package needs</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+**Own the `src` prefix.** `Brick.src` was `f&#x27;lego.bricks:{self.name}&#x27;`, hardcoded. After extraction that string names a package that no longer holds the brick. `LIB = __name__.rsplit(&#x27;.&#x27;, 1)[0]` derives it. Renaming the package therefore updates every `src` it serves.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+**Give each library its own registry.** `BRICKS` is a module-global dict and `brick()` mutates it. That works while one package registers everything. It breaks as soon as a second library keeps its own bricks. That library would call `brick()` into the extracted package&#x27;s global, and then every library&#x27;s `manifest()` would return every library&#x27;s bricks. The package exposes a `Registry` a library instantiates, with `manifest()` and `find()` reading its own. `manifest()` also returns `library`, which tells a caller which registry answered.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+**Publish the entry point.** `[project.entry-points.&quot;leela.bricks&quot;]` so Leela finds the library without `KNOWN`. `pip install` is the whole of procurement. `KNOWN` stays for a library that publishes none.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+**Say when a snippet needs a package.** A brick whose `wire` imports something should declare it. `data.fill` already catches the failure, and `remote_wire` is already the fallback. A document still discovers the missing package by running a cell and reading a traceback. The manifest row carries `needs`. A regex over the wiring&#x27;s own `import` lines produces it, minus the standard library. A component cannot claim a dependency its code does not import, and cannot hide one it does.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## What Leela ships</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Leela includes no components of its own. A `sim` is a component the document itself defines, in JavaScript, with `root`, `props` and `emit` in scope. A `sim` needs no package, and Leela therefore stays fully usable with no library installed. The canvas skill states that you can move a `sim` into a package without changing a line.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Leela ships the resolver and the contract. A chart is not IDE behaviour. A bundled component library would become a compatibility surface, held forever on Leela&#x27;s release clock rather than the library&#x27;s. The same reason keeps `kunda`, `kavacha` and `pullup` out of this repository.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## What the merge connected</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`leela/blocks/canvas/app.py` now holds both halves. The palette route is the resolver, and the two</span><span class="dl a">+routes that fetched from a host have gone. `/canvas/palette` reads `palette(libs)`, and</span><span class="dl a">+`/canvas/wire/{name}` reads the library. `_wire_from_host` keeps its name and reads the library</span><span class="dl a">+too, and it no longer drops the `src` prefix. Nothing in the block imports `urllib` any more.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`brick_host()` survives as the base for `remote_wire`. `remote_wire` is the snippet a document</span><span class="dl a">+runs when it holds the component but not the package that fills it. HTTP is the right answer in</span><span class="dl a">+that one case, and in no other.</span></div></div></div></details><details><summary>docs/canvas.md +287 -0</summary><div class="in"><div class="diff"><div class="body"><span class="dl h">@@ -0,0 +1,287 @@</span><span class="dl a">+# Canvas</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+One file holds prose, code, embedded components, simulations, PDFs and video. Each brick in it</span><span class="dl a">+recomputes when a name it reads changes.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The notebook Leela already has is a list of cells. A canvas is prose with everything else inside it,</span><span class="dl a">+and its cells are not the point of the document. `leela/blocks/canvas/` is the block.</span><span class="dl a">+`examples/canvas/` holds six of them.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+![A canvas open](screenshots/canvas-funnel.png)</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## The file</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A canvas is markdown. `*.canvas.md`. Prose is prose. Everything else is a fenced block or a</span><span class="dl a">+comment-wrapped region, and both survive a plain markdown renderer.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+````md</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas code id=c1</span><span class="dl a">+tokens = 1200</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas brick id=b1 src=lego.bricks:thrifty.costs emit_row=picked</span><span class="dl a">+bind rows = rows</span><span class="dl a">+prop height = 220</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas note id=n1--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+An **aside**, still rendered by anything that reads markdown.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+````</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Fenced kinds: `code`, `ask`, `brick`, `sim`, `data`, `pdf`, `video`. Wrapped kinds: `reply`, `note`,</span><span class="dl a">+`quiz`. Anything else in the file is a `text` brick.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The parser is a line scan rather than a pair of regular expressions. A canvas fence inside a longer</span><span class="dl a">+markdown fence is an example of a brick and not a brick. A document about canvases is itself a</span><span class="dl a">+canvas. Windows line endings read the same as Unix ones. Two bricks cannot share an id, and the</span><span class="dl a">+parser therefore gives the second brick a fresh id on read. Without that rule, every op on the first brick</span><span class="dl a">+would reach the second one in silence.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A `pdf` brick with a relative `src` is a file beside the canvas, served by `/canvas/file`, which</span><span class="dl a">+resolves under the canvas directory and refuses anything above it.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A brick body holds `bind &lt;port&gt; = &lt;expression&gt;` and `prop &lt;key&gt; = &lt;value&gt;` lines. The body of a code brick</span><span class="dl a">+is the code itself, kept exactly, and nothing reads it for directives.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A canvas stores no outputs, and opening one runs it. The file therefore diffs to what somebody</span><span class="dl a">+changed and nothing else. `test_canvas.py` opens a canvas, runs it, wires it and asks questions of</span><span class="dl a">+it, then asserts that it saves back byte for byte.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## The dataflow</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Code bricks share one namespace and run in dependency order rather than document order. `defs_of`</span><span class="dl a">+reads what a brick defines from its AST; `reads_of` reads what it needs. `order` sorts them. A cycle</span><span class="dl a">+falls back to document order.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`downstream(bricks, names)` is what makes the document live. It returns every code brick whose</span><span class="dl a">+inputs include one of `names`, transitively, followed by every brick with a binding that reads one.</span><span class="dl a">+Setting a name reruns exactly that set.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Bindings are expressions evaluated against the namespace. A binding that raises reports the error on</span><span class="dl a">+the brick rather than blanking it.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Components</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Every embedded component runs in an iframe. The document and the frame exchange four messages and</span><span class="dl a">+nothing else.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+| message | direction | meaning |</span><span class="dl a">+|---|---|---|</span><span class="dl a">+| `brick:ready` | frame to document | the frame has loaded, with its manifest |</span><span class="dl a">+| `brick:props` | document to frame | resolved port values |</span><span class="dl a">+| `brick:height` | frame to document | how tall it wants to be |</span><span class="dl a">+| `brick:emit` | frame to document | a value the person produced by using it |</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`brick:emit` is why a canvas is not a dashboard. Clicking an organelle, a rasi or a funnel bar writes</span><span class="dl a">+a name into the namespace, and every cell that reads that name reruns. A component is an input as</span><span class="dl a">+much as an output.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The brick&#x27;s attributes name the port&#x27;s target as `emit_&lt;port&gt;`. Two funnels in one document</span><span class="dl a">+therefore never fight over `stages`.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+![Clicking a component writes into the document](screenshots/canvas-cell.png)</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Wiring</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The package that owns the component declares its ports, and the document never does.</span><span class="dl a">+`leela_bricks` is one such package. Each brick in it declares its ports, what it emits, and the</span><span class="dl a">+code that fills it.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Picking a component from the palette inserts it and reads its wiring. Leela puts that code in the</span><span class="dl a">+document as an ordinary code brick, then binds the ports it filled. You can see and edit the</span><span class="dl a">+wiring, and the document holds no hidden connection.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Where a component comes from is [bricks.md](bricks.md). Leela reads the palette and the wiring in</span><span class="dl a">+process, from a library installed beside it. `LEELA_BRICK_HOST` is the fallback for a library</span><span class="dl a">+nobody installed. An earlier version of this block fetched both over HTTP, from a default that</span><span class="dl a">+was Leela&#x27;s own port. A fresh install therefore had an empty palette and no error.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A package ships its wiring twice. The first form imports the package, and the second form calls</span><span class="dl a">+the host that owns it. The document runs the first form, and falls back to the second when the</span><span class="dl a">+import fails. That import fails when the package is not beside the document.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```python</span><span class="dl a">+from lego.muhurtha.panchanga import Place, day_panchanga</span><span class="dl a">+day = day_panchanga(Place(12.97, 77.59, &#x27;Asia/Kolkata&#x27;, &#x27;Bengaluru&#x27;), date.today())</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```python</span><span class="dl a">+import json, urllib.request</span><span class="dl a">+_ports = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(&#x27;http://127.0.0.1:5001/bricks/data/panchanga.day&#x27;))</span><span class="dl a">+day = _ports[&#x27;day&#x27;]</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The ⚙ in a brick&#x27;s rail opens the wiring panel: every port, its expression, what it currently</span><span class="dl a">+resolves to, and the names in the namespace to pick from.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+![The wiring panel](screenshots/canvas-wire.png)</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The palette is what the host publishes, grouped by the block that owns each component.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+![The palette](screenshots/canvas-palette.png)</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## The helper</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Three places reach the one helper: the margin, an `ask` brick in the document, and `mod+k`</span><span class="dl a">+anywhere. All three run the same turn, and only the selection that travels with it differs.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Its reach into the document is eight tools and no others.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+| tool | does |</span><span class="dl a">+|---|---|</span><span class="dl a">+| `canvas_read` | the document as it stands |</span><span class="dl a">+| `canvas_insert` | a new brick at a position |</span><span class="dl a">+| `canvas_replace` | rewrite one brick |</span><span class="dl a">+| `canvas_remove` | take a brick out |</span><span class="dl a">+| `canvas_bind` | point a port at an expression |</span><span class="dl a">+| `canvas_run` | run a code brick and let the dataflow settle |</span><span class="dl a">+| `canvas_answer` | prose attached to the question that asked for it |</span><span class="dl a">+| `canvas_values` | read names out of the namespace |</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Every one goes through `apply_op`, which is also what the person&#x27;s own edits go through. There is no</span><span class="dl a">+second path into the document.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A turn streams `step`, `chunk`, `op`, `answer`, `done`. The document applies each `op` event as it</span><span class="dl a">+arrives, and a brick therefore appears while the turn is still running. Steering is a queue per</span><span class="dl a">+turn. The turn takes text posted to `/canvas/steer` at the next step boundary, and replans the</span><span class="dl a">+rest of the turn.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The trail is the last twelve questions, each with the brick it came from and the selection it</span><span class="dl a">+carried. It goes into the next turn&#x27;s context, which is why a follow-up needs no preamble.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+![Steering a turn that is already running](screenshots/canvas-steer.png)</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Canvas mode</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+What the agent knows about a canvas is a skill, and Leela owns it. `leela/skills/canvas.py` is the</span><span class="dl a">+body: the file format, the dataflow, what a component emits, the eight tools, and how to work in one.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+It is not a `pyskills` entry point. A skill that is only true inside a canvas should not reach</span><span class="dl a">+every agent that has Leela installed. `leela.skills.push(agent, &#x27;canvas&#x27;)` puts the skill on the</span><span class="dl a">+agent&#x27;s registry when a canvas opens, and `drop` takes it off when the canvas closes. The eight</span><span class="dl a">+tools go on and come off with it. `Agentic.open` and `Agentic.close` are those two calls.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Ramabana holds none of this. `Agent.skills` is `discover(..., extra=registry.skills)`. A pushed</span><span class="dl a">+skill therefore reaches the skill index and `read_skill` with no change to the agent core. The</span><span class="dl a">+proposal on `ramabana`&#x27;s branch turns the tools into a shalya capability group. The skill stays</span><span class="dl a">+Leela&#x27;s either way.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The skill is also the stand-in&#x27;s source. The stand-in answers a question about the canvas out of</span><span class="dl a">+the section of the skill that covers it, which keeps one text right rather than two.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## The model</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`helper_for(agent)` returns `Agentic` where a model exists and `Scripted` where none does.</span><span class="dl a">+`Scripted` is deterministic. It reads the same `Ask`, calls the same tools, and emits the same</span><span class="dl a">+events. It carries no judgement and no facts. To answer a question about a word, it finds where</span><span class="dl a">+this document already explains that word. A word the document never explains gets no answer.</span><span class="dl a">+It scores which component to embed against what the host publishes, never against a table kept</span><span class="dl a">+here.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`Agentic` runs the real turn. The spike never exercises it, because the spike has no model.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## The editor</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+You edit the document in place. Prose stays rendered while you work in it, and it returns to</span><span class="dl a">+markdown on the way out. Selecting a sentence to ask about it therefore leaves the sentence</span><span class="dl a">+looking the same.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+| where | what |</span><span class="dl a">+|---|---|</span><span class="dl a">+| gutter | `+` inserts under the block, the grip drags it, clicking the grip opens what else it can do |</span><span class="dl a">+| `/` on an empty line | the block menu, grouped, filtered as you type, driven by the keyboard |</span><span class="dl a">+| a text selection | bold, italic, code, link, and Ask AI, which is the inline turn |</span><span class="dl a">+| `Enter` | splits the block at the caret. `shift+Enter` is a line break inside one |</span><span class="dl a">+| `Escape` | leaves the text and picks the block. Then arrows move, `Enter` enters, `Backspace` deletes |</span><span class="dl a">+| `mod+k` | ask, anchored wherever you are |</span><span class="dl a">+| `mod+j` | the helper margin |</span><span class="dl a">+| `mod+b`, `mod+i`, `mod+e` | the three marks, applied to the markdown rather than to the HTML |</span><span class="dl a">+| `mod+enter` | run this cell. `mod+shift+enter` runs the document in dependency order |</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+![The gutter, on hover](screenshots/canvas-gutter.png)</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+![The block menu](screenshots/canvas-blockmenu.png)</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+![The block menu on `/`, filtered as you type](screenshots/canvas-slash.png)</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+![The format bar, with the helper in it](screenshots/canvas-format.png)</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Both themes, and every embedded component follows the one the document is in.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+![The same document in the dark](screenshots/canvas-dark.png)</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The editor writes marks to the file, never to the rendered HTML. `document.execCommand(&#x27;bold&#x27;)`</span><span class="dl a">+would put in a `&lt;b&gt;` that the markdown writer then has to guess about.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The type scale, the token names and the popover shape follow BlockSuite&#x27;s. A canvas beside an</span><span class="dl a">+editor built on BlockSuite therefore reads as the same application. Both themes sit in</span><span class="dl a">+`canvas.css`, and `test_canvas.py` asserts the dark half names no token the light half lacks.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Modes</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`mode: make` and `mode: learn` in the frontmatter. The substrate is the same. The palette and the</span><span class="dl a">+default bricks differ. `a-sales-funnel`, `the-traditional-day`, `tunnelling` and `an-animal-cell` use</span><span class="dl a">+learn. `pricing-a-run` and `making-a-block` use make.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Nothing in the runtime branches on the mode. It is a label on the document and a filter on the</span><span class="dl a">+palette.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Running it</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`leela/blocks/__init__.py` connects the block, which serves `/canvas` from the IDE app. It also</span><span class="dl a">+runs on its own, with no kernels, no agent and no workspace:</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```sh</span><span class="dl a">+uv run python tools/canvas_spike.py # http://localhost:5002/canvas</span><span class="dl a">+BRICK_HOST=http://127.0.0.1:5001 uv run python tools/canvas_spike.py</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The components come from a component host on `BRICK_HOST`. Without one, the palette is empty, and</span><span class="dl a">+a brick already in a document draws with the sample data its package declares.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The canvas serves its own bundle from `/canvas/js` rather than joining the three IDE bundles.</span><span class="dl a">+Those three share one lexical scope, which a separate document has no reason to enter.</span><span class="dl a">+`build_ide_js.OWN_BUNDLE` names the blocks that serve their own bundle.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Walkthroughs</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Recorded against this branch, with the scripted helper and a component host on 5001.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+| what it shows | file |</span><span class="dl a">+|---|---|</span><span class="dl a">+| dragging a funnel bar rewrites every number under it | [`media/canvas/canvas-reactive.webm`](../media/canvas/canvas-reactive.webm) |</span><span class="dl a">+| clicking an organelle, an inline rewrite, an ask and a steer | [`media/canvas/canvas-helper.webm`](../media/canvas/canvas-helper.webm) |</span><span class="dl a">+| slash menu to palette to a component wired from its package | [`media/canvas/canvas-wiring.webm`](../media/canvas/canvas-wiring.webm) |</span><span class="dl a">+| the barrier sliders driving the simulation and the sentence under it | [`media/canvas/canvas-learn.webm`](../media/canvas/canvas-learn.webm) |</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## The six shipped canvases</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+| canvas | mode | what it exercises |</span><span class="dl a">+|---|---|---|</span><span class="dl a">+| [a-sales-funnel](../examples/canvas/a-sales-funnel.canvas.md) | learn | a component as an input, and prose bound to what it writes |</span><span class="dl a">+| [the-traditional-day](../examples/canvas/the-traditional-day.canvas.md) | learn | three components off one data source, wired over the host |</span><span class="dl a">+| [tunnelling](../examples/canvas/tunnelling.canvas.md) | learn | a sketch driving a simulation, and a video |</span><span class="dl a">+| [an-animal-cell](../examples/canvas/an-animal-cell.canvas.md) | learn | click-to-name, an accumulating list, a check |</span><span class="dl a">+| [pricing-a-run](../examples/canvas/pricing-a-run.canvas.md) | make | a table you pick a row from, and a slider that repeats the sum |</span><span class="dl a">+| [making-a-block](../examples/canvas/making-a-block.canvas.md) | make | a function, its chart, and a component sketched in the file |</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+![The whole of the panchangam canvas](screenshots/canvas-the-traditional-day.png)</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A PDF, a sketch and a chart in the same document.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+![A PDF open in a canvas](screenshots/canvas-pdf.png)</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## What the spike does not do</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+- The runtime is `exec` in the web process, not a kunda kernel. Ordering, staleness and error shape</span><span class="dl a">+ are the real ones. Isolation, interrupt and restart are not there.</span><span class="dl a">+- There is no undo. `apply_op` is the single write path a history would hook, and nothing hooks it.</span><span class="dl a">+- Prose editing round-trips through `cvHtmlToMd`, which handles what `cvMd` can produce and no more.</span><span class="dl a">+ `mod+e` shows the markdown for a block where that is not enough.</span><span class="dl a">+- A canvas is a page, not a tab. Opening one inside the IDE means a tab kind, a mount, and a place</span><span class="dl a">+ in the command palette.</span><span class="dl a">+- `Agentic` has never run.</span><span class="dl a">+- Block selection takes one block at a time. Dragging a range across many blocks is not there.</span><span class="dl a">+- The markdown writer handles what the renderer can produce and no more. `mod+e` shows the source</span><span class="dl a">+ for a block where that is not enough.</span></div></div></div></details><details><summary>docs/change.canvas.md +354 -0</summary><div class="in"><div class="diff"><div class="body"><span class="dl h">@@ -0,0 +1,354 @@</span><span class="dl a">+---</span><span class="dl a">+title: The canvas document: a goal, its plan and its changes in one file</span><span class="dl a">+---</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+# What this is</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A goal like &quot;increase procurement productivity by 10%&quot; is not one kind of work. You frame the</span><span class="dl a">+measure. You collect what people already know. You pull an extract apart. You prototype one rule.</span><span class="dl a">+You write the recommendation.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Today each of those lives in a different tool. The plan is in a tracker. The numbers are in a</span><span class="dl a">+notebook. The research is in browser tabs. The recommendation is in a deck. Nothing crosses</span><span class="dl a">+between them except a person who remembers all four.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+One file now holds every one of the four. It is a markdown file. Prose stays prose, and each</span><span class="dl a">+other part is a brick.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas goal id=g measure=&quot;tools you open to review one change against its goal&quot; baseline=&quot;4: tracker, notebook, diff, deck&quot; target=&quot;1 page&quot; by=2026-10-31--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+Give Leela one document that holds a goal, its plan, its research, its code and its questions.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas bundle id=canvas title=&quot;The canvas block: the document, the basket, and three views&quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ goal=g</span><span class="dl a">+ contributes=&quot;all of the review step; none of the run step, which the canvas branch owns&quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ covers=&quot;Words,Why it helps,The file,The basket,The wiring,The change,The value,The prompts,This page,The numbers,Checks&quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ paths=leela/blocks/canvas/*,tools/make_change_page.py,tests/test_canvas_doc.py,docs/*.md,media/*,leela/blocks/__init__.py,tests/routes.txt</span><span class="dl a">+ refs=doc:docs/dynamic-documents.md,file:leela/blocks/nb/nb.py,pkg:mdhtml--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+Adds `leela/blocks/canvas`, a block that reads and writes the canvas document. A question in the</span><span class="dl a">+document names what the model may read. A boundary on the canvas is one change. A change names the</span><span class="dl a">+goal that it serves.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas task id=t1 status=done owner=me--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+Read the document format from the canvas branch.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas task id=t2 status=done owner=me--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+Build the context basket, the change bundle, the review and the value view.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas task id=t3 status=done owner=me--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+Write this page from the document, with the code it explains.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas task id=t4 status=done owner=me--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+Move the modules into `leela/blocks/canvas/`.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+# Words</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Read this table first. Every later section uses these words and no others.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+| word | means |</span><span class="dl a">+|---|---|</span><span class="dl a">+| **brick** | one part of the document. A fence or a comment wrap. A code cell, a question, a goal, a task, a clipping. |</span><span class="dl a">+| **prose** | ordinary markdown between bricks. It needs no markup of its own. |</span><span class="dl a">+| **region** | the bricks under one heading. The headings make the regions, so nobody writes one. |</span><span class="dl a">+| **basket** | the exact list of bricks that one question sends to the model. |</span><span class="dl a">+| **scope** | how a question gathers its first set of bricks. `page`, `region`, `upstream`, `doc` or `none`. |</span><span class="dl a">+| **pin** | a brick a question always reads, whatever the scope says. A `mute` is the opposite. |</span><span class="dl a">+| **budget** | how many characters a question may send. The goal and the pins survive it. |</span><span class="dl a">+| **upstream** | the bricks a brick reads from. Read off the code, never drawn by hand. |</span><span class="dl a">+| **bundle** | one unit of change. It claims a region, names a goal, and owns a list of files. |</span><span class="dl a">+| **snippet** | a brick that cites code out of a file. It holds no copy of that code. |</span><span class="dl a">+| **canvas** | the second view of the document. The same bricks, with coordinates. |</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The block is `canvas` and the file is `*.canvas.md`. An earlier draft of this work was a separate</span><span class="dl a">+package called `pata`, from the Sanskrit `pata`, the cloth a painter paints a scroll on. That</span><span class="dl a">+name is gone, and `canvas` is the only name now.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+# Why it helps</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A notebook picks context by position: every cell above the question. That is right for a script,</span><span class="dl a">+where the cells above are the steps you took. A plan holds four lines of work at once. Position therefore hands the recommendation question</span><span class="dl a">+three failed attempts at a groupby. The alternative is to turn it off and paste the same</span><span class="dl a">+paragraphs again.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+An audit shows the limit. It belongs to the question near the top of the document and to the risk</span><span class="dl a">+question near the bottom, and to nothing between them. Where a brick sits says nothing about which</span><span class="dl a">+questions it answers.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A document that can say it gives three things.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A question shows its basket before it runs: each brick, why it is there, and what it costs. Mute</span><span class="dl a">+one and the count drops.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A boundary on the canvas is a change you can review. It names the goal, owns the files, and holds</span><span class="dl a">+the tasks, the prose and the code together. One page therefore answers whether the change does</span><span class="dl a">+what the goal said.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A goal shows what serves it, and shows a goal that nothing serves. The second is the worse finding,</span><span class="dl a">+because it looks like a goal that is going well.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+# The file</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A `pata` document is one markdown file. Prose stays prose. Each other part is a brick. A brick is</span><span class="dl a">+a fence or a comment wrap.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The reader reads the file line by line. It does not use one pattern on the whole file. This is</span><span class="dl a">+necessary. A document about canvases shows fences as examples. A fence inside a longer fence is an</span><span class="dl a">+example. It is not a brick.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas snippet id=s-scan path=leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py symbol=_scan</span><span class="dl a">+The `TICKS` branch does the work. It sees a plain fence, puts the fence into the prose, and skips</span><span class="dl a">+to the end of it. Nothing inside that fence becomes a brick. This page is such a document, and it</span><span class="dl a">+reads correctly.</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Headings are the regions of the document. Nobody writes a region. The reader gives each brick the</span><span class="dl a">+heading above it.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas snippet id=s-regions path=leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py symbol=Doc._regions</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+# The basket</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Each question carries a rule. The rule says what the question may read. `resolve` turns the rule</span><span class="dl a">+into the exact list that the turn will send.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The list is the point. `resolve` gives back items, not one string. The same list draws the panel</span><span class="dl a">+and builds the prompt. What a person sees is what the model gets.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas snippet id=s-resolve path=leela/blocks/canvas/context.py symbol=resolve</span><span class="dl a">+Four rules, in order. The goal goes in first. Then each pin. A pin that no longer exists becomes a</span><span class="dl a">+`missing` item. It is visible. A silent drop is worse, because the person still believes the pin is</span><span class="dl a">+there.</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A scope gives the first set of bricks. `page` is the notebook rule. `region` is the section that</span><span class="dl a">+you work in. `upstream` is what the question reads from.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas snippet id=s-members path=leela/blocks/canvas/context.py symbol=members</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The budget cuts the list. Two rules must hold. The goal and the pins stay. A pin that is larger</span><span class="dl a">+than the whole budget gets shorter; it does not go.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas snippet id=s-fit path=leela/blocks/canvas/context.py symbol=_fit</span><span class="dl a">+The last block is the one that matters. If every item that is left is pinned, the code cuts each</span><span class="dl a">+item to a share of the budget and marks it. It never drops a pin.</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The markup is `&lt;cell&gt;` with a `compact` attribute. This is Leela&#x27;s own notebook shape, and the</span><span class="dl a">+choice is deliberate. Ramabana drops `&lt;cell&gt;` elements when a prompt is too large for the window.</span><span class="dl a">+A document that wrote `&lt;block&gt;` would lose that net.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas snippet id=s-render path=leela/blocks/canvas/context.py symbol=render</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+# The wiring</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`upstream` reads the code. It does not read a diagram. A name belongs to the brick that binds it.</span><span class="dl a">+A diagram beside the code goes wrong; the code does not.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas snippet id=s-defs path=leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py symbol=defs_of</span><span class="dl a">+`defs_of` finds each name that a cell binds at the top level of its code. It looks inside `if`,</span><span class="dl a">+`for`, `try` and `with`. It does not look inside a `def`, because a name in a function belongs to</span><span class="dl a">+the function.</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Three additions reach where the code cannot see.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A question anchors on the brick above it. &quot;Fix that&quot; means that brick and all that it reads.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A name in backticks is a name that the question reads. Write `` `triage` `` and the brick that</span><span class="dl a">+defines `triage` goes in.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`supports=`, `refutes=` and `blocks=` state a relation between two bricks. No code states these.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas snippet id=s-upstream path=leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py symbol=upstream</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+# The change</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A region groups bricks to read. A `bundle` brick claims its region as one change. The boundary on</span><span class="dl a">+the canvas is then the thing that a reviewer opens.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The files come from the code first. A code brick with `#|export` writes a module. Leela therefore knows the module</span><span class="dl a">+path. `paths=` adds only what the bricks do not write.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas snippet id=s-paths path=leela/blocks/canvas/change.py symbol=Bundle.paths</span><span class="dl a">+A list that a person keeps by hand goes out of date. A claim that is out of date is worse than no</span><span class="dl a">+claim, because a reviewer trusts it.</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`coverage` holds the claim against the diff. It reports three things. Two of them are new.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`matched` is a file that the bundle claims and the diff changed. `unmet` is a file that the bundle</span><span class="dl a">+claims and the diff did not change. `unclaimed` is a file that the diff changed and no bundle</span><span class="dl a">+explains.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas snippet id=s-coverage path=leela/blocks/canvas/change.py symbol=coverage</span><span class="dl a">+No diff tool can find `unclaimed`. Only the document knows what the change had to be.</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`pr` cuts a pull request from one change. It gives back the title, the branch, the body, the files</span><span class="dl a">+and the attachments. It opens nothing. Git belongs to `gheasy`. The forge belongs to `pullup`.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas snippet id=s-pr path=leela/blocks/canvas/change.py symbol=pr</span><span class="dl a">+The `_reasoning` line is the part that a diff never has. Each question inside the change, with the</span><span class="dl a">+answer that it got, goes into the body in a fold.</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+# The value</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`state` comes from the document. No person sets it. There is no key here. The prose above each</span><span class="dl a">+snippet came from the session that wrote the code, under the same prompt. `capture` wrote the</span><span class="dl a">+prompts out and `replay` would put a model&#x27;s answers back.</span></div></div></div></details><details><summary>docs/dynamic-documents.md +200 -0</summary><div class="in"><div class="diff"><div class="body"><span class="dl h">@@ -0,0 +1,200 @@</span><span class="dl a">+# Dynamic documents</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A goal like &quot;increase procurement productivity by 10%&quot; is neither a coding task nor a writing task. Reaching it takes five steps. Frame the measure. Collect what the team already knows. Pull an extract apart until the numbers say something. Prototype the one rule that might work. Write the recommendation. Today those five steps live in five tools. The notebook holds the extract. The deck holds the recommendation. The research sits in tabs, and the plan sits in a tracker. Only a person carries context between them.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Leela already holds four of the five. It has the kernel, the files, the vault, the agent and the notebook. It lacks a document that follows the work rather than a script.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Two branches have gone at that. `claude/dynamic-document-canvas-ohgfud` built the file and the runtime, wired into Leela as a block. `leela/blocks/canvas` builds the context engine on that file. This document is the design both halves answer to.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## What a flat list cannot be</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Every notebook is one flat list. Its prompt cells read from the top of the document down to the cell being asked, which `Notebook.context` does in `leela/blocks/nb/nb.py`. The list works because it is the order the work happened in. Every cell above yours is work you did before, and the model should probably know it.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+That rule dies the moment the document holds more than one line of work. Framing the goal, reading the audit, cleaning the extract and drafting the recommendation are four strands, not four consecutive steps. Ask the recommendation prompt to read everything above it and it reads three failed attempts at a groupby. Ask it to read nothing and you are pasting again.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The audit is the case that makes it concrete. It belongs in the context of the synthesis question near the top, and in the context of the risk question near the bottom, and in nothing between them. Position cannot express that. Nothing about where a brick sits says which questions it answers.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## The file</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`*.canvas.md`. Prose is prose. A brick markdown cannot show is a fence, `` ```canvas code id=c1 ``. A brick whose body is markdown a plain renderer should still show is a comment wrap, `&lt;!--canvas goal id=goal--&gt;`. Headings are the document&#x27;s regions. Frontmatter carries the title.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+This is the canvas branch&#x27;s format. A plan, a design doc and a set of research clippings are prose, and nobody reads or reviews prose held in JSON. Markdown gives three things. `git diff` shows the argument changing rather than a re-serialised tree. The document opens in any reader. The design doc and the code that tests it stay in one file.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Reading it works line by line rather than by one regex over the file. A canvas fence inside a longer markdown fence is an example of a brick and not a brick. A document about canvases therefore parses as a document. This rule matters, because a `source` brick holding a clipped page is where quoted markup arrives.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## What AFFiNE contributes</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+AFFiNE&#x27;s [BlockSuite](https://blocksuite.io) puts one block tree behind two views. A document is a list of blocks, each with a flavour named `namespace:name`. Page mode reads the tree top to bottom. Edgeless mode reads the same blocks off a surface that gives them coordinates, frames that group them, and connectors that join them. Neither view owns the document.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Two of those ideas belong here, and the code replaces the third.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The named kind belongs. A notebook cell has three types, because a notebook holds three kinds of thing. A document that holds a goal, a task, a clipping and a chart needs a name for each. A `goal` brick carries `measure`, `baseline`, `target` and `by`, which holds a measure better than a markdown cell and a convention.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The two views belong. The list is the right way to read finished work, and the only way to review it. The canvas suits work in progress, because unfinished thinking is not linear. `prop x` and `prop y` are the only trace the canvas leaves in the file. A document nobody has laid out is therefore still complete, and `arrange` places an unopened document on a canvas.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The connector does not belong. On AFFiNE&#x27;s canvas a person draws a connector by hand, and a diagram kept beside the code goes wrong. The code already states the graph.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Upstream is read off the code</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`defs_of` and `reads_of` walk the AST. Whichever brick binds a name owns it. Which bricks a brick reads from is therefore a fact about the document rather than a drawing over it. `order` runs code in dependency order, and `upstream` answers what one question is downstream of.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Three things extend it where the AST cannot see.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A question anchors on the brick above it. &quot;Fix that&quot; means that brick and everything it reads, which is what a person means and what `scope=upstream` on a question should give them. `anchor=&lt;id&gt;` overrides it.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A name a question puts in backticks is a name it reads. Writing `` `triage` `` in a question pulls in the brick that defines `triage` and its own upstream. Backticks around an identifier already mean &quot;this one&quot;, and nobody has to learn a new rule.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`supports=`, `refutes=` and `blocks=` name a relation between bricks that no AST can find. That is where a clipping supporting a claim goes, and it is the only hand-drawn edge left.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Context is the design</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Every question carries a rule, and `canvas.context.resolve` turns that rule into the exact list of items the turn will send.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+scope=region none | page | region | upstream | doc</span><span class="dl a">+pin s-audit always in; also file:, vault:, url:, var:, sel:</span><span class="dl a">+mute n-cap always out</span><span class="dl a">+budget=12000 characters</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`page` is the notebook&#x27;s own behaviour, kept because it is right for a document being read as a document. `region` is the section you are working in. `upstream` is the dataflow. The risk question therefore reads the backtest, the rule, the split and the extract. It reads none of the four tasks sitting beside them.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`resolve` is pure, and it returns items rather than a string. One list builds the prompt and draws the panel. The panel shows every brick in the basket, what put it there, what it costs in characters, and a running total against the budget. Bricks in the basket glow on the canvas. Click a row to mute it, and the glow goes out. The panel therefore shows exactly what the model gets.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Under a budget, the goal and the pins survive. A `context=discard` brick goes first, then the oldest ordinary one, which is what notebook cells already do through `context_mode`. `resolve` clips and marks a pin larger than the whole budget rather than dropping it. A pin that vanishes silently costs a reader more than one that arrives short.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`render` emits `&lt;cell id= type= compact= why= region=&gt;`. That is Leela&#x27;s own notebook markup, chosen on purpose. Ramabana&#x27;s `compact_notebook_context` sheds elements matching exactly that pattern when a prompt overflows the window. A document that rendered anything else would carry a budget with nothing underneath it. An oversized turn would then fail at the provider rather than shed a research clipping.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## No stored outputs</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A canvas keeps no outputs. Opening one runs it, and a code brick&#x27;s value comes from the live namespace.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+That deletes the whole staleness problem rather than solving it. There is no hash to compare, no `output_hash` to carry, and no case where a chart is correct about a dataframe somebody has since reloaded. It also deletes the merge conflicts that notebook outputs cause, which is most of them.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+It costs two things: a document that does not open instantly, and one nobody can read offline with its numbers in it. `bind` answers the second cost. A `data` brick renders a sentence from live values, and the prose therefore never carries last month&#x27;s numbers.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## A boundary that is a unit of change</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A region groups bricks for reading. A `bundle` brick claims its region as one change, and that is the difference between a Miro frame and something worth having. The boundary names a goal, owns a set of files, holds the tasks and the prose and the code together, and is the thing a reviewer opens.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Four parts, and the last one is the point.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`goal=&lt;id&gt;` is the value link. A change serves a goal, and the goal carries a measure and a target. `contributes=` says in words what this change is worth against that target. Leela invents no arithmetic. A share of a ten-point target is a judgement, and pretending otherwise would put a fake number in a pull request.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The files come from the code. A code brick marked `#|export` writes a module. That module is the change, and `modules()` already knows the path. `paths=` adds what the bricks do not generate: tests, config, a migration. Deriving first matters because a list maintained by hand is a list that goes stale, and a stale claim is worse than no claim.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`refs=` attaches packages, files and other documents for review. It uses the same `pkg:`, `file:`, `doc:` vocabulary as a context pin. Attaching something for a human reviewer therefore also puts it within the model&#x27;s reach. One vocabulary, two readers.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`coverage(doc, changed)` holds the claim against the diff, which turns the boundary into a check. Per bundle it reports `matched` and `unmet`, a claimed file the diff never touched. Across the document it reports `unclaimed`, a changed file no bundle explains. No diff tool can produce `unclaimed`, because only the document knows what the change promised to do.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## The value view</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`value(doc, changed)` is the third document. It lists every goal, and every change serving it, each with its state and a line on how much of it has finished.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Leela derives the state. A change reaches `blocked` when one of its tasks blocks. It reaches `done` when every task reaches `done` and every claimed file moved. It reaches `doing` when some of either has. Nobody sets these as a field, because a status somebody must remember goes stale. One case needs care. An absent diff is no evidence about files, and it must not read as evidence against them. Otherwise a finished change reports as untouched work whenever you ask without a diff.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The view exists for two findings, and neither appears anywhere else in the document.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A change serving no goal appears under `Serving no goal`. Somebody is doing work that nothing in the plan asked for.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A goal nothing serves says so under its own heading. A goal with no change against it reads the same as a goal on track, until the date arrives.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The tally at the end lists every change by state, and every changed file no bundle claims. The question below it pins every goal.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Review is another canvas</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`review(doc, bundle_id, diff)` builds a document: the goal, what the change contributes, the prose, the tasks, the questions asked inside the change with their recorded answers, one `diff` brick per file, the attachments, the coverage checks, and a question with the goal already pinned.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+It is a `Doc`. It therefore draws in both views through the same renderer, keeps the outline, and keeps the context basket. Nothing about the review view is a second implementation of anything, and a question asked inside a review has the whole change in scope.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+That also answers whether this replaces Leela&#x27;s git view. It does not. The existing view is for line-level work: staging, hunks, blame, conflicts. This is for the question a diff cannot answer, which is whether the change does what the goal said. `canvas.change.hunks` takes unified diff text. Whatever produces the diff, `gheasy` included, can feed it.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Leela builds a review per request and never writes it back. A diff is a fact about a commit range, not part of the document.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## The literate page</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`lit` writes one document as one column for a phone. `paint` draws a canvas for someone working in it; this draws the same document for someone reading it on the way to a meeting. No JavaScript, no other requests, both colour schemes, and everything long folded.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Writing this repository&#x27;s own change as a canvas document, and rendering it with `lit`, found four things the design was missing. That is the argument for dogfooding rather than a claim about the tool.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A `snippet` brick cites code instead of holding it. `snip` reads the file the brick names and finds the symbol in it, decorators included. A literate page wants the function that does the work rather than the whole diff. A copy pasted into prose goes stale. The whole page rests on this primitive, and nothing before it could do the job.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A comment wrap had to fit on one line. A bundle carries a goal, a contribution, a covers list, a paths list and a refs list. One line therefore ran 300 characters wide in a file a person edits. The reader now joins lines until it finds `--&gt;`.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Two headings with only prose between them became one region. Prose accumulates into one text brick, and the reader took only its first heading. The second heading never started a section. The reader now splits prose at every heading, skipping headings inside a plain fence.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A heading and the prose under it are one brick, and the page renderer took the heading as a section title and dropped the brick. Every paragraph under a first-level heading disappeared. It now trims the heading and keeps the rest.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`review` also changed. It now places the prose that cites a path next to that file&#x27;s hunks. A document that explains its files therefore produces a literate diff with no further work, which is what the exercise was for.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`tools/make_change_page.py` builds the page. `docs/change.canvas.md` is the source, and `media/canvas-change.html` is the output. `--prompts FILE` writes the drafting prompts and stops; `--answers FILE` puts a model&#x27;s answers back.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Where the prompts live</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`lit` draws and `explain` writes. Three places hold the three parts, and the split is the point.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The register lives in ramabana. `write_docs` is a pyskill, and `rule_text` reads it through `shalya.skills.discover`. `CLAUDE.md` says no repository holds a copy of a writing skill, and a prompt with one pasted into it is that copy. `rule_text` therefore raises when the skill is missing rather than falling back. A silent fallback puts the wrong register on the page, and nobody notices.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The task lives in the package. `explain.md` is the template and `ste.md` states the ASD-STE100 limits for this output. Neither restates `write_docs`. `ste.md` is nine lines, and every one of them is an output constraint rather than a rule about English.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The prose lives in the document. `explain` writes each answer into the brick body and marks it `wrote=ai`. A drafted sentence is therefore in `git diff`, a reviewer can see which sentences a model wrote, and editing one is editing the document. `explain` leaves a brick that already has a body alone, because a sentence a person wrote is the one worth keeping.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The prompt&#x27;s context comes from `resolve`, which is the same basket a question in the document would send. Nothing in `canvas` imports a model. Leela therefore opens it, and the prompts are still prompts. `from_ipynb` reads it back and migrates a notebook that was never a document. `to_report` writes the document with the canvas taken off. `modules` writes the code bricks marked `#|export` in dependency order, which is the &quot;extract the software&quot; half of the goal.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## The prototypes</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The package generates both, and nobody draws them by hand. They therefore show what `resolve` and `arrange` actually do.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+- `media/canvas-session.html` and `media/canvas-change.html` are the literate pages, written by the block itself from `docs/session.canvas.md` and `docs/change.canvas.md`. The prototype that drew the first mockups of both views is gone, and so are its two pages.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+Both carry three documents behind one toggle: the document, the review of one change, and the value view. `page` and `canvas` switch how the loaded document draws.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`leela/blocks/canvas/procurement.canvas.md` is the document itself, and a reader should read it as a file.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## Where the two branches meet</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The canvas branch owns the format, the parser, the dataflow, the reactive runtime and the embedded components. Merging leaves one parser in whichever half survives, and the other half imports it.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The canvas branch has two things this does not. A brick body keeps its</span><span class="dl a">+final newline, because the format keeps code exactly.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+**What the browser half draws.** `leela/blocks/canvas/*.js` draws it, built into</span><span class="dl a">+`leela/static/lee-canvas.js` and served from `/canvas/js`. Whether the agent may also add bricks, rebind ports</span><span class="dl a">+and reorganise a document is a larger claim.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+## What integration costs</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A review of the standalone design against the repository found the seam work, and none of it is one line. The canvas branch has done some of it already.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`Assistant.compose` in Ramabana wraps any context in `&lt;notebook path=...&gt;`, and the briefing tells the model to call `notebook_cells` on that path. It writes no script, so the fold is</span><span class="dl a">+`&lt;details&gt;` and the page works with JavaScript turned off.</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+# The prompts</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas bundle id=u-pr title=&quot;Drafting the prose the reviewer reads&quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ goal=g</span><span class="dl a">+ contributes=&quot;the words on this page&quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ covers=&quot;The prompts,t5&quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ paths=leela/blocks/canvas/explain.py,leela/blocks/canvas/explain.md,leela/blocks/canvas/ste.md</span><span class="dl a">+ refs=pkg:ramabana,pkg:shalya--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+Leela drafts from two files, and no third. `explain.md` holds the task and `ste.md` holds the English.</span><span class="dl a">+`rule_text` reads the writing rules from ramabana&#x27;s `write_docs` pyskill at the time of the call,</span><span class="dl a">+so this repository keeps no copy of them.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas source id=src-rules url=pyskill:write_docs title=&quot;ramabana write_docs&quot;--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+The voiceless GDS register, the banned words, no hedging, no restatement. When the skill is missing, `rule_text` raises</span><span class="dl a">+rather than falling back to a stale copy.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas snippet id=s-rules path=leela/blocks/canvas/explain.py symbol=rule_text</span><span class="dl a">+`rule_text` reads the writing rules from where ramabana installed them. A missing skill raises rather than</span><span class="dl a">+falling back, because a silent fallback would draft prose against stale rules.</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+A brick the model drafted carries `wrote=ai` in the file. `git diff` therefore shows the drafting,</span><span class="dl a">+and a reviewer can read those bricks first. A person wrote every snippet on this page, and no</span><span class="dl a">+brick here carries the mark.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+# The library</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas bundle id=u-brk title=&quot;A component comes from an installed library&quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ goal=g</span><span class="dl a">+ contributes=&quot;the palette, with no second process&quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ covers=&quot;The library,t6,t7,t11&quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ paths=leela/blocks/canvas/bricks.py,extensions/bricks/*,tests/fixtures/*,docs/bricks.md</span><span class="dl a">+ refs=pkg:leela-bricks,doc:docs/bricks.md--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+The palette used to be an HTTP call to a second server. It is now an entry-point group. A library</span><span class="dl a">+answers four questions: its manifest, one brick, that brick&#x27;s wiring, and its own routes. An HTTP</span><span class="dl a">+host answers the same four, and it stays for a library nobody installed.</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--/canvas--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+The four questions are the whole contract. A library that answers them needs to know nothing about</span><span class="dl a">+Leela, and Leela needs to know nothing about the library.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas snippet id=s-lib path=leela/blocks/canvas/bricks.py symbol=Library</span><span class="dl a">+A library answers four questions and knows nothing about Leela. `manifest` lists its components,</span><span class="dl a">+`find` returns one, `wire` returns the code that fills its ports, and `mount` puts its own routes</span><span class="dl a">+on the app it is handed. `manifest` is read in process, so the palette needs no second server.</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+`needs` comes from the wiring&#x27;s own imports. A component cannot claim a dependency its code does</span><span class="dl a">+not import, and cannot hide one it does.</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+```canvas snippet id=s-needs path=extensions/bricks/leela_bricks/bricks.py symbol=needs</span><span class="dl a">+`needs` reads the imports out of the wiring text. A component cannot claim a dependency its code</span><span class="dl a">+does not import, and cannot hide one it does. The standard library is dropped, so the list is what</span><span class="dl a">+a person must install before the cell will run.</span><span class="dl a">+```</span><span class="dl a">+</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;!--canvas note id=n-src--&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+A library never writes its own name into a `src` string. `LIB` comes from `__name__`.
