named = {p.resolve() for p in modules()}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl r&quot;&gt;- found = {p.resolve() for p in (*(PKG/&amp;#x27;static&amp;#x27;/&amp;#x27;js&amp;#x27;).glob(&amp;#x27;*.js&amp;#x27;), *PKG.glob(&amp;#x27;blocks/*/*.js&amp;#x27;))}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ found = {p.resolve() for p in (*(PKG/&amp;#x27;static&amp;#x27;/&amp;#x27;js&amp;#x27;).glob(&amp;#x27;*.js&amp;#x27;), *PKG.glob(&amp;#x27;blocks/*/*.js&amp;#x27;))&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if p.parent.name not in OWN_BUNDLE}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; return sorted(found - named)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; def build(check=False):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; if gone := missing(): raise SystemExit(f&amp;#x27;named but absent: {[p.name for p in gone]}&amp;#x27;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; if extra := orphans(): raise SystemExit(f&amp;#x27;present but unnamed: {[str(p.relative_to(PKG)) for p in extra]}&amp;#x27;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl r&quot;&gt;- for name in LAYERS:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl r&quot;&gt;- text, out = bundle(name), OUTDIR/name&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ plan = [(name, bundle(name), OUTDIR/name) for name in LAYERS]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ plan += [(own_out(b).name, own_bundle(b), own_out(b)) for b in OWN_BUNDLE]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ for name, text, out in plan:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; if check:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; if not out.is_file(): raise SystemExit(f&amp;#x27;{name} has never been built&amp;#x27;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; if out.read_text() != text: raise SystemExit(f&amp;#x27;{name} is stale; run python tools/build_ide_js.py&amp;#x27;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; else: out.write_text(text)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl r&quot;&gt;- n = len(modules())&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ n = len(modules()) + sum(len(own_order(b)) for b in OWN_BUNDLE)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; verb = &amp;#x27;match&amp;#x27; if check else &amp;#x27;built from&amp;#x27;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl r&quot;&gt;- print(f&amp;#x27;{len(LAYERS)} bundle(s) {verb} {n} modules: &amp;#x27; +&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl r&quot;&gt;- &amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;.join(f&amp;#x27;{k} ({len(v)})&amp;#x27; for k, v in LAYERS.items()))&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ print(f&amp;#x27;{len(plan)} bundle(s) {verb} {n} modules: &amp;#x27; +&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ &amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;.join(f&amp;#x27;{k} ({len(v)})&amp;#x27; for k, v in LAYERS.items()) +&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ &amp;#x27;&amp;#x27;.join(f&amp;#x27;, {own_out(b).name} ({len(own_order(b))})&amp;#x27; for b in OWN_BUNDLE))&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; if __name__ == &amp;#x27;__main__&amp;#x27;: build(check=&amp;#x27;--check&amp;#x27; in sys.argv)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/details&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;card note&quot;&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;OWN_BUNDLE&lt;/code&gt; names the blocks that serve their own page. The build writes and commits each one, like</span><span class="dl a">+the IDE&#x27;s three. The order comes from that block&#x27;s own &lt;code&gt;ui.FILES&lt;/code&gt;, written down once.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;/div&gt;&lt;figure&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;diff&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;hd&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;p&quot;&gt;tools/canvas_spike.py&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip add&quot;&gt;+14&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip rm&quot;&gt;-0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;body&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl h&quot;&gt;@@ -0,0 +1,14 @@&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;quot;Boot the canvas block on its own: no kernels, no models, no workspace. `uv run python tools/canvas_spike.py`.&amp;quot;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+import os, sys&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+from pathlib import Path&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent.parent))&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+from fasthtml.common import fast_app, serve&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+from leela.blocks.canvas.app import connect&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+app, _ = fast_app(default_hdrs=False, pico=False, live=False)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+connect(app, ctx=None)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+if __name__ == &amp;#x27;__main__&amp;#x27;:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ serve(&amp;#x27;canvas_spike&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;app&amp;#x27;, port=int(os.getenv(&amp;#x27;PORT&amp;#x27;, 5002)), reload=False)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Attached&lt;/h3&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;figure&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;b&gt;pkg:shalya&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;card note&quot;&gt;&lt;p&gt;Every changed file is claimed and every task is done.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;card ask&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;q&quot;&gt;&lt;p&gt;Does this change do what the goal says, and what would you push back on?&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;h2 id=&quot;a-component-comes-from-an-installed-libr&quot;&gt;A component comes from an installed library&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;card goal&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;stmt&quot;&gt;Give Leela one document that holds a goal, its plan, its research, its code and its questions,</span><span class="dl a">+and one page that shows all five to a reviewer on a phone.&lt;/div&gt;&lt;dl&gt;&lt;dt&gt;measure&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;tools you open to review one branch&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;dt&gt;baseline&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;4: tracker, notebook, diff, deck&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;dt&gt;target&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;1 page&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;dt&gt;by&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;2026-10-31&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;/dl&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;card note&quot;&gt;&lt;p&gt;Contributes: the palette, with no second process&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;The palette used to be an HTTP call to a second server. It is an entry-point group now. A library</span><span class="dl a">+answers four questions. Its manifest, one brick, that brick&#x27;s wiring, and its own routes.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;h3&gt;Change&lt;/h3&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;details&gt;&lt;summary&gt;docs/bricks.md +104 -0&lt;/summary&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;in&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;diff&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;body&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl h&quot;&gt;@@ -0,0 +1,104 @@&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+# Bricks&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A `brick` in a canvas document embeds a component from a library. `src=leela_bricks:viz.series` says which library and which component. This is where a component comes from, and what a library has to be.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Read this with [dynamic-documents.md](dynamic-documents.md), which is what a brick sits in.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## Where a component comes from&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`leela/blocks/canvas/bricks.py` finds libraries three ways, in this order.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+An entry point under `leela.bricks`, which is how a pip-installed library publishes itself. `shalya` finds pyskills the same way, and the codebase therefore already uses this pattern.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A name in `KNOWN`, for a library that publishes no entry point. `lego.bricks` is the only one.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`LEELA_BRICK_HOST`, for a library nobody installed. It is empty by default. The earlier design defaulted it to `http://127.0.0.1:5001`, which is Leela&amp;#x27;s own port. A fresh install therefore fetched its palette from Leela, got nothing, and reported nothing.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A library is any module with `manifest()` and `find(name)`. There is no base class and nothing to register. `leela_bricks` satisfies it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## What Leela does with one&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`palette(libs)` merges every library&amp;#x27;s manifest and stamps each row with the library it came from. `locate(src)` returns the library and the brick. `wire(src)` returns the snippet that fills the brick&amp;#x27;s ports. `mount(app)` registers each library&amp;#x27;s own routes on Leela&amp;#x27;s app.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The library&amp;#x27;s `serve.py` takes `(app, page=None)`, and it opens with &amp;quot;Nothing here imports the application it is mounted in&amp;quot;. Leela&amp;#x27;s own process therefore serves the gallery, the component frame and the port data, on Leela&amp;#x27;s own port. No second server runs, and `LEELA_BRICK_HOST` serves only a library nobody installed.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`split_src` keeps the library prefix. The earlier code did `src.split(&amp;#x27;:&amp;#x27;)[-1]` and threw it away, which makes two libraries that each have a `viz.series` resolve to whichever answered first. Only the named library now answers a prefixed `src`. A bare name searches every library and takes the first, which is why a document should write the prefix.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## What was measured&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Eight files went into an empty package with a two-line `__init__.py`, and nothing else changed. The package imports on `fastcore` and `fasthtml` alone. Leela&amp;#x27;s resolver reads it as 10 bricks in 4 groups. `locate` finds ports and emits. `wire` returns the package&amp;#x27;s own snippet and its remote fallback. `mount` registers all seven routes on a `FastHTML` app. `data.fill(&amp;#x27;viz.series&amp;#x27;)` runs the snippet and returns real values.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The extraction is a packaging change rather than a redesign, and the code already sits on the right side of the line.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Two facts decide where the line goes.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`lego/__init__.py` is `from .app import *` and `lego/bricks/__init__.py` is `from .app import connect`. Either one is enough to make `import lego.bricks` boot lego&amp;#x27;s whole application. In this container it fails on `ujson`, one of lego&amp;#x27;s thirteen dependencies. Nothing under `lego/bricks/` other than `app.py` imports `lego`.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Four of the ten bricks carry wiring that imports a domain package. `panchanga.day`, `panchanga.horas` and `panchanga.wheel` import `lego.muhurtha.panchanga`. `thrifty.costs` imports `lego.thrifty.data`. The other six, every `viz.*` and every `learn.*`, ship no wiring at all. They are display components that read whatever the document already computed.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## What to extract&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Take the contract and the six domain-free bricks. Leave the four domain bricks with the packages their wiring needs.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| goes | is |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+|---|---|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `bricks.py` | `Port`, `Brick`, the registry, `manifest()`, `find()` |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `cfg.py` | the seven route paths |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `serve.py` | `connect(app, page=None)`, which imports nothing about the app |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `data.py` | `fill()` runs a brick&amp;#x27;s snippet here; `remote_wire()` is the call for a document that lacks the package |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `ui.py`, `bricks.js`, `bricks.css`, `frame.js` | the gallery, the frame, and the drawing keyed by brick name |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `viz.*`, `learn.*` | six bricks with no wiring and no domain dependency |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| stays | why |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+|---|---|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `app.py` | it is the upstream seam: `lego.core`, `RouteOverrides`, the upstream nav |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `panchanga.*`, `thrifty.*` | their wiring imports `lego.muhurtha` and `lego.thrifty` |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## The spec is now built&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`extensions/bricks` is the extracted package, `leela-bricks`. Eight files moved with no&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+edit. Only `bricks.py` changed, and it took all four changes below.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ uv pip install -e extensions/bricks&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+That is the whole install, and the entry point does the rest. `libraries()` finds&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`leela_bricks`, `palette()` reads ten components in four groups, and the notes list is empty.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`KNOWN` still names `lego.bricks` for a library that publishes no entry point, and an absent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+library produces no note.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The four domain bricks came too, and their wiring still imports `lego.muhurtha` and `lego.thrifty`.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`needs` exists for that case, and the palette therefore names the package a component wants before the cell runs.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| brick | needs |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+|---|---|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `panchanga.day`, `panchanga.horas`, `panchanga.wheel` | `lego.muhurtha.panchanga` |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `thrifty.costs` | `lego.thrifty.data` |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `viz.tiles`, `viz.series`, `viz.funnel` | nothing |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `learn.cell`, `learn.wavepacket`, `learn.orbit` | nothing |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## Four changes the extracted package needs&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+**Own the `src` prefix.** `Brick.src` was `f&amp;#x27;lego.bricks:{self.name}&amp;#x27;`, hardcoded. After extraction that string names a package that no longer holds the brick. `LIB = __name__.rsplit(&amp;#x27;.&amp;#x27;, 1)[0]` derives it. Renaming the package therefore updates every `src` it serves.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+**Give each library its own registry.** `BRICKS` is a module-global dict and `brick()` mutates it. That works while one package registers everything. It breaks as soon as a second library keeps its own bricks. That library would call `brick()` into the extracted package&amp;#x27;s global, and then every library&amp;#x27;s `manifest()` would return every library&amp;#x27;s bricks. The package exposes a `Registry` a library instantiates, with `manifest()` and `find()` reading its own. `manifest()` also returns `library`, which tells a caller which registry answered.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+**Publish the entry point.** `[project.entry-points.&amp;quot;leela.bricks&amp;quot;]` so Leela finds the library without `KNOWN`. `pip install` is the whole of procurement. `KNOWN` stays for a library that publishes none.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+**Say when a snippet needs a package.** A brick whose `wire` imports something should declare it. `data.fill` already catches the failure, and `remote_wire` is already the fallback. A document still discovers the missing package by running a cell and reading a traceback. The manifest row carries `needs`. A regex over the wiring&amp;#x27;s own `import` lines produces it, minus the standard library. A component cannot claim a dependency its code does not import, and cannot hide one it does.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## What Leela ships&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Leela includes no components of its own. A `sim` is a component the document itself defines, in JavaScript, with `root`, `props` and `emit` in scope. A `sim` needs no package, and Leela therefore stays fully usable with no library installed. The canvas skill states that you can move a `sim` into a package without changing a line.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Leela ships the resolver and the contract. A chart is not IDE behaviour. A bundled component library would become a compatibility surface, held forever on Leela&amp;#x27;s release clock rather than the library&amp;#x27;s. The same reason keeps `kunda`, `kavacha` and `pullup` out of this repository.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## What the merge connected&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`leela/blocks/canvas/app.py` now holds both halves. The palette route is the resolver, and the two&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+routes that fetched from a host have gone. `/canvas/palette` reads `palette(libs)`, and&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`/canvas/wire/{name}` reads the library. `_wire_from_host` keeps its name and reads the library&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+too, and it no longer drops the `src` prefix. Nothing in the block imports `urllib` any more.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`brick_host()` survives as the base for `remote_wire`. `remote_wire` is the snippet a document&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+runs when it holds the component but not the package that fills it. HTTP is the right answer in&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+that one case, and in no other.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/details&gt;&lt;figure&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;diff&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;hd&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;p&quot;&gt;extensions/bricks/.gitignore&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip add&quot;&gt;+1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip rm&quot;&gt;-0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;body&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl h&quot;&gt;@@ -0,0 +1 @@&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+__pycache__/&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;details&gt;&lt;summary&gt;extensions/bricks/README.md +57 -0&lt;/summary&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;in&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;diff&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;body&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl h&quot;&gt;@@ -0,0 +1,57 @@&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+# leela-bricks&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Components a canvas document can embed. Ten of them, in four groups.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A canvas document embeds one with a `brick` brick:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```markdown&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```canvas brick id=b1 src=leela_bricks:viz.series emit_point=point&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+bind labels = list(cycle.index)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+bind series = [{&amp;#x27;name&amp;#x27;: &amp;#x27;days to clear&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;values&amp;#x27;: list(cycle.values)}]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+prop height = 240&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## Install&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```sh&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+pip install -e extensions/bricks&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Leela finds it through the `leela.bricks` entry point. Leela needs no other configuration, and&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`LEELA_BRICK_HOST` serves only a library nobody installed. See&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+[docs/bricks.md](../../docs/bricks.md).&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## What a brick declares&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`Registry.brick(name, title, group, ports, emits, wire, height, doc)`. `ports` name what the component draws&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+from. `emits` name what a click writes back into the document&amp;#x27;s namespace. `wire` is the code&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+that fills the ports.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`wire` gives `needs`, and nobody declares it. `needs` is the top-level packages the snippet&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+imports, minus the standard library. Six of the ten need nothing. The four under `panchanga` and&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`thrifty` each import a domain package, and a document without that package reads its ports over&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`data.remote_wire` instead.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`src` is `LIB:name`, and `LIB` is this package&amp;#x27;s own module name. It is never a literal. A frozen desktop export would</span><span class="dl a">+have failed.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;/div&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Attached&lt;/h3&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;figure&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;b&gt;pkg:kunda&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;figure&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;b&gt;pkg:pullup&lt;/b&gt;&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;card note&quot;&gt;&lt;p&gt;Every changed file is claimed and every task is done.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;card ask&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;q&quot;&gt;&lt;p&gt;Does this change do what the goal says, and what would you push back on?&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;h2 id=&quot;what-the-suites-hold-and-what-running-th&quot;&gt;What the suites hold, and what running them found&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;card goal&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;stmt&quot;&gt;Leave nothing in this branch that a reviewer called critical or high.&lt;/div&gt;&lt;dl&gt;&lt;dt&gt;measure&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;findings from a review of this branch that are still open&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;dt&gt;baseline&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;17&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;dt&gt;target&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;0&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;dt&gt;by&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;2026-09-30&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;/dl&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;card note&quot;&gt;&lt;p&gt;Contributes: a suite that finishes&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;The kernel killed &lt;code&gt;pytest -m slow&lt;/code&gt; a third of the way in. It reported nothing. Not the tests it</span><span class="dl a">+could never run, and not the ones above them that pass in seconds. Two suites resolved a real local</span><span class="dl a">+model, because the machine happened to hold its bundle in the cache.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;ul class=&quot;tasks&quot;&gt;&lt;li class=&quot;done&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;box&quot;&gt;[x]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span&gt;Make `pytest -m slow` finish, and fix what running it found.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;who&quot;&gt;me&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;h3&gt;Change&lt;/h3&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;figure&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;diff&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;hd&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;p&quot;&gt;leela/blocks/agent/threads.py&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip add&quot;&gt;+4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip rm&quot;&gt;-1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;body&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl h&quot;&gt;@@ -416,7 +416,10 @@ class TurnRunner:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; with self._lock:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; for ident, r in list(self._pending.items()):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; worker = r.get(&amp;#x27;worker&amp;#x27;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl r&quot;&gt;- gone = worker is not None and not worker.is_alive()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ # `ident` is None until the thread runs. `start` publishes the pending turn before&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ # it starts the worker, so `is_alive` alone reaps the turn it is still setting up.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ started = worker is not None and worker.ident is not None&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ gone = started and not worker.is_alive()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; quiet = (r[&amp;#x27;accepted&amp;#x27;] and r[&amp;#x27;gate&amp;#x27;].is_set() and not running&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; and now - r[&amp;#x27;at&amp;#x27;] &amp;gt;= self.stale_after)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl &quot;&gt; There is no base class and nothing to register. `leela_bricks` satisfies it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## What Leela does with one&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`palette(libs)` merges every library&amp;#x27;s manifest and stamps each row with the library it came from. `locate(src)` returns the library and the brick. `wire(src)` returns the snippet that fills the brick&amp;#x27;s ports. `mount(app)` registers each library&amp;#x27;s own routes on Leela&amp;#x27;s app.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The library&amp;#x27;s `serve.py` takes `(app, page=None)`, and it opens with &amp;quot;Nothing here imports the application it is mounted in&amp;quot;. No second server runs, and `LEELA_BRICK_HOST` serves only a library nobody installed.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`split_src` keeps the library prefix. The earlier code did `src.split(&amp;#x27;:&amp;#x27;)[-1]` and threw it away, which makes two libraries that each have a `viz.series` resolve to whichever answered first. Only the named library now answers a prefixed `src`. A bare name searches every library and takes the first, which is why a document should write the prefix.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## What was measured&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Eight files went into an empty package with a two-line `__init__.py`, and nothing else changed. The package imports on `fastcore` and `fasthtml` alone. Leela&amp;#x27;s resolver reads it as 10 bricks in 4 groups. `locate` finds ports and emits. `wire` returns the package&amp;#x27;s own snippet and its remote fallback. `mount` registers all seven routes on a `FastHTML` app. `data.fill(&amp;#x27;viz.series&amp;#x27;)` runs the snippet and returns real values.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The extraction is a packaging change rather than a redesign, and the code already sits on the right side of the line.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Two facts decide where the line goes.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`lego/__init__.py` is `from .app import *` and `lego/bricks/__init__.py` is `from .app import connect`. Either one is enough to make `import lego.bricks` boot lego&amp;#x27;s whole application. In this container it fails on `ujson`, one of lego&amp;#x27;s thirteen dependencies. Nothing under `lego/bricks/` other than `app.py` imports `lego`.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Four of the ten bricks carry wiring that imports a domain package. `panchanga.day`, `panchanga.horas` and `panchanga.wheel` import `lego.muhurtha.panchanga`. `thrifty.costs` imports `lego.thrifty.data`. The other six, every `viz.*` and every `learn.*`, ship no wiring at all. They are display components that read whatever the document already computed.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## What to extract&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Take the contract and the six domain-free bricks. Leave the four domain bricks with the packages their wiring needs.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| goes | is |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+|---|---|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `bricks.py` | `Port`, `Brick`, the registry, `manifest()`, `find()` |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `cfg.py` | the seven route paths |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `serve.py` | `connect(app, page=None)`, which imports nothing about the app |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `data.py` | `fill()` runs a brick&amp;#x27;s snippet here; `remote_wire()` is the call for a document that lacks the package |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `ui.py`, `bricks.js`, `bricks.css`, `frame.js` | the gallery, the frame, and the drawing keyed by brick name |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `viz.*`, `learn.*` | six bricks with no wiring and no domain dependency |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| stays | why |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+|---|---|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `app.py` | it is the upstream seam: `lego.core`, `RouteOverrides`, the upstream nav |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `panchanga.*`, `thrifty.*` | their wiring imports `lego.muhurtha` and `lego.thrifty` |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## The spec is now built&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`extensions/bricks` is the extracted package, `leela-bricks`. Eight files moved with no&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+edit. Only `bricks.py` changed, and it took all four changes below.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ uv pip install -e extensions/bricks&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+That is the whole install, and the entry point does the rest. `libraries()` finds&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`leela_bricks`, `palette()` reads ten components in four groups, and the notes list is empty.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`KNOWN` still names `lego.bricks` for a library that publishes no entry point, and an absent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+library produces no note.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The four domain bricks came too, and their wiring still imports `lego.muhurtha` and `lego.thrifty`.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`needs` exists for that case, and the palette therefore names the package a component wants before the cell runs.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| brick | needs |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+|---|---|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `panchanga.day`, `panchanga.horas`, `panchanga.wheel` | `lego.muhurtha.panchanga` |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `thrifty.costs` | `lego.thrifty.data` |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `viz.tiles`, `viz.series`, `viz.funnel` | nothing |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `learn.cell`, `learn.wavepacket`, `learn.orbit` | nothing |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## Four changes the extracted package needs&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+**Own the `src` prefix.** `Brick.src` was `f&amp;#x27;lego.bricks:{self.name}&amp;#x27;`, hardcoded. After extraction that string names a package that no longer holds the brick. `LIB = __name__.rsplit(&amp;#x27;.&amp;#x27;, 1)[0]` derives it. Renaming the package therefore updates every `src` it serves.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+**Give each library its own registry.** `BRICKS` is a module-global dict and `brick()` mutates it. That works while one package registers everything. It breaks as soon as a second library keeps its own bricks. That library would call `brick()` into the extracted package&amp;#x27;s global, and then every library&amp;#x27;s `manifest()` would return every library&amp;#x27;s bricks. The package exposes a `Registry` a library instantiates, with `manifest()` and `find()` reading its own. `manifest()` also returns `library`, which tells a caller which registry answered.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+**Publish the entry point.** `[project.entry-points.&amp;quot;leela.bricks&amp;quot;]` so Leela finds the library without `KNOWN`. `pip install` is the whole of procurement. `KNOWN` stays for a library that publishes none.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+**Say when a snippet needs a package.** A brick whose `wire` imports something should declare it. `data.fill` already catches the failure, and `remote_wire` is already the fallback. A document still discovers the missing package by running a cell and reading a traceback. The manifest row carries `needs`. A regex over the wiring&amp;#x27;s own `import` lines produces it, minus the standard library. A component cannot claim a dependency its code does not import, and cannot hide one it does.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## What Leela ships&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Leela includes no components of its own. A `sim` is a component the document itself defines, in JavaScript, with `root`, `props` and `emit` in scope. A `sim` needs no package, and Leela therefore stays fully usable with no library installed. The canvas skill states that you can move a `sim` into a package without changing a line.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Leela ships the resolver and the contract. A chart is not IDE behaviour. A bundled component library would become a compatibility surface, held forever on Leela&amp;#x27;s release clock rather than the library&amp;#x27;s. The same reason keeps `kunda`, `kavacha` and `pullup` out of this repository.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## What the merge connected&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`leela/blocks/canvas/app.py` now holds both halves. The palette route is the resolver, and the two&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+routes that fetched from a host have gone. `/canvas/palette` reads `palette(libs)`, and&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`/canvas/wire/{name}` reads the library. `_wire_from_host` keeps its name and reads the library&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+too, and it no longer drops the `src` prefix. Nothing in the block imports `urllib` any more.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`brick_host()` survives as the base for `remote_wire`. `remote_wire` is the snippet a document&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+runs when it holds the component but not the package that fills it. HTTP is the right answer in&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+that one case, and in no other.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/details&gt;&lt;details&gt;&lt;summary&gt;docs/canvas.md +287 -0&lt;/summary&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;in&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;diff&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;body&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl h&quot;&gt;@@ -0,0 +1,287 @@&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+# Canvas&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+One file holds prose, code, embedded components, simulations, PDFs and video. Each brick in it&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+recomputes when a name it reads changes.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The notebook Leela already has is a list of cells. A canvas is prose with everything else inside it,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+and its cells are not the point of the document. `leela/blocks/canvas/` is the block.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`examples/canvas/` holds six of them.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+![A canvas open](screenshots/canvas-funnel.png)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## The file&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A canvas is markdown. `*.canvas.md`. Prose is prose. Everything else is a fenced block or a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+comment-wrapped region, and both survive a plain markdown renderer.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+````md&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```canvas code id=c1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+tokens = 1200&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```canvas brick id=b1 src=lego.bricks:thrifty.costs emit_row=picked&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+bind rows = rows&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+prop height = 220&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;!--canvas note id=n1--&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+An **aside**, still rendered by anything that reads markdown.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;!--/canvas--&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+````&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Fenced kinds: `code`, `ask`, `brick`, `sim`, `data`, `pdf`, `video`. Wrapped kinds: `reply`, `note`,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`quiz`. Anything else in the file is a `text` brick.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The parser is a line scan rather than a pair of regular expressions. A canvas fence inside a longer&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+markdown fence is an example of a brick and not a brick. A document about canvases is itself a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+canvas. Windows line endings read the same as Unix ones. Two bricks cannot share an id, and the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+parser therefore gives the second brick a fresh id on read. Without that rule, every op on the first brick&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+would reach the second one in silence.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A `pdf` brick with a relative `src` is a file beside the canvas, served by `/canvas/file`, which&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+resolves under the canvas directory and refuses anything above it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A brick body holds `bind &amp;lt;port&amp;gt; = &amp;lt;expression&amp;gt;` and `prop &amp;lt;key&amp;gt; = &amp;lt;value&amp;gt;` lines. The body of a code brick&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+is the code itself, kept exactly, and nothing reads it for directives.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A canvas stores no outputs, and opening one runs it. The file therefore diffs to what somebody&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+changed and nothing else. `test_canvas.py` opens a canvas, runs it, wires it and asks questions of&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+it, then asserts that it saves back byte for byte.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## The dataflow&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Code bricks share one namespace and run in dependency order rather than document order. `defs_of`&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+reads what a brick defines from its AST; `reads_of` reads what it needs. `order` sorts them. A cycle&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+falls back to document order.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`downstream(bricks, names)` is what makes the document live. It returns every code brick whose&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+inputs include one of `names`, transitively, followed by every brick with a binding that reads one.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Setting a name reruns exactly that set.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Bindings are expressions evaluated against the namespace. A binding that raises reports the error on&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+the brick rather than blanking it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## Components&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Every embedded component runs in an iframe. The document and the frame exchange four messages and&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+nothing else.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| message | direction | meaning |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+|---|---|---|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `brick:ready` | frame to document | the frame has loaded, with its manifest |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `brick:props` | document to frame | resolved port values |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `brick:height` | frame to document | how tall it wants to be |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `brick:emit` | frame to document | a value the person produced by using it |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`brick:emit` is why a canvas is not a dashboard. Clicking an organelle, a rasi or a funnel bar writes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+a name into the namespace, and every cell that reads that name reruns. A component is an input as&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+much as an output.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The brick&amp;#x27;s attributes name the port&amp;#x27;s target as `emit_&amp;lt;port&amp;gt;`. Two funnels in one document&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+therefore never fight over `stages`.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+![Clicking a component writes into the document](screenshots/canvas-cell.png)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## Wiring&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The package that owns the component declares its ports, and the document never does.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`leela_bricks` is one such package. Each brick in it declares its ports, what it emits, and the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+code that fills it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Picking a component from the palette inserts it and reads its wiring. Leela puts that code in the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+document as an ordinary code brick, then binds the ports it filled. You can see and edit the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+wiring, and the document holds no hidden connection.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Where a component comes from is [bricks.md](bricks.md). Leela reads the palette and the wiring in&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+process, from a library installed beside it. `LEELA_BRICK_HOST` is the fallback for a library&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+nobody installed. An earlier version of this block fetched both over HTTP, from a default that&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+was Leela&amp;#x27;s own port. A fresh install therefore had an empty palette and no error.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A package ships its wiring twice. The first form imports the package, and the second form calls&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+the host that owns it. The document runs the first form, and falls back to the second when the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+import fails. That import fails when the package is not beside the document.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```python&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+from lego.muhurtha.panchanga import Place, day_panchanga&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+day = day_panchanga(Place(12.97, 77.59, &amp;#x27;Asia/Kolkata&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;Bengaluru&amp;#x27;), date.today())&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```python&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+import json, urllib.request&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+_ports = json.load(urllib.request.urlopen(&amp;#x27;http://127.0.0.1:5001/bricks/data/panchanga.day&amp;#x27;))&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+day = _ports[&amp;#x27;day&amp;#x27;]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The ⚙ in a brick&amp;#x27;s rail opens the wiring panel: every port, its expression, what it currently&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+resolves to, and the names in the namespace to pick from.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+![The wiring panel](screenshots/canvas-wire.png)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The palette is what the host publishes, grouped by the block that owns each component.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+![The palette](screenshots/canvas-palette.png)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## The helper&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Three places reach the one helper: the margin, an `ask` brick in the document, and `mod+k`&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+anywhere. All three run the same turn, and only the selection that travels with it differs.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Its reach into the document is eight tools and no others.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| tool | does |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+|---|---|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `canvas_read` | the document as it stands |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `canvas_insert` | a new brick at a position |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `canvas_replace` | rewrite one brick |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `canvas_remove` | take a brick out |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `canvas_bind` | point a port at an expression |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `canvas_run` | run a code brick and let the dataflow settle |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `canvas_answer` | prose attached to the question that asked for it |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `canvas_values` | read names out of the namespace |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Every one goes through `apply_op`, which is also what the person&amp;#x27;s own edits go through. There is no&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+second path into the document.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A turn streams `step`, `chunk`, `op`, `answer`, `done`. The document applies each `op` event as it&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+arrives, and a brick therefore appears while the turn is still running. Steering is a queue per&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+turn. The turn takes text posted to `/canvas/steer` at the next step boundary, and replans the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+rest of the turn.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The trail is the last twelve questions, each with the brick it came from and the selection it&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+carried. It goes into the next turn&amp;#x27;s context, which is why a follow-up needs no preamble.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+![Steering a turn that is already running](screenshots/canvas-steer.png)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## Canvas mode&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+What the agent knows about a canvas is a skill, and Leela owns it. `leela/skills/canvas.py` is the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+body: the file format, the dataflow, what a component emits, the eight tools, and how to work in one.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+It is not a `pyskills` entry point. A skill that is only true inside a canvas should not reach&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+every agent that has Leela installed. `leela.skills.push(agent, &amp;#x27;canvas&amp;#x27;)` puts the skill on the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+agent&amp;#x27;s registry when a canvas opens, and `drop` takes it off when the canvas closes. The eight&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+tools go on and come off with it. `Agentic.open` and `Agentic.close` are those two calls.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Ramabana holds none of this. `Agent.skills` is `discover(..., extra=registry.skills)`. A pushed&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+skill therefore reaches the skill index and `read_skill` with no change to the agent core. The&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+proposal on `ramabana`&amp;#x27;s branch turns the tools into a shalya capability group. The skill stays&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Leela&amp;#x27;s either way.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The skill is also the stand-in&amp;#x27;s source. The stand-in answers a question about the canvas out of&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+the section of the skill that covers it, which keeps one text right rather than two.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## The model&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`helper_for(agent)` returns `Agentic` where a model exists and `Scripted` where none does.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`Scripted` is deterministic. It reads the same `Ask`, calls the same tools, and emits the same&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+events. It carries no judgement and no facts. To answer a question about a word, it finds where&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+this document already explains that word. A word the document never explains gets no answer.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+It scores which component to embed against what the host publishes, never against a table kept&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+here.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`Agentic` runs the real turn. The spike never exercises it, because the spike has no model.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## The editor&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+You edit the document in place. Prose stays rendered while you work in it, and it returns to&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+markdown on the way out. Selecting a sentence to ask about it therefore leaves the sentence&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+looking the same.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| where | what |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+|---|---|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| gutter | `+` inserts under the block, the grip drags it, clicking the grip opens what else it can do |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `/` on an empty line | the block menu, grouped, filtered as you type, driven by the keyboard |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| a text selection | bold, italic, code, link, and Ask AI, which is the inline turn |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `Enter` | splits the block at the caret. `shift+Enter` is a line break inside one |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `Escape` | leaves the text and picks the block. Then arrows move, `Enter` enters, `Backspace` deletes |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `mod+k` | ask, anchored wherever you are |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `mod+j` | the helper margin |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `mod+b`, `mod+i`, `mod+e` | the three marks, applied to the markdown rather than to the HTML |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| `mod+enter` | run this cell. `mod+shift+enter` runs the document in dependency order |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+![The gutter, on hover](screenshots/canvas-gutter.png)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+![The block it](screenshots/canvas-format.png)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Both themes, and every embedded component follows the one the class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The editor writes marks to the file, never to the rendered HTML. `document.execCommand(&amp;#x27;bold&amp;#x27;)`&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+would put in a `&amp;lt;b&amp;gt;` that the markdown writer then has to guess about.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The type scale, the token names and the popover shape follow BlockSuite&amp;#x27;s. A canvas beside an&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+editor built on BlockSuite therefore reads as the same application. Both themes sit in&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`canvas.css`, and `test_canvas.py` asserts the dark half names no token the light half lacks.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## Modes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`mode: make` and `mode: learn` in the frontmatter. The substrate is the same. The palette and the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+default bricks differ. `a-sales-funnel`, `the-traditional-day`, `tunnelling` and `an-animal-cell` use&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+learn. `pricing-a-run` and `making-a-block` use make.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Nothing in the runtime branches on the mode. It is a label on the document and a filter on the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+palette.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## Running it&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`leela/blocks/__init__.py` connects the block, which serves `/canvas` from the IDE app. It also&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+runs on its own, with no kernels, no agent and no workspace:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```sh&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+uv run python tools/canvas_spike.py # http://localhost:5002/canvas&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+BRICK_HOST=http://127.0.0.1:5001 uv run python tools/canvas_spike.py&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The components come from a component host on `BRICK_HOST`. Without one, the palette is empty, and&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+a brick already in a document draws with the sample data its package declares.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The canvas serves its own bundle from `/canvas/js` rather than joining the three IDE bundles.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span a&quot;&gt;+![A PDF open in a canvas](screenshots/canvas-pdf.png)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## What the spike does not do&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+- The runtime is `exec` in the web process, not a kunda kernel. Ordering, staleness and error shape&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ are the real ones. Isolation, interrupt and restart are not there.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+- There is no undo. `apply_op` is the single write path a history would hook, and nothing hooks it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+- Prose editing round-trips through `cvHtmlToMd`, which handles what `cvMd` can produce and no more.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ `mod+e` shows the markdown for a block where that is not enough.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+- A canvas is a page, not a tab. Opening one inside the IDE means a tab kind, a mount, and a place&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ in the command palette.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+- `Agentic` has never run.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+- Block selection takes one block at a time. Dragging a range across many blocks is not there.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+- The markdown writer handles what the renderer can produce and no more. `mod+e` shows the source&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ for a block where that is not enough.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/details&gt;&lt;details&gt;&lt;summary&gt;docs/change.canvas.md +354 -0&lt;/summary&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;in&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;diff&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;body&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl h&quot;&gt;@@ -0,0 +1,354 @@&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+---&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+title: The canvas document: a goal, its plan and its changes in one file&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+---&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+# What this is&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A goal like &amp;quot;increase procurement productivity by 10%&amp;quot; is not one kind of work. You frame the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+measure. You collect what people already know. You pull an extract apart. You prototype one rule.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+You write the recommendation.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Today each of those lives in a different tool. The plan is in a tracker. The numbers are in a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+notebook. The research is in browser tabs. The recommendation is in a deck. Nothing crosses&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+between them except a person who remembers all four.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+One file now holds every one of the four. It is a markdown file. The context comes from `resolve`, which is the same basket a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+question in the document would send. The document stays the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+record. `git diff` therefore shows the drafting, and a person can edit a sentence and delete the mark.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```canvas snippet id=s-explain path=leela/blocks/canvas/explain.py symbol=explain&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A brick that already has a body is left alone. A sentence a person wrote is the one to keep.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`overwrite` is the only way past that rule.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`ask(prompt, brick)` is the host&amp;#x27;s. Nothing here imports a model. Leela passes its own assistant.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`capture` and `replay` stand in when no model is reachable: `capture` writes the prompts out, and&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`replay` answers from a file.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```canvas snippet id=s-replay path=leela/blocks/canvas/explain.py symbol=replay&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+# This page&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`review` builds a document from a diff. `lit` draws a document as one column for a phone.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A `snippet` brick cites code. It does not hold a copy. `snip` reads the file and finds the symbol&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+in it. This page cannot show code that the file no longer has.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```canvas snippet id=s-snip path=leela/blocks/canvas/change.py symbol=snip&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Each long snippet and each long diff arrives folded. A phone screen holds about 20 lines.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```canvas snippet id=s-diff path=leela/blocks/canvas/lit.py symbol=_diff&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The diff body scrolls sideways inside its own box. The page does not scroll sideways. This is the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+one rule that most diff pages get wrong on a phone.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`review` now puts the prose next to the file that it explains. A document that explains its files&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+therefore gives a literate diff without more work.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```canvas snippet id=s-lit path=leela/blocks/canvas/lit.py symbol=html_of&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Here is one real diff, from the commit that added the value view. wiring, the example, the build file |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Almost every file is new, and no earlier version exists to
