The page therefore&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+shows snippets rather than one large diff.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+# Checks&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+40 tests pass. Each test states one rule.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Five faults came out of writing the tests and this page.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A `context=discard` brick left the budget in document order, and not first. The item carried the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+scope that chose it, and not the mode of the brick.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`state` reported `todo` for a finished change whenever a caller passed no diff.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The `# %%` text form tore a brick in two when the prose quoted the marker. The markdown form&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+removed that fault, because prose is prose.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A comment wrap had to fit on one line. This document&amp;#x27;s own bundle has five attributes. The reader&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+now joins the lines until it finds `--&amp;gt;`.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Two headings with only prose between them became one region. The second heading never started a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+section. The reader now splits prose at each heading.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+# Not done&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The document format and the dataflow exist twice. `leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py` here and&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py` on the `dynamic-document-canvas` branch read the same file. That&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+branch also has the reactive runtime, the embedded components and the eight `canvas_*` agent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+tools. This branch has the basket, the change bundle and the three views. A merge keeps one&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`doc.py` and both halves of the rest.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The block serves its own client from `/canvas/js`, built into `leela/static/lee-canvas.js`. The&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+prototype that stood in for it while the routes were being written is gone.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`inline_ai` is one conversation with one approval slot. A canvas invites two questions at once.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Ramabana wraps any context in `&amp;lt;notebook path=...&amp;gt;`. A `.canvas.md` path given to `notebook_cells`&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+will fail.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+No model answered the prompts in this container. There is no key here. The prose above each&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+snippet came from the session that wrote the code, under the same prompt. `capture` wrote the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+prompts out and `replay` would put a model&amp;#x27;s answers back.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/details&gt;&lt;details&gt;&lt;summary&gt;docs/dynamic-documents.md +200 -0&lt;/summary&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;in&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;diff&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;body&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl h&quot;&gt;@@ -0,0 +1,200 @@&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+# Dynamic documents&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A goal like &amp;quot;increase procurement productivity by 10%&amp;quot; is neither a coding task nor a writing task. Reaching it takes five steps. Frame the measure. Collect what the team already knows. Pull an extract apart until the numbers say something. Prototype the one rule that might work. Write the recommendation. Today those five steps live in five tools. The notebook holds the extract. The deck holds the recommendation. The research sits in tabs, and the plan sits in a tracker. Only a person carries context between them.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Leela already holds four of the five. It has the kernel, the files, the vault, the agent and the notebook. It lacks a document that follows the work rather than a script.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Two branches have gone at that. `claude/dynamic-document-canvas-ohgfud` built the file and the runtime, wired into Leela as a block. `leela/blocks/canvas` builds the context engine on that file. This document is the design both halves answer to.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## What a flat list cannot be&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Every notebook is one flat list. Its prompt cells read from the top of the document down to the cell being asked, which `Notebook.context` does in `leela/blocks/nb/nb.py`. The list works because it is the order the work happened in. Every cell above yours is work you did before, and the model should probably know it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+That rule dies the moment the document holds more than one line of work. Framing the goal, reading the audit, cleaning the extract and drafting the recommendation are four strands, not four consecutive steps. Ask the recommendation prompt to read everything above it and it reads three failed attempts at a groupby. Ask it to read nothing and you are pasting again.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The audit is the case that makes it concrete. It belongs in the context of the synthesis question near the top, and in the context of the risk question near the bottom, and in nothing between them. Position cannot express that. Nothing about where a brick sits says which questions it answers.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## The file&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`*.canvas.md`. Prose is prose. A brick markdown cannot show is a fence, `` ```canvas code id=c1 ``. A brick whose body is markdown a plain renderer should still show is a comment wrap, `&amp;lt;!--canvas goal id=goal--&amp;gt;`. Headings are the document&amp;#x27;s regions. Frontmatter carries the title.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+This is the canvas branch&amp;#x27;s format. A plan, a design doc and a set of research clippings are prose, and nobody reads or reviews prose held in JSON. Markdown gives three things. `git diff` shows the argument changing rather than a re-serialised tree. The document opens in any reader. The design doc and the code that tests it stay in one file.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Reading it works line by line rather than by one regex over the file. A canvas fence inside a longer markdown fence is an example of a brick and not a brick. A document about canvases therefore parses as a document. This rule matters, because a `source` brick holding a clipped page is where quoted markup arrives.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## What AFFiNE contributes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+AFFiNE&amp;#x27;s [BlockSuite](https://blocksuite.io) puts one block tree behind two views. A document is a list of blocks, each with a flavour named `namespace:name`. Page mode reads the tree top to bottom. Edgeless mode reads the same blocks off a surface that gives them coordinates, frames that group them, and connectors that join them. Neither view owns the document.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Two of those ideas belong here, and the code replaces the third.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The named kind belongs. A notebook cell has three types, because a notebook holds three kinds of thing. A document that holds a goal, a task, a clipping and a chart needs a name for each. A `goal` brick carries `measure`, `baseline`, `target` and `by`, which holds a measure better than a markdown cell and a convention.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The two views belong. The list is the right way to read finished work, and the only way to review it. The canvas suits work in progress, because unfinished thinking is not linear. `prop x` and `prop y` are the only trace the canvas leaves in the file. A document nobody has laid out is therefore still complete, and `arrange` places an unopened document on a canvas.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The connector does not belong. On AFFiNE&amp;#x27;s canvas a person draws a connector by hand, and a diagram kept beside the code goes wrong. The code already states the graph.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## Upstream is read off the code&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`defs_of` and `reads_of` walk the AST. Whichever brick binds a name owns it. Which bricks a brick reads from is therefore a fact about the document rather than a drawing over it. `order` runs code in dependency order, and `upstream` answers what one question is downstream of.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Three things extend it where the AST cannot see.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A question anchors on the brick above it. &amp;quot;Fix that&amp;quot; means that brick and everything it reads, which is what a person means and what `scope=upstream` on a question should give them. `anchor=&amp;lt;id&amp;gt;` overrides it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A name a question puts in backticks is a name it reads. Writing `` `triage` `` in a question pulls in the brick that defines `triage` and its own upstream. Backticks around an identifier already mean &amp;quot;this one&amp;quot;, and nobody has to learn a new rule.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`supports=`, `refutes=` and `blocks=` name a relation between bricks that no AST can find. That is where a clipping supporting a claim goes, and it is the only hand-drawn edge left.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## Context is the design&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Every question carries a rule, and `canvas.context.resolve` turns that rule into the exact list of items the turn will send.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+scope=region none | page | region | upstream | doc&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+pin s-audit always in; also file:, vault:, url:, var:, sel:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+mute n-cap always out&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+budget=12000 characters&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+```&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`page` is the notebook&amp;#x27;s own behaviour, kept because it is right for a document being read as a document. `region` is the section you are working in. `upstream` is the dataflow. The risk question therefore reads the backtest, the rule, the split and the extract. It reads none of the four tasks sitting beside them.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`resolve` is pure, and it returns items rather than a string. One list builds the prompt and draws the panel. The panel shows every brick in the basket, what put it there, what it costs in characters, and a running total against the budget. Bricks in the basket glow on the canvas. Click a row to mute it, and the glow goes out. The panel therefore shows exactly what the model gets.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Under a budget, the goal and the pins survive. A `context=discard` brick goes first, then the oldest ordinary one, which is what notebook cells already do through `context_mode`. `resolve` clips and marks a pin larger than the whole budget rather than dropping it. A pin that vanishes silently costs a reader more than one that arrives short.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`render` emits `&amp;lt;cell id= type= compact= why= region=&amp;gt;`. That is Leela&amp;#x27;s own notebook markup, chosen on purpose. Ramabana&amp;#x27;s `compact_notebook_context` sheds elements matching exactly that pattern when a prompt overflows the window. A document that rendered anything else would carry a budget with nothing underneath it. An oversized turn would then fail at the provider rather than shed a research clipping.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## No stored outputs&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A canvas keeps no outputs. Opening one runs it, and a code brick&amp;#x27;s value comes from the live namespace.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+That deletes the whole staleness problem rather than solving it. There is no hash to compare, no `output_hash` to carry, and no case where a chart is correct about a dataframe somebody has since reloaded. It also deletes the merge conflicts that notebook outputs cause, which is most of them.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+It costs two things: a document that does not open instantly, and one nobody can read offline with its numbers in it. `bind` answers the second cost. A `data` brick renders a sentence from live values, and the prose therefore never carries last month&amp;#x27;s numbers.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## A boundary that is a unit of change&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A region groups bricks for reading. A `bundle` brick claims its region as one change, and that is the difference between a Miro frame and something worth having. The boundary names a goal, owns a set of files, holds the tasks and the prose and the code together, and is the thing a reviewer opens.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Four parts, and the last one is the point.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`goal=&amp;lt;id&amp;gt;` is the value link. A change serves a goal, and the goal carries a measure and a target. `contributes=` says in words what this change is worth against that target. Leela invents no arithmetic. A share of a ten-point target is a judgement, and pretending otherwise would put a fake number in a pull request.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The files come from the code. A code brick marked `#|export` writes a module. That module is the change, and `modules()` already knows the path. `paths=` adds what the bricks do not generate: tests, config, a migration. Deriving first matters because a list maintained by hand is a list that goes stale, and a stale claim is worse than no claim.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`refs=` attaches packages, files and other documents for review. It uses the same `pkg:`, `file:`, `doc:` vocabulary as a context pin. Attaching something for a human reviewer therefore also puts it within the model&amp;#x27;s reach. One vocabulary, two readers.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`coverage(doc, changed)` holds the claim against the diff, which turns the boundary into a check. Per bundle it reports `matched` and `unmet`, a claimed file the diff never touched. Across the document it reports `unclaimed`, a changed file no bundle explains. No diff tool can produce `unclaimed`, because only the document knows what the change promised to do.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## The value view&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`value(doc, changed)` is the third document. It lists every goal, and every change serving it, each with its state and a line on how much of it has finished.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Leela derives the state. A change reaches `blocked` when one of its tasks blocks. It reaches `done` when every task reaches `done` and every claimed file moved. It reaches `doing` when some of either has. Nobody sets these as a field, because a status somebody must remember goes stale. One case needs care. An absent diff is no evidence about files, and it must not read as evidence against them. Otherwise a finished change reports as untouched work whenever you ask without a diff.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The view exists for two findings, and neither appears anywhere else in the document.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A change serving no goal appears under `Serving no goal`. Somebody is doing work that nothing in the plan asked for.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A goal nothing serves says so under its own heading. A goal with no change against it reads the same as a goal on track, until the date arrives.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The tally at the end lists every change by state, and every changed file no bundle claims. The question below it pins every goal.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## Review is another canvas&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`review(doc, bundle_id, diff)` builds a document: the goal, what the change contributes, the prose, the tasks, the questions asked inside the change with their recorded answers, one `diff` brick per file, the attachments, the coverage checks, and a question with the goal already pinned.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+It is a `Doc`. It therefore draws in both views through the same renderer, keeps the outline, and keeps the context basket. Nothing about the review view is a second implementation of anything, and a question asked inside a review has the whole change in scope.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+That also answers whether this replaces Leela&amp;#x27;s git view. It does not. The existing view is for line-level work: staging, hunks, blame, conflicts. This is for the question a diff cannot answer, which is whether the change does what the goal said. `canvas.change.hunks` takes unified diff text. Whatever produces the diff, `gheasy` included, can feed it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Leela builds a review per request and never writes it back. A diff is a fact about a commit range, not part of the document.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## The literate page&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`lit` writes one document as one column for a phone. `paint` draws a canvas for someone working in it; this draws the same document for someone reading it on the way to a meeting. No JavaScript, no other requests, both colour schemes, and everything long folded.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Writing this repository&amp;#x27;s own change as a canvas document, and rendering it with `lit`, found four things the design was missing. That is the argument for dogfooding rather than a claim about the tool.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A `snippet` brick cites code instead of holding it. `snip` reads the file the brick names and finds the symbol in it, decorators included. A literate page wants the function that does the work rather than the whole diff. A copy pasted into prose goes stale. The whole page rests on this primitive, and nothing before it could do the job.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A comment wrap had to fit on one line. A bundle carries a goal, a contribution, a covers list, a paths list and a refs list. One line therefore ran 300 characters wide in a file a person edits. The reader now joins lines until it finds `--&amp;gt;`.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Two headings with only prose between them became one region. Prose accumulates into one text brick, and the reader took only its first heading. The second heading never started a section. The reader now splits prose at every heading, skipping headings inside a plain fence.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A heading and the prose under it are one brick, and the page renderer took the heading as a section title and dropped the brick. Every paragraph under a first-level heading disappeared. It now trims the heading and keeps the rest.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`review` also changed. It now places the prose that cites a path next to that file&amp;#x27;s hunks. A document that explains its files therefore produces a literate diff with no further work, which is what the exercise was for.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`tools/make_change_page.py` builds the page. `docs/change.canvas.md` is the source, and `media/canvas-change.html` is the output. `--prompts FILE` writes the drafting prompts and stops; `--answers FILE` puts a model&amp;#x27;s answers back.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## Where the prompts live&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`lit` draws and `explain` writes. Three places hold the three parts, and the split is the point.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The register lives in ramabana. `write_docs` is a pyskill, and `rule_text` reads it through `shalya.skills.discover`. `CLAUDE.md` says no repository holds a copy of a writing skill, and a prompt with one pasted into it is that copy. `rule_text` therefore raises when the skill is missing rather than falling back. A silent fallback puts the wrong register on the page, and nobody notices.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The task lives in the package. `explain.md` is the template and `ste.md` states the ASD-STE100 limits for this output. Neither restates `write_docs`. `ste.md` is nine lines, and every one of them is an output constraint rather than a rule about English.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The prose lives in the document. `explain` writes each answer into the brick body and marks it `wrote=ai`. A drafted sentence is therefore in `git diff`, a reviewer can see which sentences a model wrote, and editing one is editing the document. `explain` leaves a brick that already has a body alone, because a sentence a person wrote is the one worth keeping.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The prompt&amp;#x27;s context comes from `resolve`, which is the same basket a question in the document would send. One context engine serves the reader and the drafter, and the panel that already exists can therefore inspect a prompt.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`ask(prompt, brick)` is the host&amp;#x27;s. Nothing in `canvas` imports a model. Leela passes its own assistant. `capture` and `replay` stand in where no model is reachable: `capture` writes the prompts out, `replay` answers from a file.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## Getting work back out&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Nothing here is a new place for work to get stuck.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`to_ipynb` writes a real notebook, with questions in the `metadata.leela` shape `Cell.nbcell` already uses. Leela therefore opens it, and the prompts are still prompts. `from_ipynb` reads it back and migrates a notebook that was never a document. `to_report` writes the document with the canvas taken off. `modules` writes the code bricks marked `#|export` in dependency order, which is the &amp;quot;extract the software&amp;quot; half of the goal.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## The prototypes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The package generates both, and nobody draws them by hand. They therefore show what `resolve` and `arrange` actually do.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+- `media/canvas-session.html` and `media/canvas-change.html` are the literate pages, written by the block itself from `docs/session.canvas.md` and `docs/change.canvas.md`. The prototype that drew the first mockups of both views is gone, and so are its two pages.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Both carry three documents behind one toggle: the document, the review of one change, and the value view. `page` and `canvas` switch how the loaded document draws.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`leela/blocks/canvas/procurement.canvas.md` is the document itself, and a reader should read it as a file.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## Where the two branches meet&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The canvas branch owns the format, the parser, the dataflow, the reactive runtime and the embedded components. It also owns the eight `canvas_*` tools the agent gets when a canvas opens. `canvas` owns the context engine, the three brick kinds a plan needs, and the second view.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+They are one thing, not two. `blocks/canvas/doc.py` reimplements the canvas branch&amp;#x27;s scanner and dataflow, which lets the package stand alone while the shape is still moving. That fork should not survive a decision. Merging leaves one parser in whichever half survives, and the other half imports it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The canvas branch has two things this does not. It has the reactive runtime, and it has the agent editing the document through tools rather than answering into a brick. This side has two things the canvas branch does not: a context rule a person can see and change, and a goal.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## What is not decided&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+**Nothing, on this one.** The merge is complete. `leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py` is one file: the format and the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+AST dataflow from the canvas branch, with the plan kinds, the regions, the pins and mutes, the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+prose splitting and the geometry from this one. The class is `Canvas`. `index` returns `None` for a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+brick that is not there, because `ops._at` and `Ask.near` both read that. A brick body keeps its&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+final newline, because the format keeps code exactly.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+**What the browser half draws.** `leela/blocks/canvas/*.js` draws it, built into&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`leela/static/lee-canvas.js` and served from `/canvas/js`. The block serves its own page rather&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+than joining the IDE&amp;#x27;s three bundles, so nothing in `lee-ide.js` calls its routes.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+**Whether the second view is version one.** The basket, the goal and the plan kinds work in a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+linear document and are most of the value. `arrange` plus `prop x` is the whole of the canvas, and&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+this stays cheap either way.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+**What the agent may write.** The canvas branch already answers this with eight tools and a skill&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+pushed onto the agent while a canvas is open. Whether the agent may also add bricks, rebind ports&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+and reorganise a document is a larger claim.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+## What integration costs&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A review of the standalone design against the repository found the seam work, and none of it is one line. The canvas branch has done some of it already.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`Assistant.compose` in Ramabana wraps any context in `&amp;lt;notebook path=...&amp;gt;`, and the briefing tells the model to call `notebook_cells` on that path. A `.canvas.md` path handed to `notebook_cells` reaches `Notebook.load` on text that is not nbformat. Ramabana needs to know a second document kind, or Leela needs to hand it a path it can honour.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`workspace.py` decides `Tab.kind` by suffix, with no extension point, and `tab_state`, `tab_disk`, `tab_buffer`, `cwd_for` and `kernel_key` each need a branch. `write_text_at` special-cases `.ipynb` so a rollback does not put jupytext markers into JSON. `DocStore` holds notebooks only. `blocks/refactor` treats anything not `.ipynb` as text to rewrite, which would rename identifiers inside prose; a markdown file makes that more likely rather than less.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The format answers two things that code does not. Git conflicts on prose are ordinary text conflicts, which is what markdown buys. Undo granularity for a canvas drag is a stream of `prop x` writes, and a drag that writes only on release is one edit.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Nothing anywhere answers one of them. `inline_ai` is one conversation with one `_approval_target`, while a canvas invites running two questions at once.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/details&gt;&lt;details&gt;&lt;summary&gt;docs/session.canvas.md +567 -0&lt;/summary&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;in&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;diff&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;body&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl h&quot;&gt;@@ -0,0 +1,567 @@&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+---&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+title: One session, reviewed: the canvas block, the brick library, and the page you are reading&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+---&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+# What this is&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+This file is the review of one working session, in the format the session built, read by the code&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+the session added.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`leela/blocks/canvas/app.py:page` wrote the page you are reading. It read this file, asked git for&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+the diff this file names, and rendered both.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;!--canvas goal id=g measure=&amp;quot;tools you open to review one session against its goal&amp;quot; baseline=&amp;quot;4: tracker, notebook, diff, deck&amp;quot; target=&amp;quot;1 page&amp;quot; by=2026-10-31--&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Give Leela one document that holds a goal, its plan, its research, its code and its questions,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+and one page that shows all five to a reviewer on a phone.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;!--/canvas--&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;!--canvas goal id=g2 measure=&amp;quot;slopometer density on the worst page of the branch&amp;quot; baseline=&amp;quot;26.8&amp;quot; target=&amp;quot;under 8&amp;quot; by=2026-09-30--&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Hold every page this branch adds to the English that ste.md already states, and measure it&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+rather than assert it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;!--/canvas--&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;!--canvas goal id=g3 measure=&amp;quot;findings from a review of this branch that are still open&amp;quot; baseline=&amp;quot;17&amp;quot; target=0 by=2026-09-30--&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Leave nothing in this branch that a reviewer called critical or high.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;!--/canvas--&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+# Words&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Read this table first. Every later section uses these words and no others.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| word | means |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+|---|---|&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| **brick** | one part of the document: a fence or a comment wrap. A code cell, a question, a goal, a task, a clipping. |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| **prose** | ordinary markdown between bricks. It carries no markup of its own. |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| **region** | the bricks under one heading. The headings make the regions, so nobody writes one. |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| **basket** | the exact list of bricks that one question sends to the model. |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| **bundle** | one unit of change. It claims a region, names a goal, and owns a list of files. |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| **snippet** | a brick that cites code out of a file. It keeps no copy of that code. |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| **slot** | a `diff` brick with no body. It states which diff it wants; Leela fills it. |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| **library** | an installed package of components. `leela_bricks` is the first one. |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| **needs** | what a component&amp;#x27;s wiring imports. Read off the code, never written by hand. |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+| **pata** | the retired name for this work. Sanskrit for the cloth a scroll painting is made on. The name now is `canvas`. |&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+# Why it helps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A diff tells a reviewer which lines moved. It cannot answer the three questions a reviewer brings&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+to a change.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+1. What was this change supposed to do?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+2. Did it do that?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+3. Did anything else move that nobody meant to move?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+The intent is in the document, not in the diff. So the document states the intent, the diff states&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+the fact, and `coverage` compares them. Its `unmet` list is a claim with no change behind it, and&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+its `unclaimed` list is a change with no claim behind it. Neither list can come out of a diff tool,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+which holds one of the two sets.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+This page shows that comparison at the top, as chips, before any code.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;!--canvas ask id=q1 scope=region pins=g budget=6000--&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Why can a diff tool not report `unclaimed` on its own?&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;!--/canvas--&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;!--canvas reply id=r1 of=q1--&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+`unclaimed` is the difference between two sets. A diff tool holds the files that moved. It does&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+not hold the files a change promised to touch, which sit in each bundle&amp;#x27;s `paths`. A finding&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+needs both sets.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;!--/canvas--&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+# The plan&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;!--canvas task id=t1 status=done owner=me--&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+Read the document format from the canvas branch and adopt it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl The plan is in a tracker. The numbers are in a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+notebook. The research is in browser tabs. The recommendation is in a deck. Nothing crosses&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+between them except a person who remembers all four.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;One file now holds every one of the four. It is a markdown file. class=&amp;quot;who&amp;quot;&amp;gt;me&amp;lt;/span&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/li&amp;gt;&amp;lt;li class=&amp;quot;done&amp;quot;&amp;gt;&amp;lt;span class=&amp;quot;box&amp;quot;&amp;gt;[x]&amp;lt;/span&amp;gt;&amp;lt;span&amp;gt;Move the modules into `leela/blocks/canvas/`.&amp;lt;/span&amp;gt;&amp;lt;span class=&amp;quot;who&amp;quot;&amp;gt;me&amp;lt;/span&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/li&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/ul&amp;gt;&amp;lt;h2 id=&amp;quot;words&amp;quot;&amp;gt;Words&amp;lt;/h2&amp;gt;&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;Read this table first. Every later section uses these words and no others.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;table&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;thead&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;tr&amp;gt;&amp;lt;th&amp;gt;word&amp;lt;/th&amp;gt;&amp;lt;th&amp;gt;means&amp;lt;/th&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/tr&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;/thead&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;tbody&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;tr&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;strong&amp;gt;brick&amp;lt;/strong&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;one part of the document. A fence or a comment wrap. A code cell, a question, a goal, a task, a clipping.&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/tr&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;tr&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;strong&amp;gt;prose&amp;lt;/strong&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;ordinary markdown between bricks. It needs no markup of its own.&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/tr&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;tr&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;strong&amp;gt;region&amp;lt;/strong&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;the bricks under one heading. The headings make the regions, so nobody writes one.&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/tr&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;tr&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;strong&amp;gt;basket&amp;lt;/strong&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;the exact list of bricks that one question sends to the model.&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/tr&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;tr&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;strong&amp;gt;scope&amp;lt;/strong&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;how a question gathers its first set of bricks. &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;page&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;, &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;region&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;, &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;upstream&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;, &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;doc&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; or &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;none&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;.&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/tr&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;tr&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;strong&amp;gt;pin&amp;lt;/strong&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;a brick a question always reads, whatever the scope says. A &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;mute&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; is the opposite.&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/tr&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;tr&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;strong&amp;gt;budget&amp;lt;/strong&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;how many characters a question may send. The goal and the pins survive it.&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/tr&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;tr&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;strong&amp;gt;upstream&amp;lt;/strong&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;the bricks a brick reads from. Read off the code, never drawn by hand.&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/tr&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;tr&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;strong&amp;gt;bundle&amp;lt;/strong&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;one unit of change. It claims a region, names a goal, and owns a list of files.&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/tr&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;tr&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;strong&amp;gt;snippet&amp;lt;/strong&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;a brick that cites code out of a file. It holds no copy of that code.&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/tr&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;tr&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;strong&amp;gt;canvas&amp;lt;/strong&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;td&amp;gt;the second view of the document. The same bricks, with coordinates.&amp;lt;/td&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/tr&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;/tbody&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;/table&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;The block is &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;canvas&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; and the file is &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;*.canvas.md&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;. An earlier draft of this work was a separate&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+package called &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;pata&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;, from the Sanskrit &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;pata&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;, the cloth a painter paints a scroll on. That&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+name is gone, and &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;canvas&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; is the only name now.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;h2 id=&amp;quot;why-it-helps&amp;quot;&amp;gt;Why it helps&amp;lt;/h2&amp;gt;&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;A notebook picks context by position: every cell above the question. That is right for a script,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+where the cells above are the steps you took. A plan holds four lines of work at once. Position therefore hands the recommendation question&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+three failed attempts at a groupby. The alternative is to turn it off and paste the same&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+paragraphs again.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;An audit shows the limit. It belongs to the question near the top of the document and to the risk&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+question near the bottom, and to nothing between them. Where a brick sits says nothing about which&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+questions it answers.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;A document that can say it gives three things.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;A question shows its basket before it runs: each brick, why it is there, and what it costs. Mute&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+one and the count drops.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;A boundary on the canvas is a change you can review. It names the goal, owns the files, and holds&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+the tasks, the prose and the code together. One page therefore answers whether the change does&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+what the goal said.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;A goal shows what serves it, and shows a goal that nothing serves. The second is the worse finding,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+because it looks like a goal that is going well.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;h2 id=&amp;quot;the-file&amp;quot;&amp;gt;The file&amp;lt;/h2&amp;gt;&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;A &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;pata&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; document is one markdown file. Prose stays prose. Each other part is a brick. A brick is&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+a fence or a comment wrap.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;The reader reads the file line by line. It does not use one pattern on the whole file. This is&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+necessary. A document about canvases shows fences as examples. A fence inside a longer fence is an&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+example. It is not a brick.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;The &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;TICKS&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; branch does the work. It sees a plain fence, puts the fence into the prose, and skips&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+to the end of it. Nothing inside that fence becomes a brick. This page is such a document, and it&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+reads correctly.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;b&amp;gt;leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py&amp;lt;/b&amp;gt; &amp;amp;middot; _scan&amp;lt;/figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;summary&amp;gt;_scan (36 lines)&amp;lt;/summary&amp;gt;&amp;lt;div class=&amp;quot;in&amp;quot;&amp;gt;&amp;lt;pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code class=&amp;quot;lang-python&amp;quot;&amp;gt;def _scan(text):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ &amp;amp;quot;`(kind, attrline, body)` per brick. A fence inside a longer fence is an example of one, not one.&amp;amp;quot;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ lines, i, prose, out = text.split(&amp;amp;#x27;\n&amp;amp;#x27;), 0, [], []&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ def flush():&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ for part in _prose_parts(&amp;amp;#x27;\n&amp;amp;#x27;.join(prose)): out.append((&amp;amp;#x27;text&amp;amp;#x27;, &amp;amp;#x27;&amp;amp;#x27;, part))&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ prose.clear()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ def upto(j, shut, keep):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ body = []&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ while j &amp;amp;lt; len(lines) and not shut(lines[j]): body.append(lines[j]); j += 1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if keep and j &amp;amp;lt; len(lines): body.append(lines[j])&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ return j, body&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ while i &amp;amp;lt; len(lines):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ line = lines[i]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if (m := FENCE.match(line)):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ flush()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ end = _shut(m[1])&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ i, body = upto(i + 1, lambda l: end.match(l), False)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ out.append((m[2], m[3], &amp;amp;#x27;\n&amp;amp;#x27;.join(body) + (&amp;amp;#x27;\n&amp;amp;#x27; if body else &amp;amp;#x27;&amp;amp;#x27;)))&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ elif (m := TICKS.match(line)):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ end = _shut(m[1])&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ prose.append(line)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ i, body = upto(i + 1, lambda l: end.match(l), True)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ prose.extend(body)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ elif (m := WRAP.match(line)):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ flush()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ attr = [line[m.end():]]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ while not SHUT_TAG.search(attr[-1]) and i + 1 &amp;amp;lt; len(lines): # a long attribute list wraps&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ i += 1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ attr.append(lines[i])&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ i, body = upto(i + 1, lambda l: l.strip() == SHUT, False)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ out.append((m[1], SHUT_TAG.sub(&amp;amp;#x27;&amp;amp;#x27;, &amp;amp;#x27; &amp;amp;#x27;.join(attr)), &amp;amp;#x27;\n&amp;amp;#x27;.join(body) + (&amp;amp;#x27;\n&amp;amp;#x27; if body else &amp;amp;#x27;&amp;amp;#x27;)))&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ else:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ prose.append(line); i += 1; continue&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ i += 1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ flush()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ return out&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/div&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;Headings are the regions of the document. Nobody writes a region. The reader gives each brick the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+heading above it.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;b&amp;gt;leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py&amp;lt;/b&amp;gt; &amp;amp;middot; Doc._regions&amp;lt;/figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code class=&amp;quot;lang-python&amp;quot;&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;h2 id=&amp;quot;the-basket&amp;quot;&amp;gt;The basket&amp;lt;/h2&amp;gt;&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;Each question carries a rule. The rule says what the question may read. &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;resolve&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; turns the rule&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+into the exact list that the turn will send.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;The list is the point. &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;resolve&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; gives back items, not one string. The same list draws the panel&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+and builds the prompt. What a person sees is what the model gets.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;Four rules, in order. The goal goes in first. Then each pin. A pin that no longer exists becomes a&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;code&amp;gt;missing&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; item. It is visible. A silent drop is worse, because the person still believes the pin is&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+there.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;b&amp;gt;leela/blocks/canvas/context.py&amp;lt;/b&amp;gt; &amp;amp;middot; resolve&amp;lt;/figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;summary&amp;gt;resolve (29 lines)&amp;lt;/summary&amp;gt;&amp;lt;div class=&amp;quot;in&amp;quot;&amp;gt;&amp;lt;pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code class=&amp;quot;lang-python&amp;quot;&amp;gt;def resolve(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ doc, # the document&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ bid, # which brick asks&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ spec=None, # the rule, else the one the brick carries&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ values=None, # `{brick id: output text}` from the live namespace&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ lookup=None, # `lookup(ref)` for a pin the document does not own&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ extra=(), # items the host adds, such as live variables&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ &amp;amp;quot;The exact basket for question `bid`, in the order the model reads it.&amp;amp;quot;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ b = doc.by_id(bid)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if b is None: raise KeyError(bid)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ spec = spec or spec_of(b)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ mutes, items, seen = set(spec.mutes), [], {b.id}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ def take(x, why, pinned=False):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if x.id in seen or x.id in mutes: return&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if not (t := body_text(x, values, doc)).strip(): return&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ seen.add(x.id)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ items.append(Item(ref=x.id, kind=x.kind, label=_label(x), text=t, why=why,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ region=x.region, mode=x.mode, pinned=pinned or x.mode == &amp;amp;#x27;keep&amp;amp;#x27;))&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if spec.goal and (g := doc.goal_for(bid)) is not None and g.id not in mutes: take(g, &amp;amp;#x27;goal&amp;amp;#x27;, True)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ for r in spec.pins:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if r in mutes: continue&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if _is_ref(r): items.append(_ref_item(r, lookup))&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ elif (x := doc.by_id(r)) is not None: take(x, &amp;amp;#x27;pin&amp;amp;#x27;, True)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ else: items.append(Item(ref=r, kind=&amp;amp;#x27;missing&amp;amp;#x27;, label=r, text=&amp;amp;#x27;&amp;amp;#x27;, why=&amp;amp;#x27;pin&amp;amp;#x27;, pinned=True,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ clipped=True))&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ for x in members(doc, b, spec.scope): take(x, spec.scope)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ items += list(extra)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ return _fit(items, spec.budget)&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/div&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;A scope gives the first set of bricks. &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;page&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; is the notebook rule. &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;region&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; is the section that&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+you work in. &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;upstream&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; is what the question reads from.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;b&amp;gt;leela/blocks/canvas/context.py&amp;lt;/b&amp;gt; &amp;amp;middot; members&amp;lt;/figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code class=&amp;quot;lang-python&amp;quot;&amp;gt;def members(doc, b, scope):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ &amp;amp;quot;The bricks a scope offers, before pins, mutes and the budget.&amp;amp;quot;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if scope == &amp;amp;#x27;none&amp;amp;#x27;: return L()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ at = doc.index(b.id)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if at is None: at = len(doc)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if scope == &amp;amp;#x27;page&amp;amp;#x27;: return L(doc.bricks[:at])&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if scope == &amp;amp;#x27;doc&amp;amp;#x27;: return L(x for x in doc.bricks if x.id != b.id)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if scope == &amp;amp;#x27;region&amp;amp;#x27;: return L(x for x in doc.in_region(b.region) if x.id != b.id)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ return upstream(doc.bricks, b.id)&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;The budget cuts the list. Two rules must hold. The goal and the pins stay. A pin that is larger&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+than the whole budget gets shorter; it does not go.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;The last block is the one that matters. If every item that is left is pinned, the code cuts each&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+item to a share of the budget and marks it. It never drops a pin.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;b&amp;gt;leela/blocks/canvas/context.py&amp;lt;/b&amp;gt; &amp;amp;middot; _fit&amp;lt;/figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code class=&amp;quot;lang-python&amp;quot;&amp;gt;def _fit(items, budget):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ &amp;amp;quot;Trim to `budget`. Pins and `keep` never drop; `discard` goes first, then the oldest `auto`.&amp;amp;quot;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if not budget: return items&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ total = sum(i.chars + WRAP for i in items)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if total &amp;amp;lt;= budget: return items&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ order = sorted((i for i, it in enumerate(items) if not it.pinned),&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ key=lambda i: (items[i].mode != &amp;amp;#x27;discard&amp;amp;#x27;, i))&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ drop, n = set(), 0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ while total &amp;amp;gt; budget and n &amp;amp;lt; len(order):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ total -= items[order[n]].chars + WRAP&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ drop.add(order[n])&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ n += 1&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ kept = [it for i, it in enumerate(items) if i not in drop]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if sum(i.chars + WRAP for i in kept) &amp;amp;gt; budget and kept:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ share = max(200, budget // max(1, len(kept)) - WRAP)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ kept = [replace(it, text=it.text[:share] + &amp;amp;#x27;\n…&amp;amp;#x27;, clipped=True) if it.chars &amp;amp;gt; share else it&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ for it in kept]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ return kept&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;The markup is &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;&amp;amp;lt;cell&amp;amp;gt;&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; with a &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;compact&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; attribute. This is Leela&amp;#x27;s own notebook shape, and the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+choice is deliberate. Ramabana drops &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;&amp;amp;lt;cell&amp;amp;gt;&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; elements when a prompt is too large for the window.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A document that wrote &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;&amp;amp;lt;block&amp;amp;gt;&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; would lose that net.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;b&amp;gt;leela/blocks/canvas/context.py&amp;lt;/b&amp;gt; &amp;amp;middot; render&amp;lt;/figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code class=&amp;quot;lang-python&amp;quot;&amp;gt;def render(items, doc=None):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ &amp;amp;quot;The basket as `&amp;amp;lt;cell&amp;amp;gt;` markup, which is Leela’s own notebook context shape.&amp;amp;quot;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ out = []&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ for it in items:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if not it.text.strip(): continue&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ attr = (f&amp;amp;#x27;id=&amp;amp;quot;{it.ref}&amp;amp;quot; type=&amp;amp;quot;{it.kind}&amp;amp;quot; compact=&amp;amp;quot;{&amp;amp;quot;keep&amp;amp;quot; if it.pinned else &amp;amp;quot;auto&amp;amp;quot;}&amp;amp;quot; &amp;amp;#x27;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ f&amp;amp;#x27;why=&amp;amp;quot;{it.why}&amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;#x27;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if it.region: attr += f&amp;amp;#x27; region=&amp;amp;quot;{it.region}&amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;#x27;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if it.clipped: attr += &amp;amp;#x27; clipped=&amp;amp;quot;true&amp;amp;quot;&amp;amp;#x27;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ out.append(f&amp;amp;#x27;&amp;amp;lt;cell {attr}&amp;amp;gt;\n{it.text}\n&amp;amp;lt;/cell&amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;#x27;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if doc is not None and (links := _links(doc, {i.ref for i in items if i.text.strip()})):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ out.append(&amp;amp;#x27;&amp;amp;lt;links&amp;amp;gt;\n&amp;amp;#x27; + &amp;amp;#x27;\n&amp;amp;#x27;.join(links) + &amp;amp;#x27;\n&amp;amp;lt;/links&amp;amp;gt;&amp;amp;#x27;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ return &amp;amp;#x27;\n&amp;amp;#x27;.join(out)&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;h2 id=&amp;quot;the-wiring&amp;quot;&amp;gt;The wiring&amp;lt;/h2&amp;gt;&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code&amp;gt;upstream&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; reads the code. It does not read a diagram. A name belongs to the brick that binds it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+A diagram beside the code goes wrong; the code does not.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code&amp;gt;defs_of&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; finds each name that a cell binds at the top level of its code. It looks inside &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;if&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;code&amp;gt;for&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;, &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;try&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; and &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;with&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;. It does not look inside a &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;def&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;, because a name in a function belongs to&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+the function.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;b&amp;gt;leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py&amp;lt;/b&amp;gt; &amp;amp;middot; defs_of&amp;lt;/figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code class=&amp;quot;lang-python&amp;quot;&amp;gt;def defs_of(source):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ &amp;amp;quot;Names a code brick binds at module level, however it binds them.&amp;amp;quot;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ t = _walk(source)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if t is None: return L()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ out = L()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ for n in _module_body(t):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)): out.append(n.name)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ elif isinstance(n, ast.Assign): out += L(n.targets).map(_targets).concat()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ elif isinstance(n, (ast.AnnAssign, ast.AugAssign)): out += _targets(n.target)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ elif isinstance(n, (ast.For, ast.AsyncFor)): out += _targets(n.target)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ elif isinstance(n, (ast.With, ast.AsyncWith)):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ out += L(n.items).map(lambda i: _targets(i.optional_vars)).concat()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ elif isinstance(n, (ast.Import, ast.ImportFrom)):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ out += L(n.names).map(lambda a: (a.asname or a.name).split(&amp;amp;#x27;.&amp;amp;#x27;)[0])&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ for n in ast.walk(t):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if isinstance(n, ast.NamedExpr): out += _targets(n.target)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ return out.unique()&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;Three additions reach where the code cannot see.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;A question anchors on the brick above it. &amp;quot;Fix that&amp;quot; means that brick and all that it reads.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;A name in backticks is a name that the question reads. Write &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;`triage`&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; and the brick that&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+defines &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;triage&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; goes in.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code&amp;gt;supports=&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;, &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;refutes=&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; and &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;blocks=&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; state a relation between two bricks. No code states these.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;b&amp;gt;leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py&amp;lt;/b&amp;gt; &amp;amp;middot; upstream&amp;lt;/figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code class=&amp;quot;lang-python&amp;quot;&amp;gt;def upstream(bricks, bid, depth=12):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ &amp;amp;quot;Every brick `bid` reads from, transitively, in document order.&amp;amp;quot;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ bricks = L(bricks)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ owner, seen = _owners(bricks), set()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ want = {bid} | ({a} if (a := anchor_of(bricks, bid)) else set())&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ seen |= want - {bid}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ for _ in range(depth):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ nxt = set()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ for b in bricks.filter(lambda b: b.id in want):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ nxt |= {owner[n] for n in b.reads if n in owner}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ for ids in b.links.values(): nxt |= set(ids)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ nxt -= seen | {bid}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if not nxt: break&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ seen |= nxt&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ want = nxt&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ seen |= {b.id for b in bricks if bid in {i for ids in b.links.values() for i in ids}}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ return bricks.filter(lambda b: b.id in seen - {bid})&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;h2 id=&amp;quot;the-change&amp;quot;&amp;gt;The change&amp;lt;/h2&amp;gt;&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;A region groups bricks to read. A &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;bundle&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; brick claims its region as one change. The boundary on&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+the canvas is then the thing that a reviewer opens.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;The files come from the code first. A code brick with &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;#|export&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; writes a module. Leela therefore knows the module&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+path. &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;paths=&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; adds only what the bricks do not write.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;A list that a person keeps by hand goes out of date. A claim that is out of date is worse than no&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+claim, because a reviewer trusts it.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;b&amp;gt;leela/blocks/canvas/change.py&amp;lt;/b&amp;gt; &amp;amp;middot; Bundle.paths&amp;lt;/figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code class=&amp;quot;lang-python&amp;quot;&amp;gt; @property&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ def paths(self):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ &amp;amp;quot;Files this change owns: what its code exports, then what `paths=` declares.&amp;amp;quot;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ mine = {b.id for b in self.of(&amp;amp;#x27;code&amp;amp;#x27;)}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ one = Canvas(bricks=[b for b in self.doc.bricks if b.id in mine], meta=self.doc.meta)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ return sorted(set(modules(one)) | set(_list(self.brick.attrs.get(&amp;amp;#x27;paths&amp;amp;#x27;))))&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code&amp;gt;coverage&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; holds the claim against the diff. It reports three things. Two of them are new.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code&amp;gt;matched&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; is a file that the bundle claims and the diff changed. &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;unmet&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; is a file that the bundle&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+claims and the diff did not change. &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;unclaimed&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; is a file that the diff changed and no bundle&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+explains.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;No diff tool can find &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;unclaimed&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;. Only the document knows what the change had to be.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;b&amp;gt;leela/blocks/canvas/change.py&amp;lt;/b&amp;gt; &amp;amp;middot; coverage&amp;lt;/figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code class=&amp;quot;lang-python&amp;quot;&amp;gt;def coverage(&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ doc, # the document&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ changed, # paths a diff says moved&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ &amp;amp;quot;What each change claims, what moved, and what nobody claimed.&amp;amp;quot;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ changed, rows, claimed = sorted(changed), [], set()&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ for b in bundles(doc):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ hit = {p for c in b.paths for p in changed if _matches(c, p)}&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ claimed |= hit&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ rows.append({&amp;amp;#x27;id&amp;amp;#x27;: b.id, &amp;amp;#x27;title&amp;amp;#x27;: b.title, &amp;amp;#x27;goal&amp;amp;#x27;: b.goal.id if b.goal else &amp;amp;#x27;&amp;amp;#x27;,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ &amp;amp;#x27;paths&amp;amp;#x27;: b.paths, &amp;amp;#x27;matched&amp;amp;#x27;: sorted(hit),&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ &amp;amp;#x27;unmet&amp;amp;#x27;: [c for c in b.paths if not any(_matches(c, p) for p in changed)],&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ &amp;amp;#x27;tasks_open&amp;amp;#x27;: [t.id for t in b.of(&amp;amp;#x27;task&amp;amp;#x27;)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ if t.attrs.get(&amp;amp;#x27;status&amp;amp;#x27;, &amp;amp;#x27;todo&amp;amp;#x27;) not in (&amp;amp;#x27;done&amp;amp;#x27;,)]})&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ return {&amp;amp;#x27;bundles&amp;amp;#x27;: rows, &amp;amp;#x27;unclaimed&amp;amp;#x27;: [p for p in changed if p not in claimed]}&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;/figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code&amp;gt;pr&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; cuts a pull request from one change. It gives back the title, the branch, the body, the files&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+and the attachments. It opens nothing. Git belongs to &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;gheasy&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;. The forge belongs to &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;pullup&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt;.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;p&amp;gt;The &amp;lt;code&amp;gt;_reasoning&amp;lt;/code&amp;gt; line is the part that a diff never has. Each question inside the change, with the&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+answer that it got, goes into the body in a fold.&amp;lt;/p&amp;gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+&amp;lt;figure&amp;gt;&amp;lt;figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;b&amp;gt;leela/blocks/canvas/change.py&amp;lt;/b&amp;gt; &amp;amp;middot; pr&amp;lt;/figcaption&amp;gt;&amp;lt;details&amp;gt;&amp;lt;summary&amp;gt;pr (23 lines)&amp;lt;/summary&amp;gt;&amp;lt;div class=&amp;quot;in&amp;quot;&amp;gt;&amp;lt;pre&amp;gt;&amp;lt;code class=&amp;quot;lang-python&amp;quot;&amp;gt;def pr(doc, bid, branch=None):&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;dl a&quot;&gt;+ &amp;amp;quot;A pull request cut from one change.
