href=&quot;#the-diff&quot;&gt;The diff&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&quot;#the-numbers&quot;&gt;The numbers&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li&gt;&lt;a href=&quot;#checks&quot;&gt;Checks&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ol&gt;&lt;/nav&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/details&gt;&lt;h2 id=&quot;what-this-is&quot;&gt;What this is&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;This file is the review of one working session, in the format the session built, read by the code</span><span class="dl a">+the session added.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/app.py:page&lt;/code&gt; wrote the page you are reading. It read this file, asked git for</span><span class="dl a">+the diff this file names, and rendered both.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;div class=&quot;card goal&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;stmt&quot;&gt;Give Leela one document that holds a goal, its plan, its research, its code and its questions,</span><span class="dl a">+and one page that shows all five to a reviewer on a phone.&lt;/div&gt;&lt;dl&gt;&lt;dt&gt;measure&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;tools you open to review one session against its goal&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;dt&gt;baseline&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;4: tracker, notebook, diff, deck&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;dt&gt;target&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;1 page&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;dt&gt;by&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;2026-10-31&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;/dl&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;card goal&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;stmt&quot;&gt;Hold every page this branch adds to the English that ste.md already states, and measure it</span><span class="dl a">+rather than assert it.&lt;/div&gt;&lt;dl&gt;&lt;dt&gt;measure&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;slopometer density on the worst page of the branch&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;dt&gt;baseline&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;26.8&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;dt&gt;target&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;under 8&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;dt&gt;by&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;2026-09-30&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;/dl&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;card goal&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;stmt&quot;&gt;Leave nothing in this branch that a reviewer called critical or high.&lt;/div&gt;&lt;dl&gt;&lt;dt&gt;measure&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;findings from a review of this branch that are still open&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;dt&gt;baseline&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;17&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;dt&gt;target&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;0&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;dt&gt;by&lt;/dt&gt;&lt;dd&gt;2026-09-30&lt;/dd&gt;&lt;/dl&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;h2 id=&quot;words&quot;&gt;Words&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;Read this table first. Every later section uses these words and no others.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;table&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;thead&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;tr&gt;&lt;th&gt;word&lt;/th&gt;&lt;th&gt;means&lt;/th&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;/thead&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;tbody&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td&gt;&lt;strong&gt;brick&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td&gt;one part of the document: a fence or a comment wrap. A code cell, a question, a goal, a task, a clipping.&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td&gt;&lt;strong&gt;prose&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td&gt;ordinary markdown between bricks. It carries no markup of its own.&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td&gt;&lt;strong&gt;region&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td&gt;the bricks under one heading. The headings make the regions, so nobody writes one.&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td&gt;&lt;strong&gt;basket&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td&gt;the exact list of bricks that one question sends to the model.&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td&gt;&lt;strong&gt;bundle&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td&gt;one unit of change. It claims a region, names a goal, and owns a list of files.&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td&gt;&lt;strong&gt;snippet&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td&gt;a brick that cites code out of a file. It keeps no copy of that code.&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td&gt;&lt;strong&gt;slot&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td&gt;a &lt;code&gt;diff&lt;/code&gt; brick with no body. It states which diff it wants; Leela fills it.&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td&gt;&lt;strong&gt;library&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td&gt;an installed package of components. &lt;code&gt;leela_bricks&lt;/code&gt; is the first one.&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td&gt;&lt;strong&gt;needs&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td&gt;what a component&#x27;s wiring imports. Read off the code, never written by hand.&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td&gt;&lt;strong&gt;pata&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td&gt;the retired name for this work. Sanskrit for the cloth a scroll painting is made on. The name now is &lt;code&gt;canvas&lt;/code&gt;.&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;/tbody&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;/table&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;h2 id=&quot;why-it-helps&quot;&gt;Why it helps&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;A diff tells a reviewer which lines moved. It cannot answer the three questions a reviewer brings</span><span class="dl a">+to a change.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;ol&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;li&gt;What was this change supposed to do?&lt;/li&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;li&gt;Did it do that?&lt;/li&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;li&gt;Did anything else move that nobody meant to move?&lt;/li&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;/ol&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;p&gt;The intent is in the document, not in the diff. So the document states the intent, the diff states</span><span class="dl a">+the fact, and &lt;code&gt;coverage&lt;/code&gt; compares them. Its &lt;code&gt;unmet&lt;/code&gt; list is a claim with no change behind it, and</span><span class="dl a">+its &lt;code&gt;unclaimed&lt;/code&gt; list is a change with no claim behind it. Neither list can come out of a diff tool,</span><span class="dl a">+which holds one of the two sets.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;p&gt;This page shows that comparison at the top, as chips, before any code.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;div class=&quot;card ask&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;q&quot;&gt;&lt;p&gt;Why can a diff tool not report &lt;code&gt;unclaimed&lt;/code&gt; on its own?&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;a&quot;&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;unclaimed&lt;/code&gt; is the difference between two sets. A diff tool holds the files that moved. It does</span><span class="dl a">+not hold the files a change promised to touch, which sit in each bundle&#x27;s &lt;code&gt;paths&lt;/code&gt;. A finding</span><span class="dl a">+needs both sets.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;h2 id=&quot;the-plan&quot;&gt;The plan&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;ul class=&quot;tasks&quot;&gt;&lt;li class=&quot;done&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;box&quot;&gt;[x]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span&gt;Read the document format from the canvas branch and adopt it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;who&quot;&gt;me&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li class=&quot;done&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;box&quot;&gt;[x]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span&gt;Build the context basket: scope, pins, mutes, budget, and an inspectable result.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;who&quot;&gt;me&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li class=&quot;done&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;box&quot;&gt;[x]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span&gt;Make a boundary on the canvas a unit of change: tasks, prose, code and diff together.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;who&quot;&gt;me&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li class=&quot;done&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;box&quot;&gt;[x]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span&gt;Add the value view: every goal, and every change that serves it.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;who&quot;&gt;me&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li class=&quot;done&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;box&quot;&gt;[x]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span&gt;Write the literate page from the document, in ASD-STE100 English, under ramabana&amp;#x27;s rules.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;who&quot;&gt;me&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li class=&quot;done&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;box&quot;&gt;[x]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span&gt;Resolve a component from an installed library, in Leela, with no second server.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;who&quot;&gt;me&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li class=&quot;done&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;box&quot;&gt;[x]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span&gt;Vendor the brick library as `extensions/bricks`. The package must extract with no code change.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;who&quot;&gt;me&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li class=&quot;done&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;box&quot;&gt;[x]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span&gt;Merge the canvas branch: one `doc.py`, one palette, one editor.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;who&quot;&gt;me&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li class=&quot;done&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;box&quot;&gt;[x]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span&gt;Move the page assembly out of the tool and into Leela.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;who&quot;&gt;me&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li class=&quot;done&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;box&quot;&gt;[x]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span&gt;Score every page with `slopometer`, and rewrite the prose that fails ASD-STE100.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;who&quot;&gt;me&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li class=&quot;done&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;box&quot;&gt;[x]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span&gt;Run `chkstyle` over the branch&amp;#x27;s Python, and cut the imports nothing uses.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;who&quot;&gt;me&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;li class=&quot;done&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;box&quot;&gt;[x]&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span&gt;Get the suite green: 2003 pass, 15 skip, none fail.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;who&quot;&gt;me&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/li&gt;&lt;/ul&gt;&lt;h2 id=&quot;the-document&quot;&gt;The document&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;card change&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;chips&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip done&quot;&gt;done&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;meta&quot;&gt;Worth: the file every other part reads&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;A canvas is a markdown file. Prose stays prose. A brick is a fence or a comment wrap. Every</span><span class="dl a">+markdown reader therefore shows the file, and git shows a useful diff. The &lt;code&gt;ast&lt;/code&gt; module reads the dataflow</span><span class="dl a">+between code bricks off the code itself.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;div class=&quot;chips&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/example.py&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/export.py&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/layout.py&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/ops.py&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;chips&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;doc:docs/canvas.md&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;file:leela/blocks/nb/nb.py&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Two brick shapes, and the shape follows the content. Code goes in a fence, because a fence is how</span><span class="dl a">+markdown holds code. A goal or a task goes in a comment wrap, because a reader should see the</span><span class="dl a">+words and not the markup.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;p&gt;A fence holds what markdown already knows how to show, so a code cell stays a code block. A</span><span class="dl a">+comment wrap holds what a reader should read as prose, so a goal shows its words and not its</span><span class="dl a">+markup. &lt;code&gt;KINDS&lt;/code&gt; is the whole vocabulary, and a document with a word outside it does not parse.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;figure&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;b&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py&lt;/b&gt; &amp;middot; 12-15&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&quot;lang-python&quot;&gt;FENCED = (&amp;#x27;code&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;ask&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;brick&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;sim&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;data&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;diff&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;snippet&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;pdf&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;video&amp;#x27;)</span><span class="dl a">+#: Bricks whose body is markdown a plain renderer should still show, written as a comment wrap.</span><span class="dl a">+WRAPPED = (&amp;#x27;reply&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;note&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;quiz&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;goal&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;task&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;source&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;bundle&amp;#x27;)</span><span class="dl a">+KINDS = (&amp;#x27;text&amp;#x27;,) + FENCED + WRAPPED&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;order&lt;/code&gt; reads the graph rather than storing it. &lt;code&gt;defs_of&lt;/code&gt; asks the code what it defines, and</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;code&gt;reads_of&lt;/code&gt; asks what it reads. &lt;code&gt;order&lt;/code&gt; joins two bricks when one defines what the other reads.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;order&lt;/code&gt; reads the dependency from the code. &lt;code&gt;_owners&lt;/code&gt; says which brick defines each name, and</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;code&gt;b.reads&lt;/code&gt; says which names a brick needs, so no person draws an edge. On a cycle the visit stops</span><span class="dl a">+and the document order stands, so a plan with a loop in it still opens.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;figure&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;b&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py&lt;/b&gt; &amp;middot; order&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&quot;lang-python&quot;&gt;def order(bricks):</span><span class="dl a">+ &amp;quot;Runnable bricks in dependency order, falling back to document order on a cycle.&amp;quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ live = L(bricks).filter(lambda b: b.runs)</span><span class="dl a">+ owner = _owners(live)</span><span class="dl a">+ need = {b.id: {owner[n] for n in b.reads if n in owner and owner[n] != b.id} for b in live}</span><span class="dl a">+ out, seen = [], set()</span><span class="dl a">+ def visit(b, path):</span><span class="dl a">+ if b.id in seen or b.id in path: return</span><span class="dl a">+ for dep in need[b.id]: visit(first(x for x in live if x.id == dep), path | {b.id})</span><span class="dl a">+ seen.add(b.id); out.append(b)</span><span class="dl a">+ for b in live: visit(b, set())</span><span class="dl a">+ return L(out)&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;h2 id=&quot;the-basket&quot;&gt;The basket&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;card change&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;chips&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip done&quot;&gt;done&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;meta&quot;&gt;Worth: what a question in the document may read&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;A question names its own scope, its pins and its budget. &lt;code&gt;resolve&lt;/code&gt; returns the exact bricks, and each one</span><span class="dl a">+carries the reason it is there. &lt;code&gt;render&lt;/code&gt; emits the cells that ramabana&#x27;s &lt;code&gt;compact_notebook_context&lt;/code&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+already knows how to shed.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;div class=&quot;chips&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/context.py&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;chips&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;pkg:ramabana&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;file:leela/blocks/nb/nb.py&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;A notebook sends every brick above the question. A pin sends the two that matter, wherever they</span><span class="dl a">+sit. An audit belongs to the question at the top of the page and the one at the bottom, and to</span><span class="dl a">+nothing between.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;p&gt;A question states its own rule, and the rule is four fields. &lt;code&gt;scope&lt;/code&gt; gathers the first set, &lt;code&gt;pins&lt;/code&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+add what the scope missed, and &lt;code&gt;mutes&lt;/code&gt; remove what it caught. An unknown scope becomes &lt;code&gt;page&lt;/code&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+rather than an error, so a typed attribute cannot stop a document from opening.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;figure&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;b&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/context.py&lt;/b&gt; &amp;middot; Spec&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&quot;lang-python&quot;&gt;@dataclass</span><span class="dl a">+class Spec:</span><span class="dl a">+ &amp;quot;A question&amp;#x27;s context rule, written on the brick as attributes and `pin`/`mute` directives.&amp;quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ scope: str = &amp;#x27;page&amp;#x27;</span><span class="dl a">+ pins: list = field(default_factory=list)</span><span class="dl a">+ mutes: list = field(default_factory=list)</span><span class="dl a">+ budget: int | None = None</span><span class="dl a">+ goal: bool = True</span><span class="dl a">+ def __post_init__(self):</span><span class="dl a">+ if self.scope not in SCOPES: self.scope = &amp;#x27;page&amp;#x27;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;card note&quot;&gt;&lt;p&gt;The budget sheds the least useful brick first, not the oldest, and never a pin or the goal. Each</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;code&gt;Item&lt;/code&gt; carries the &lt;code&gt;why&lt;/code&gt; that put it there. A reviewer can therefore see which bricks the budget</span><span class="dl a">+dropped.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;/div&gt;&lt;h2 id=&quot;the-change&quot;&gt;The change&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;card change&quot;&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;chips&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip done&quot;&gt;done&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;meta&quot;&gt;Worth: all of the review step&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;A bundle claims a region, names a goal and owns a list of files. &lt;code&gt;coverage&lt;/code&gt; compares the claim</span><span class="dl a">+with the diff. Leela reads &lt;code&gt;state&lt;/code&gt; off the document, and no one sets it by hand. &lt;code&gt;review&lt;/code&gt;, &lt;code&gt;value&lt;/code&gt; and &lt;code&gt;pr&lt;/code&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+are three views over the same file.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;div class=&quot;chips&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;README.md&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;docs/README.md&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;docs/blocks.md&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;docs/canvas.md&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;docs/change.canvas.md&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;docs/dynamic-documents.md&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;docs/session.canvas.md&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/change.py&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/lit.css&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/lit.py&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;media/*.md&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;media/canvas-*.html&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;tools/canvas_spike.py&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;tools/make_change_page.py&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div class=&quot;chips&quot;&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;doc:docs/change.canvas.md&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;pkg:mdhtml&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span class=&quot;chip&quot;&gt;pkg:gheasy&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;p&gt;Leela derives the state of a change. A bundle reaches &lt;code&gt;done&lt;/code&gt; once every task reaches &lt;code&gt;done&lt;/code&gt; and</span><span class="dl a">+every claimed file moved. No one writes that word into the file.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;state&lt;/code&gt; reads the word off the document. One blocked task blocks the change, and every task done</span><span class="dl a">+with every claimed file moved makes it done. &lt;code&gt;files_ok&lt;/code&gt; treats an absent diff as no evidence, so a</span><span class="dl a">+change nobody has diffed yet does not read as work not started.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;figure&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;b&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/change.py&lt;/b&gt; &amp;middot; state&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&quot;lang-python&quot;&gt;def state(</span><span class="dl a">+ b, # the `Bundle`</span><span class="dl a">+ changed=(), # paths a diff says moved, else no evidence about files</span><span class="dl a">+):</span><span class="dl a">+ &amp;quot;Where one change stands, read off the document.&amp;quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ st = [t.attrs.get(&amp;#x27;status&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;todo&amp;#x27;) for t in b.of(&amp;#x27;task&amp;#x27;)]</span><span class="dl a">+ hit = {p for c in b.paths for p in changed if _matches(c, p)}</span><span class="dl a">+ unmet = [c for c in b.paths if not any(_matches(c, p) for p in changed)]</span><span class="dl a">+ files_ok = not changed or not b.paths or not unmet</span><span class="dl a">+ if &amp;#x27;blocked&amp;#x27; in st: return &amp;#x27;blocked&amp;#x27;</span><span class="dl a">+ if st and all(x == &amp;#x27;done&amp;#x27; for x in st) and files_ok: return &amp;#x27;done&amp;#x27;</span><span class="dl a">+ if &amp;#x27;doing&amp;#x27; in st or &amp;#x27;done&amp;#x27; in st or hit: return &amp;#x27;doing&amp;#x27;</span><span class="dl a">+ return &amp;#x27;todo&amp;#x27;&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;p&gt;The comparison a diff tool cannot make:&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;matched&lt;/code&gt; is a claim the diff confirms, &lt;code&gt;unmet&lt;/code&gt; is a claim with nothing behind it, and &lt;code&gt;unclaimed&lt;/code&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+is a file that moved with no claim on it. A claim is a glob, so &lt;code&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/*&lt;/code&gt; covers</span><span class="dl a">+every file the change touched in that folder without naming one of them.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;figure&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;b&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/change.py&lt;/b&gt; &amp;middot; coverage&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&quot;lang-python&quot;&gt;def coverage(</span><span class="dl a">+ doc, # the document</span><span class="dl a">+ changed, # paths a diff says moved</span><span class="dl a">+):</span><span class="dl a">+ &amp;quot;What each change claims, what moved, and what nobody claimed.&amp;quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ changed, rows, claimed = sorted(changed), [], set()</span><span class="dl a">+ for b in bundles(doc):</span><span class="dl a">+ hit = {p for c in b.paths for p in changed if _matches(c, p)}</span><span class="dl a">+ claimed |= hit</span><span class="dl a">+ rows.append({&amp;#x27;id&amp;#x27;: b.id, &amp;#x27;title&amp;#x27;: b.title, &amp;#x27;goal&amp;#x27;: b.goal.id if b.goal else &amp;#x27;&amp;#x27;,</span><span class="dl a">+ &amp;#x27;paths&amp;#x27;: b.paths, &amp;#x27;matched&amp;#x27;: sorted(hit),</span><span class="dl a">+ &amp;#x27;unmet&amp;#x27;: [c for c in b.paths if not any(_matches(c, p) for p in changed)],</span><span class="dl a">+ &amp;#x27;tasks_open&amp;#x27;: [t.id for t in b.of(&amp;#x27;task&amp;#x27;)</span><span class="dl a">+ if t.attrs.get(&amp;#x27;status&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;todo&amp;#x27;) not in (&amp;#x27;done&amp;#x27;,)]})</span><span class="dl a">+ return {&amp;#x27;bundles&amp;#x27;: rows, &amp;#x27;unclaimed&amp;#x27;: [p for p in changed if p not in claimed]}&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;h2 id=&quot;the-page&quot;&gt;The page&lt;/h2&gt;&lt;p&gt;Leela now assembles this page. The tool that used to do it picks a file and prints a line.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;page&lt;/code&gt; fills the slots, counts the files and writes the HTML in one call. Every snippet is read from the &amp;#x27;</span><span class="dl a">+ &amp;#x27;file it names.&amp;#x27;)</span><span class="dl a">+ out = lit(doc, dest, changed=changed, root=root, subtitle=sub)</span><span class="dl a">+ return {&amp;#x27;path&amp;#x27;: str(out), &amp;#x27;changed&amp;#x27;: changed,</span><span class="dl a">+ &amp;#x27;unclaimed&amp;#x27;: coverage(doc, changed)[&amp;#x27;unclaimed&amp;#x27;],</span><span class="dl a">+ &amp;#x27;diffs&amp;#x27;: [b.id for b in doc.of(&amp;#x27;diff&amp;#x27;)]}&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;p&gt;A &lt;code&gt;diff&lt;/code&gt; brick with no body is a slot. It says which paths it wants and which two commits to</span><span class="dl a">+compare. &lt;code&gt;place_diff&lt;/code&gt; calls git once per slot and replaces the slot with one brick a file. &lt;code&gt;place_diff&lt;/code&gt; marks a brick</span><span class="dl a">+no bundle claims, and the page shows a warning on it.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;p&gt;&lt;code&gt;place_diff&lt;/code&gt; reads the request off the brick. One brick per file.&amp;quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ for slot in doc.of(&amp;#x27;diff&amp;#x27;).filter(lambda b: not b.body.strip()):</span><span class="dl a">+ at = doc.index(slot.id)</span><span class="dl a">+ if at is None: continue</span><span class="dl a">+ doc.bricks.pop(at)</span><span class="dl a">+ raw = get(_list(slot.attrs.get(&amp;#x27;paths&amp;#x27;)), slot.attrs.get(&amp;#x27;left&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;&amp;#x27;),</span><span class="dl a">+ slot.attrs.get(&amp;#x27;right&amp;#x27;, &amp;#x27;&amp;#x27;))</span><span class="dl a">+ made = []</span><span class="dl a">+ for n, (path, text) in enumerate(hunks(raw).items()):</span><span class="dl a">+ add, rm = diff_stat(text)</span><span class="dl a">+ made.append(Brick(&amp;#x27;diff&amp;#x27;, text, id=f&amp;#x27;{slot.id}-{Path(path).name}&amp;#x27;,</span><span class="dl a">+ attrs={&amp;#x27;path&amp;#x27;: path, &amp;#x27;added&amp;#x27;: str(add), &amp;#x27;removed&amp;#x27;: str(rm)}))</span><span class="dl a">+ doc.bricks.insert(at + n, made[-1])</span><span class="dl a">+ loose = set(coverage(doc, [b.attrs[&amp;#x27;path&amp;#x27;] for b in made])[&amp;#x27;unclaimed&amp;#x27;])</span><span class="dl a">+ for b in made:</span><span class="dl a">+ if b.attrs[&amp;#x27;path&amp;#x27;] in loose: b.attrs[&amp;#x27;claimed&amp;#x27;] = &amp;#x27;no&amp;#x27;</span><span class="dl a">+ return doc._regions()&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;p&gt;The page folds anything longer than a phone screen. A diff body scrolls sideways inside its own</span><span class="dl a">+box, and a long line therefore never widens the page.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;p&gt;The renderer folds a diff longer than a phone screen, and the summary still names the file and the</span><span class="dl a">+counts. It drops the git headers a reader does not need. It writes no script, so the fold is</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;code&gt;&amp;lt;details&amp;gt;&lt;/code&gt; and the page works with JavaScript turned off.&lt;/p&gt;</span><span class="dl a">+&lt;figure&gt;&lt;figcaption&gt;&lt;b&gt;leela/blocks/canvas/lit.py&lt;/b&gt; &amp;middot; _diff&lt;/figcaption&gt;&lt;pre&gt;&lt;code class=&quot;lang-python&quot;&gt;def _diff(b):</span><span class="dl a">+ rows = [l for l in b.body.split(&amp;#x27;\n&amp;#x27;) if not l.startswith(_SKIP)]</span><span class="dl a">+ body = &amp;#x27;&amp;#x27;.join(_dline(l) for l in rows[:DIFF_CAP])</span><span class="dl a">+ if (over := len(rows) - DIFF_CAP) &amp;gt; 0: body += f&amp;#x27;&amp;lt;span class=&amp;quot;dl cut&amp;quot;&amp;gt;{over} more lines, not shown&amp;lt;/span&amp;gt;&amp;#x27;</span><span class="dl a">+ add, rm = diff_stat(b.body)</span><span class="dl a">+ chips = (f&amp;#x27;&amp;lt;span class=&amp;quot;chip add&amp;quot;&amp;gt;+{add}&amp;lt;/span&amp;gt;&amp;lt;span class=&amp;quot;chip rm&amp;quot;&amp;gt;-{rm}&amp;lt;/span&amp;gt;&amp;#x27;</span><span class="dl a">+ + (&amp;#x27;&amp;lt;span class=&amp;quot;chip warn&amp;quot;&amp;gt;no bundle claims this&amp;lt;/span&amp;gt;&amp;#x27;</span><span class="dl a">+ if b.attrs.get(&amp;#x27;claimed&amp;#x27;) == &amp;#x27;no&amp;#x27; This package holds no copy of them.&amp;quot;</span><span class="dl a">+ try: from shalya.skills import discover, find</span><span class="dl a">+ except ImportError as e:</span><span class="dl a">+ raise LookupError(&amp;#x27;shalya is not installed, so the skills cannot be read; pass `rules=`&amp;#x27;) from e</span><span class="dl a">+ found = discover()</span><span class="dl a">+ out = []</span><span class="dl a">+ for n in names:</span><span class="dl a">+ s = find(found, n)</span><span class="dl a">+ if s is None: raise LookupError(f&amp;#x27;skill {n!r} is not installed; pass `rules=` instead&amp;#x27;)</span><span class="dl a">+ out.append(f&amp;#x27;## {s.name}\n\n{s.text()}&amp;#x27;)</span><span class="dl a">+ return &amp;#x27;\n\n&amp;#x27;.join(out)&lt;/code&gt;&lt;/pre&gt;&lt;/figure&gt;&lt;p&gt;A brick the model drafted carries &lt;code&gt;wrote=ai&lt;/code&gt; in the file. &lt;code&gt;git diff&lt;/code&gt; therefore shows the drafting,</span><span class="dl a">+and a reviewer can read those bricks first. literate diff</div><h1>The canvas document: a goal, its plan and its changes in one file</h1><div class="chips"><span class="chip done">canvas done</span><span class="chip warn">81 file(s) claimed by nobody</span></div></div></header><div class="wrap"><details><summary>Contents</summary><div class="in"><nav><ol><li><a href="#what-this-is">What this is</a></li><li><a href="#words">Words</a></li><li><a href="#why-it-helps">Why it helps</a></li><li><a href="#the-file">The file</a></li><li><a href="#the-basket">The basket</a></li><li><a href="#the-wiring">The wiring</a></li><li><a href="#the-change">The change</a></li><li><a href="#the-value">The value</a></li><li><a href="#the-prompts">The prompts</a></li><li><a href="#this-page">This page</a></li><li><a href="#the-numbers">The numbers</a></li><li><a href="#checks">Checks</a></li><li><a href="#not-done">Not done</a></li></ol></nav></div></details><h2 id="what-this-is">What this is</h2><p>A goal like "increase procurement productivity by 10%" is not one kind of work. You frame the+measure. You collect what people already know. You pull an extract apart. You prototype one rule.+You write the recommendation.</p>+<p>Today each of those lives in a different tool. The plan is in a tracker. The numbers are in a+notebook. The research is in browser tabs. The recommendation is in a deck. Nothing crosses+between them except a person who remembers all four.</p>+<p>One file now holds every one of the four. It is a markdown file. Prose stays prose, and each+other part is a brick.</p>+<div class="card goal"><div class="stmt">Give Leela one document that holds a goal, its plan, its research, its code and its questions.</div><dl><dt>measure</dt><dd>tools you open to review one change against its goal</dd><dt>baseline</dt><dd>4: tracker, notebook, diff, deck</dd><dt>target</dt><dd>1 page</dd><dt>by</dt><dd>2026-10-31</dd></dl></div><div class="card change"><div class="chips"><span class="chip done">done</span></div><div class="meta">Worth: all of the review step; none of the run step, which the canvas branch owns</div><p>Adds <code>leela/blocks/canvas</code>, a block that reads and writes the canvas document. A question in the+document names what the model may read. A boundary on the canvas is one change. A change names the+goal that it serves.</p>+<div class="chips"><span class="chip">docs/*.md</span><span class="chip">leela/blocks/__init__.py</span><span class="chip">leela/blocks/canvas/*</span><span class="chip">media/*</span><span class="chip">tests/routes.txt</span><span class="chip">tests/test_canvas_doc.py</span><span class="chip">tools/make_change_page.py</span></div><div class="chips"><span class="chip">doc:docs/dynamic-documents.md</span><span class="chip">file:leela/blocks/nb/nb.py</span><span class="chip">pkg:mdhtml</span></div></div><ul class="tasks"><li class="done"><span class="box">[x]</span><span>Read the document format from the canvas branch.</span><span class="who">me</span></li><li class="done"><span class="box">[x]</span><span>Build the context basket, the change bundle, the review and the value view.</span><span class="who">me</span></li><li class="done"><span class="box">[x]</span><span>Write this page from the document, with the code it explains.</span><span class="who">me</span></li><li class="done"><span class="box">[x]</span><span>Move the modules into `leela/blocks/canvas/`.</span><span class="who">me</span></li></ul><h2 id="words">Words</h2><p>Read this table first. Every later section uses these words and no others.</p>+<table>+<thead>+<tr><th>word</th><th>means</th></tr>+</thead>+<tbody>+<tr><td><strong>brick</strong></td><td>one part of the document. A fence or a comment wrap. A code cell, a question, a goal, a task, a clipping.</td></tr>+<tr><td><strong>prose</strong></td><td>ordinary markdown between bricks. It needs no markup of its own.</td></tr>+<tr><td><strong>region</strong></td><td>the bricks under one heading. The headings make the regions, so nobody writes one.</td></tr>+<tr><td><strong>basket</strong></td><td>the exact list of bricks that one question sends to the model.</td></tr>+<tr><td><strong>scope</strong></td><td>how a question gathers its first set of bricks. <code>page</code>, <code>region</code>, <code>upstream</code>, <code>doc</code> or <code>none</code>.</td></tr>+<tr><td><strong>pin</strong></td><td>a brick a question always reads, whatever the scope says. A <code>mute</code> is the opposite.</td></tr>+<tr><td><strong>budget</strong></td><td>how many characters a question may send. The goal and the pins survive it.</td></tr>+<tr><td><strong>upstream</strong></td><td>the bricks a brick reads from. Read off the code, never drawn by hand.</td></tr>+<tr><td><strong>bundle</strong></td><td>one unit of change. It claims a region, names a goal, and owns a list of files.</td></tr>+<tr><td><strong>snippet</strong></td><td>a brick that cites code out of a file. It holds no copy of that code.</td></tr>+<tr><td><strong>canvas</strong></td><td>the second view of the document. The same bricks, with coordinates.</td></tr>+</tbody>+</table>+<p>The block is <code>canvas</code> and the file is <code>*.canvas.md</code>. An earlier draft of this work was a separate+package called <code>pata</code>, from the Sanskrit <code>pata</code>, the cloth a painter paints a scroll on. That+name is gone, and <code>canvas</code> is the only name now.</p>+<h2 id="why-it-helps">Why it helps</h2><p>A notebook picks context by position: every cell above the question. That is right for a script,+where the cells above are the steps you took. A plan holds four lines of work at once. Position therefore hands the recommendation question+three failed attempts at a groupby. The alternative is to turn it off and paste the same+paragraphs again.</p>+<p>An audit shows the limit. It belongs to the question near the top of the document and to the risk+question near the bottom, and to nothing between them. Where a brick sits says nothing about which+questions it answers.</p>+<p>A document that can say it gives three things.</p>+<p>A question shows its basket before it runs: each brick, why it is there, and what it costs. Mute+one and the count drops.</p>+<p>A boundary on the canvas is a change you can review. It names the goal, owns the files, and holds+the tasks, the prose and the code together. One page therefore answers whether the change does+what the goal said.</p>+<p>A goal shows what serves it, and shows a goal that nothing serves. The second is the worse finding,+because it looks like a goal that is going well.</p>+<h2 id="the-file">The file</h2><p>A <code>pata</code> document is one markdown file. Prose stays prose. Each other part is a brick. A brick is+a fence or a comment wrap.</p>+<p>The reader reads the file line by line. It does not use one pattern on the whole file. This is+necessary. A document about canvases shows fences as examples. A fence inside a longer fence is an+example. It is not a brick.</p>+<p>The <code>TICKS</code> branch does the work. It sees a plain fence, puts the fence into the prose, and skips+to the end of it. Nothing inside that fence becomes a brick. This page is such a document, and it+reads correctly.</p>+<figure><figcaption><b>leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py</b> &middot; _scan</figcaption><details><summary>_scan (36 lines)</summary><div class="in"><pre><code class="lang-python">def _scan(text):+ &quot;`(kind, attrline, body)` per brick. A fence inside a longer fence is an example of one, not one.&quot;+ lines, i, prose, out = text.split(&#x27;\n&#x27;), 0, [], []+ def flush():+ for part in _prose_parts(&#x27;\n&#x27;.join(prose)): out.append((&#x27;text&#x27;, &#x27;&#x27;, part))+ prose.clear()+ def upto(j, shut, keep):+ body = []+ while j &lt; len(lines) and not shut(lines[j]): body.append(lines[j]); j += 1+ if keep and j &lt; len(lines): body.append(lines[j])+ return j, body+ while i &lt; len(lines):+ line = lines[i]+ if (m := FENCE.match(line)):+ flush()+ end = _shut(m[1])+ i, body = upto(i + 1, lambda l: end.match(l), False)+ out.append((m[2], m[3], &#x27;\n&#x27;.join(body) + (&#x27;\n&#x27; if body else &#x27;&#x27;)))+ elif (m := TICKS.match(line)):+ end = _shut(m[1])+ prose.append(line)+ i, body = upto(i + 1, lambda l: end.match(l), True)+ prose.extend(body)+ elif (m := WRAP.match(line)):+ flush()+ attr = [line[m.end():]]+ while not SHUT_TAG.search(attr[-1]) and i + 1 &lt; len(lines): # a long attribute list wraps+ i += 1+ attr.append(lines[i])+ i, body = upto(i + 1, lambda l: l.strip() == SHUT, False)+ out.append((m[1], SHUT_TAG.sub(&#x27;&#x27;, &#x27; &#x27;.join(attr)), &#x27;\n&#x27;.join(body) + (&#x27;\n&#x27; if body else &#x27;&#x27;)))+ else:+ prose.append(line); i += 1; continue+ i += 1+ flush()+ return out</code></pre></div></details></figure><p>Headings are the regions of the document. Nobody writes a region. The reader gives each brick the+heading above it.</p>+<figure><figcaption><b>leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py</b> &middot; Doc._regions</figcaption><pre><code class="lang-python"></code></pre></figure><h2 id="the-basket">The basket</h2><p>Each question carries a rule. The rule says what the question may read. <code>resolve</code> turns the rule+into the exact list that the turn will send.</p>+<p>The list is the point. <code>resolve</code> gives back items, not one string. The same list draws the panel+and builds the prompt. What a person sees is what the model gets.</p>+<p>Four rules, in order. The goal goes in first. Then each pin. A pin that no longer exists becomes a+<code>missing</code> item. It is visible. A silent drop is worse, because the person still believes the pin is+there.</p>+<figure><figcaption><b>leela/blocks/canvas/context.py</b> &middot; resolve</figcaption><details><summary>resolve (29 lines)</summary><div class="in"><pre><code class="lang-python">def resolve(+ doc, # the document+ bid, # which brick asks+ spec=None, # the rule, else the one the brick carries+ values=None, # `{brick id: output text}` from the live namespace+ lookup=None, # `lookup(ref)` for a pin the document does not own+ extra=(), # items the host adds, such as live variables+):+ &quot;The exact basket for question `bid`, in the order the model reads it.&quot;+ b = doc.by_id(bid)+ if b is None: raise KeyError(bid)+ spec = spec or spec_of(b)+ mutes, items, seen = set(spec.mutes), [], {b.id}+ def take(x, why, pinned=False):+ if x.id in seen or x.id in mutes: return+ if not (t := body_text(x, values, doc)).strip(): return+ seen.add(x.id)+ items.append(Item(ref=x.id, kind=x.kind, label=_label(x), text=t, why=why,+ region=x.region, mode=x.mode, pinned=pinned or x.mode == &#x27;keep&#x27;))+ if spec.goal and (g := doc.goal_for(bid)) is not None and g.id not in mutes: take(g, &#x27;goal&#x27;, True)+ for r in spec.pins:+ if r in mutes: continue+ if _is_ref(r): items.append(_ref_item(r, lookup))+ elif (x := doc.by_id(r)) is not None: take(x, &#x27;pin&#x27;, True)+ else: items.append(Item(ref=r, kind=&#x27;missing&#x27;, label=r, text=&#x27;&#x27;, why=&#x27;pin&#x27;, pinned=True,+ clipped=True))+ for x in members(doc, b, spec.scope): take(x, spec.scope)+ items += list(extra)+ return _fit(items, spec.budget)</code></pre></div></details></figure><p>A scope gives the first set of bricks. <code>page</code> is the notebook rule. <code>region</code> is the section that+you work in. <code>upstream</code> is what the question reads from.</p>+<figure><figcaption><b>leela/blocks/canvas/context.py</b> &middot; members</figcaption><pre><code class="lang-python">def members(doc, b, scope):+ &quot;The bricks a scope offers, before pins, mutes and the budget.&quot;+ if scope == &#x27;none&#x27;: return L()+ at = doc.index(b.id)+ if at is None: at = len(doc)+ if scope == &#x27;page&#x27;: return L(doc.bricks[:at])+ if scope == &#x27;doc&#x27;: return L(x for x in doc.bricks if x.id != b.id)+ if scope == &#x27;region&#x27;: return L(x for x in doc.in_region(b.region) if x.id != b.id)+ return upstream(doc.bricks, b.id)</code></pre></figure><p>The budget cuts the list. Two rules must hold. The goal and the pins stay. A pin that is larger+than the whole budget gets shorter; it does not go.</p>+<p>The last block is the one that matters. If every item that is left is pinned, the code cuts each+item to a share of the budget and marks it. It never drops a pin.</p>+<figure><figcaption><b>leela/blocks/canvas/context.py</b> &middot; _fit</figcaption><pre><code class="lang-python">def _fit(items, budget):+ &quot;Trim to `budget`. Pins and `keep` never drop; `discard` goes first, then the oldest `auto`.&quot;+ if not budget: return items+ total = sum(i.chars + WRAP for i in items)+ if total &lt;= budget: return items+ order = sorted((i for i, it in enumerate(items) if not it.pinned),+ key=lambda i: (items[i].mode != &#x27;discard&#x27;, i))+ drop, n = set(), 0+ while total &gt; budget and n &lt; len(order):+ total -= items[order[n]].chars + WRAP+ drop.add(order[n])+ n += 1+ kept = [it for i, it in enumerate(items) if i not in drop]+ if sum(i.chars + WRAP for i in kept) &gt; budget and kept:+ share = max(200, budget // max(1, len(kept)) - WRAP)+ kept = [replace(it, text=it.text[:share] + &#x27;\n…&#x27;, clipped=True) if it.chars &gt; share else it+ for it in kept]+ return kept</code></pre></figure><p>The markup is <code>&lt;cell&gt;</code> with a <code>compact</code> attribute. This is Leela's own notebook shape, and the+choice is deliberate. Ramabana drops <code>&lt;cell&gt;</code> elements when a prompt is too large for the window.+A document that wrote <code>&lt;block&gt;</code> would lose that net.</p>+<figure><figcaption><b>leela/blocks/canvas/context.py</b> &middot; render</figcaption><pre><code class="lang-python">def render(items, doc=None):+ &quot;The basket as `&lt;cell&gt;` markup, which is Leela’s own notebook context shape.&quot;+ out = []+ for it in items:+ if not it.text.strip(): continue+ attr = (f&#x27;id=&quot;{it.ref}&quot; type=&quot;{it.kind}&quot; compact=&quot;{&quot;keep&quot; if it.pinned else &quot;auto&quot;}&quot; &#x27;+ f&#x27;why=&quot;{it.why}&quot;&#x27;)+ if it.region: attr += f&#x27; region=&quot;{it.region}&quot;&#x27;+ if it.clipped: attr += &#x27; clipped=&quot;true&quot;&#x27;+ out.append(f&#x27;&lt;cell {attr}&gt;\n{it.text}\n&lt;/cell&gt;&#x27;)+ if doc is not None and (links := _links(doc, {i.ref for i in items if i.text.strip()})):+ out.append(&#x27;&lt;links&gt;\n&#x27; + &#x27;\n&#x27;.join(links) + &#x27;\n&lt;/links&gt;&#x27;)+ return &#x27;\n&#x27;.join(out)</code></pre></figure><h2 id="the-wiring">The wiring</h2><p><code>upstream</code> reads the code. It does not read a diagram. A name belongs to the brick that binds it.+A diagram beside the code goes wrong; the code does not.</p>+<p><code>defs_of</code> finds each name that a cell binds at the top level of its code. It looks inside <code>if</code>,+<code>for</code>, <code>try</code> and <code>with</code>. It does not look inside a <code>def</code>, because a name in a function belongs to+the function.</p>+<figure><figcaption><b>leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py</b> &middot; defs_of</figcaption><pre><code class="lang-python">def defs_of(source):+ &quot;Names a code brick binds at module level, however it binds them.&quot;+ t = _walk(source)+ if t is None: return L()+ out = L()+ for n in _module_body(t):+ if isinstance(n, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.ClassDef)): out.append(n.name)+ elif isinstance(n, ast.Assign): out += L(n.targets).map(_targets).concat()+ elif isinstance(n, (ast.AnnAssign, ast.AugAssign)): out += _targets(n.target)+ elif isinstance(n, (ast.For, ast.AsyncFor)): out += _targets(n.target)+ elif isinstance(n, (ast.With, ast.AsyncWith)):+ out += L(n.items).map(lambda i: _targets(i.optional_vars)).concat()+ elif isinstance(n, (ast.Import, ast.ImportFrom)):+ out += L(n.names).map(lambda a: (a.asname or a.name).split(&#x27;.&#x27;)[0])+ for n in ast.walk(t):+ if isinstance(n, ast.NamedExpr): out += _targets(n.target)+ return out.unique()</code></pre></figure><p>Three additions reach where the code cannot see.</p>+<p>A question anchors on the brick above it. "Fix that" means that brick and all that it reads.</p>+<p>A name in backticks is a name that the question reads. Write <code>`triage`</code> and the brick that+defines <code>triage</code> goes in.</p>+<p><code>supports=</code>, <code>refutes=</code> and <code>blocks=</code> state a relation between two bricks. No code states these.</p>+<figure><figcaption><b>leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py</b> &middot; upstream</figcaption><pre><code class="lang-python">def upstream(bricks, bid, depth=12):+ &quot;Every brick `bid` reads from, transitively, in document order.&quot;+ bricks = L(bricks)+ owner, seen = _owners(bricks), set()+ want = {bid} | ({a} if (a := anchor_of(bricks, bid)) else set())+ seen |= want - {bid}+ for _ in range(depth):+ nxt = set()+ for b in bricks.filter(lambda b: b.id in want):+ nxt |= {owner[n] for n in b.reads if n in owner}+ for ids in b.links.values(): nxt |= set(ids)+ nxt -= seen | {bid}+ if not nxt: break+ seen |= nxt+ want = nxt+ seen |= {b.id for b in bricks if bid in {i for ids in b.links.values() for i in ids}}+ return bricks.filter(lambda b: b.id in seen - {bid})</code></pre></figure><h2 id="the-change">The change</h2><p>A region groups bricks to read. A <code>bundle</code> brick claims its region as one change. The boundary on+the canvas is then the thing that a reviewer opens.</p>+<p>The files come from the code first. A code brick with <code>#|export</code> writes a module. Leela therefore knows the module+path. <code>paths=</code> adds only what the bricks do not write.</p>+<p>A list that a person keeps by hand goes out of date. A claim that is out of date is worse than no+claim, because a reviewer trusts it.</p>+<figure><figcaption><b>leela/blocks/canvas/change.py</b> &middot; Bundle.paths</figcaption><pre><code class="lang-python"> @property+ def paths(self):+ &quot;Files this change owns: what its code exports, then what `paths=` declares.&quot;+ mine = {b.id for b in self.of(&#x27;code&#x27;)}+ one = Canvas(bricks=[b for b in self.doc.bricks if b.id in mine], meta=self.doc.meta)+ return sorted(set(modules(one)) | set(_list(self.brick.attrs.get(&#x27;paths&#x27;))))</code></pre></figure><p><code>coverage</code> holds the claim against the diff. It reports three things. Two of them are new.</p>+<p><code>matched</code> is a file that the bundle claims and the diff changed. <code>unmet</code> is a file that the bundle+claims and the diff did not change. <code>unclaimed</code> is a file that the diff changed and no bundle+explains.</p>+<p>No diff tool can find <code>unclaimed</code>. Only the document knows what the change had to be.</p>+<figure><figcaption><b>leela/blocks/canvas/change.py</b> &middot; coverage</figcaption><pre><code class="lang-python">def coverage(+ doc, # the document+ changed, # paths a diff says moved+):+ &quot;What each change claims, what moved, and what nobody claimed.&quot;+ changed, rows, claimed = sorted(changed), [], set()+ for b in bundles(doc):+ hit = {p for c in b.paths for p in changed if _matches(c, p)}+ claimed |= hit+ rows.append({&#x27;id&#x27;: b.id, &#x27;title&#x27;: b.title, &#x27;goal&#x27;: b.goal.id if b.goal else &#x27;&#x27;,+ &#x27;paths&#x27;: b.paths, &#x27;matched&#x27;: sorted(hit),+ &#x27;unmet&#x27;: [c for c in b.paths if not any(_matches(c, p) for p in changed)],+ &#x27;tasks_open&#x27;: [t.id for t in b.of(&#x27;task&#x27;)+ if t.attrs.get(&#x27;status&#x27;, &#x27;todo&#x27;) not in (&#x27;done&#x27;,)]})+ return {&#x27;bundles&#x27;: rows, &#x27;unclaimed&#x27;: [p for p in changed if p not in claimed]}</code></pre></figure><p><code>pr</code> cuts a pull request from one change. It gives back the title, the branch, the body, the files+and the attachments. It opens nothing. Git belongs to <code>gheasy</code>. The forge belongs to <code>pullup</code>.</p>+<p>The <code>_reasoning</code> line is the part that a diff never has. Each question inside the change, with the+answer that it got, goes into the body in a fold.</p>+<figure><figcaption><b>leela/blocks/canvas/change.py</b> &middot; pr</figcaption><details><summary>pr (23 lines)</summary><div class="in"><pre><code class="lang-python">def pr(doc, bid, branch=None):+ &quot;A pull request cut from one change. It opens nothing.&quot;+ b = first(x for x in bundles(doc) if x.id == bid)+ if b is None: raise KeyError(bid)+ body = []+ if (g := b.goal) is not None:+ bits = [f&#x27;{k}: {v}&#x27; for k, v in g.attrs.items()+ if k in (&#x27;measure&#x27;, &#x27;baseline&#x27;, &#x27;target&#x27;, &#x27;by&#x27;)]+ body.append(f&#x27;**Goal.** {g.body.strip()}&#x27; + (f&#x27; \n{&quot; | &quot;.join(bits)}&#x27; if bits else &#x27;&#x27;))+ if b.contributes: body.append(f&#x27;**Contributes.** {b.contributes}&#x27;)+ if b.brick.body.strip(): body.append(b.brick.body.strip())+ if (prose := [x.body.strip() for x in b.of(&#x27;text&#x27;, &#x27;note&#x27;) if x.body.strip()]):+ body.append(&#x27;\n\n&#x27;.join(prose))+ if (tasks := b.of(&#x27;task&#x27;)):+ body.append(&#x27;### Tasks\n&#x27; + &#x27;\n&#x27;.join(+ f&quot;- [{&#x27;x&#x27; if t.attrs.get(&#x27;status&#x27;) == &#x27;done&#x27; else &#x27; &#x27;}] {t.body.strip()}&quot;+ + (f&quot; ({t.attrs[&#x27;owner&#x27;]})&quot; if t.attrs.get(&#x27;owner&#x27;) else &#x27;&#x27;) for t in tasks))+ if (why := _reasoning(b)): body.append(&#x27;### Why\n&#x27; + &#x27;\n\n&#x27;.join(why))+ if b.refs: body.append(&#x27;### Attached\n&#x27; + &#x27;\n&#x27;.join(f&#x27;- `{r}`&#x27; for r in b.refs))+ if b.paths: body.append(&#x27;### Files\n&#x27; + &#x27;\n&#x27;.join(f&#x27;- `{p}`&#x27; for p in b.paths))+ return {&#x27;id&#x27;: b.id, &#x27;title&#x27;: b.title, &#x27;branch&#x27;: branch or f&#x27;canvas/{b.id}&#x27;,+ &#x27;body&#x27;: &#x27;\n\n&#x27;.join(body) + &#x27;\n&#x27;, &#x27;paths&#x27;: b.paths, &#x27;refs&#x27;: b.refs,+ &#x27;goal&#x27;: b.goal.id if b.goal else &#x27;&#x27;}</code></pre></div></details></figure><h2 id="the-value">The value</h2><p><code>state</code> comes from the document. No person sets it. A status that a person must remember is a+status that lies.</p>+<p>One case needed care. No diff is no evidence about files. It must not read as evidence against+them. Every later section uses these words and no others.</p>+<table>+<thead>+<tr><th>word</th><th>means</th></tr>+</thead>+<tbody>+<tr><td><strong>brick</strong></td><td>one part of the document: a fence or a comment wrap. It cannot answer the three questions a reviewer brings+to a change.</p>+<ol>+<li>What was this change supposed to do?</li>+<li>Did it do that?</li>+<li>Did anything else move that nobody meant to move?</li>+</ol>+<p>The intent is in the document, not in the diff. So the document states the intent, the diff states+the fact, and <code>coverage</code> compares them. Its <code>unmet</code> list is a claim with no change behind it, and+its <code>unclaimed</code> list is a change with no claim behind it. Neither list can come out of a diff tool,+which holds one of the two sets.</p>+<p>This page shows that comparison at the top, as chips, before any code.</p>+<div class="card ask"><div class="q"><p>Why can a diff tool not report <code>unclaimed</code> on its own?</p>+</div><div class="a"><p><code>unclaimed</code> is the difference between two sets. A diff tool holds the files that moved. It does+not hold the files a change promised to touch, which sit in each bundle's <code>paths</code>. A finding+needs both sets.</p>+</div></div><h2 id="the-plan">The plan</h2><ul class="tasks"><li class="done"><span class="box">[x]</span><span>Read the document format from the canvas branch and adopt it.</span><span class="who">me</span></li><li class="done"><span class="box">[x]</span><span>Build the context basket: scope, pins, mutes, budget, and an inspectable result.</span><span class="who">me</span></li><li class="done"><span class="box">[x]</span><span>Make a boundary on the canvas a unit of change: tasks, prose, code and diff together.</span><span class="who">me</span></li><li class="done"><span class="box">[x]</span><span>Add the value view: every goal, and every change that serves it.</span><span class="who">me</span></li><li class="done"><span class="box">[x]</span><span>Write the literate page from the document, in ASD-STE100 English, under ramabana&#x27;s rules.</span><span class="who">me</span></li><li class="done"><span class="box">[x]</span><span>Resolve a component from an installed library, in Leela, with no second server.</span><span class="who">me</span></li><li class="done"><span class="box">[x]</span><span>Vendor the brick library as `extensions/bricks`. The package must extract with no code change.</span><span class="who">me</span></li><li class="done"><span class="box">[x]</span><span>Merge the canvas branch: one `doc.py`, one palette, one editor.</span><span class="who">me</span></li><li class="done"><span class="box">[x]</span><span>Move the page assembly out of the tool and into Leela.</span><span class="who">me</span></li><li class="done"><span class="box">[x]</span><span>Score every page with `slopometer`, and rewrite the prose that fails ASD-STE100.</span><span class="who">me</span></li><li class="done"><span class="box">[x]</span><span>Run `chkstyle` over the branch&#x27;s Python, and cut the imports nothing uses.</span><span class="who">me</span></li><li class="done"><span class="box">[x]</span><span>Get the suite green: 2003 pass, 15 skip, none fail.</span><span class="who">me</span></li></ul><h2 id="the-document">The document</h2><div class="card change"><div class="chips"><span class="chip done">done</span></div><div class="meta">Worth: the file every other part reads</div><p>A canvas is a markdown file. Prose stays prose. A brick is a fence or a comment wrap. Every+markdown reader therefore shows the file, and git shows a useful diff. The <code>ast</code> module reads the dataflow+between code bricks off the code itself.</p>+<div class="chips"><span class="chip">leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py</span><span class="chip">leela/blocks/canvas/example.py</span><span class="chip">leela/blocks/canvas/export.py</span><span class="chip">leela/blocks/canvas/layout.py</span><span class="chip">leela/blocks/canvas/ops.py</span></div><div class="chips"><span class="chip">doc:docs/canvas.md</span><span class="chip">file:leela/blocks/nb/nb.py</span></div></div><p>Two brick shapes, and the shape follows the content. Code goes in a fence, because a fence is how+markdown holds code. A goal or a task goes in a comment wrap, because a reader should see the+words and not the markup.</p>+<p>A fence holds what markdown already knows how to show, so a code cell stays a code block. A+comment wrap holds what a reader should read as prose, so a goal shows its words and not its+markup. <code>KINDS</code> is the whole vocabulary, and a document with a word outside it does not parse.</p>+<figure><figcaption><b>leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py</b> &middot; 12-15</figcaption><pre><code class="lang-python">FENCED = (&#x27;code&#x27;, &#x27;ask&#x27;, &#x27;brick&#x27;, &#x27;sim&#x27;, &#x27;data&#x27;, &#x27;diff&#x27;, &#x27;snippet&#x27;, &#x27;pdf&#x27;, &#x27;video&#x27;)+#: Bricks whose body is markdown a plain renderer should still show, written as a comment wrap.+WRAPPED = (&#x27;reply&#x27;, &#x27;note&#x27;, &#x27;quiz&#x27;, &#x27;goal&#x27;, &#x27;task&#x27;, &#x27;source&#x27;, &#x27;bundle&#x27;)+KINDS = (&#x27;text&#x27;,) + FENCED + WRAPPED</code></pre></figure><p><code>order</code> reads the graph rather than storing it. <code>defs_of</code> asks the code what it defines, and+<code>reads_of</code> asks what it reads. <code>order</code> joins two bricks when one defines what the other reads.</p>+<p><code>order</code> reads the dependency from the code. <code>_owners</code> says which brick defines each name, and+<code>b.reads</code> says which names a brick needs, so no person draws an edge. On a cycle the visit stops+and the document order stands, so a plan with a loop in it still opens.</p>+<figure><figcaption><b>leela/blocks/canvas/doc.py</b> &middot; order</figcaption><pre><code class="lang-python">def order(bricks):+ &quot;Runnable bricks in dependency order, falling back to document order on a cycle.&quot;+ live = L(bricks).filter(lambda b: b.runs)+ owner = _owners(live)+ need = {b.id: {owner[n] for n in b.reads if n in owner and owner[n] != b.id} for b in live}+ out, seen = [], set()+ def visit(b, path):+ if b.id in seen or b.id in path: return+ for dep in need[b.id]: visit(first(x for x in live if x.id == dep), path | {b.id})+ seen.add(b.id); out.append(b)+ for b in live: visit(b, set())+ return L(out)</code></pre></figure><h2 id="the-basket">The basket</h2><div class="card change"><div class="chips"><span class="chip done">done</span></div><div class="meta">Worth: what a question in the document may read</div><p>A question names its own scope, its pins and its budget. <code>resolve</code> returns the exact bricks, and each one+carries the reason it is there. <code>render</code> emits the cells that ramabana's <code>compact_notebook_context</code>+already knows how to shed.</p>+<div class="chips"><span class="chip">leela/blocks/canvas/context.py</span></div><div class="chips"><span class="chip">pkg:ramabana</span><span class="chip">file:leela/blocks/nb/nb.py</span></div></div><p>A notebook sends every brick above the question. A pin sends the two that matter, wherever they+sit. An audit belongs to the question at the top of the page and the one at the bottom, and to+nothing between.</p>+<p>A question states its own rule, and the rule is four fields. <code>scope</code> gathers the first set, <code>pins</code>+add what the scope missed, and <code>mutes</code> remove what it caught. An unknown scope becomes <code>page</code>+rather than an error, so a typed attribute cannot stop a document from opening.</p>+<figure><figcaption><b>leela/blocks/canvas/context.py</b> &middot; Spec</figcaption><pre><code class="lang-python">@dataclass+class Spec:+ &quot;A question&#x27;s context rule, written on the brick as attributes and `pin`/`mute` directives.&quot;+ scope: str = &#x27;page&#x27;+ pins: list = field(default_factory=list)+ mutes: list = field(default_factory=list)+ budget: int | None = None+ goal: bool = True+ def __post_init__(self):+ if self.scope not in SCOPES: self.scope = &#x27;page&#x27;</code></pre></figure><div class="card note"><p>The budget sheds the least useful brick first, not the oldest, and never a pin or the goal. Each+<code>Item</code> carries the <code>why</code> that put it there. A reviewer can therefore see which bricks the budget+dropped.</p>+</div><h2 id="the-change">The change</h2><div class="card change"><div class="chips"><span class="chip done">done</span></div><div class="meta">Worth: all of the review step</div><p>A bundle claims a region, names a goal and owns a list of files. <code>coverage</code> compares the claim+with the diff. Leela reads <code>state</code> off the document, and no one sets it by hand. <code>review</code>, <code>value</code> and <code>pr</code>+are three views over the same file.</p>+<div class="chips"><span class="chip">README.md</span><span class="chip">docs/README.md</span><span class="chip">docs/blocks.md</span><span class="chip">docs/canvas.md</span><span class="chip">docs/change.canvas.md</span><span class="chip">docs/dynamic-documents.md</span><span class="chip">docs/session.canvas.md</span><span class="chip">leela/blocks/canvas/change.py</span><span class="chip">leela/blocks/canvas/lit.css</span><span class="chip">leela/blocks/canvas/lit.py</span><span class="chip">media/*.md</span><span class="chip">media/canvas-*.html</span><span class="chip">tools/canvas_spike.py</span><span class="chip">tools/make_change_page.py</span></div><div class="chips"><span class="chip">doc:docs/change.canvas.md</span><span class="chip">pkg:mdhtml</span><span class="chip">pkg:gheasy</span></div></div><p>Leela derives the state of a change. Every snippet is read from the &#x27;+ &#x27;file it names.&#x27;)+ out = lit(doc, dest, changed=changed, root=root, subtitle=sub)+ return {&#x27;path&#x27;: str(out), &#x27;changed&#x27;: changed,+ &#x27;unclaimed&#x27;: coverage(doc, changed)[&#x27;unclaimed&#x27;],+ &#x27;diffs&#x27;: [b.id for b in doc.of(&#x27;diff&#x27;)]}</code></pre></figure><p>A <code>diff</code> brick with no body is a slot. Its manifest is read in process, never fetched.&quot;+ name: str+ module: object+ def _r(self): return _reg(self.module)+ def manifest(self):+ r = self._r()+ return r.manifest() if r else {&#x27;bricks&#x27;: [], &#x27;groups&#x27;: {}}+ def find(self, name):+ r = self._r()+ b = r.find(name) if r else None+ return b.dict() if hasattr(b, &#x27;dict&#x27;) else b+ def wire(self, name, base=&#x27;&#x27;):+ &quot;What fills this brick&#x27;s ports: the snippet it ships, and the call that reads it remotely.&quot;+ b = self.find(name)+ if b is None: return None+ d = getattr(self.module, &#x27;data&#x27;, None)+ remote = d.remote_wire(name, base) if base and hasattr(d, &#x27;remote_wire&#x27;) else &#x27;&#x27;+ return {&#x27;ok&#x27;: True, &#x27;src&#x27;: b.get(&#x27;src&#x27;) or f&#x27;{self.name}:{name}&#x27;, &#x27;wire&#x27;: b.get(&#x27;wire&#x27;, &#x27;&#x27;),+ &#x27;remote&#x27;: remote, &#x27;height&#x27;: b.get(&#x27;height&#x27;, 260),+ &#x27;binds&#x27;: {p[&#x27;name&#x27;]: p[&#x27;name&#x27;] for p in b.get(&#x27;ports&#x27;) or []},+ &#x27;emits&#x27;: [p[&#x27;name&#x27;] for p in b.get(&#x27;emits&#x27;) or []]}+ def fill(self, name):+ d = getattr(self.module, &#x27;data&#x27;, None)+ return d.fill(name) if hasattr(d, &#x27;fill&#x27;) else None+ def mount(self, app, page=None):+ &quot;Register this library&#x27;s own routes on Leela&#x27;s app. `serve` is the seam that takes any app.&quot;+ fn = first(f for f in (getattr(getattr(self.module, &#x27;serve&#x27;, None), &#x27;connect&#x27;, None),+ getattr(self.module, &#x27;connect&#x27;, None)) if callable(f))+ if fn is None: return f&#x27;{self.name}: no routes to mount&#x27;+ try:+ fn(app, page) if page is not None else fn(app)+ except TypeError: fn(app)+ return &#x27;&#x27;</code></pre></div></details></figure><p><code>needs</code> comes from the wiring's own imports.
